screening_results.reason: This study reports task-based fMRI and PET using the Tower of London planning task (an executive function: planning). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (model fit over whole brain; Talairach peaks, voxel/cluster-level inference, corrected/uncorrected thresholds, reported peaks in tables). At least one within-group task contrast is present (fMRI categorical contrast active > zero-move; parametric within-group regressions for fMRI and PET). Results are reported as coordinates/peaks. Participants are human (healthy). Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study is excluded because it does not report a within-group, voxelwise task activation contrast and reports only ROI/SVC analyses. Exclusion criteria met: E3 (only ROI/SVC analyses with no voxelwise task activation results). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (task falls within executive function domains — WCST measures cognitive flexibility/executive function), I9 (participant group is acceptable — healthy volunteers). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (not a task-based fMRI/PET activation study; PET here measured receptor binding, not task-evoked activation), I7 (no whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical map reported; model fit was over an ROI), I8 (no within-group task contrast reported — analyses are cross-subject regression of binding vs behavioral errors). Therefore the study does not meet necessary inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This fMRI study uses the Wisconsin Card Sorting Test, an established executive function paradigm (cognitive flexibility/working memory). Multiple group-level, voxelwise within-group contrasts are reported (e.g., A>HLB, B>HLB, C>HLB, A>B, A>C) using random-effects one-sample t-tests with whole-brain model fit and whole-brain inference; results are reported as peak coordinates/tables. Thus it provides whole-brain task-evoked activation maps for within-group contrasts relevant to executive function. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical).

This fMRI task-based study of working memory executive function meets inclusion criteria I5 (fMRI task), I6 (working memory executive domain), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported: H vs M, H vs L, etc.), I9 (group-level within-group contrasts reported for participants), and I10 (results reported as coordinate peaks in tables). However, NeuroStore indicates models were fit over a region of interest (Model fit over: region of interest) and not a voxelwise whole-brain/partial-brain analysis, so it fails I7. Because the report appears to contain only ROI-based analyses, Exclusion E3 (studies reporting only ROI or SVC analyses with no voxelwise results) applies. Therefore the study is excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study of executive function (working memory) using reading span and control tasks. It reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level contrasts (read > control; RST > read) for both high- and low-span subject groups, with peak coordinates/tables. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I5 (fMRI task-based executive function), I6 (working memory domain), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise results), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (participant group acceptable), and I10 (results reported in tables of coordinates). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group contrasts, empirical data).

This is an fMRI task-based study using the Tower of London planning task (an established executive function domain: planning). The record shows group-level, voxelwise analyses (model fit over cortical surface) with FDR-thresholded whole-brain results reported as peak coordinates/tables. It includes within-group task contrasts for healthy controls (active > scrambled baseline) and for TBI patients (active > scrambled), satisfying the requirement for at least one within-group task contrast. Results are presented in coordinate tables. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective.

This is an event-related fMRI study of the Wisconsin Card Sorting Task (an executive function task assessing cognitive flexibility), reporting group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise within-group contrasts with coordinate peak tables. NeuroStore extraction shows model fit and inference over the whole brain, multiple within-group task contrasts (e.g., Receiving negative feedback > control feedback), and reported peak coordinates/tables. Participants are human adults (n=11). Therefore all required inclusion criteria for task-based executive-function whole-brain voxelwise activation are met, and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study of random number generation, a task involving executive functions (controlled response generation and suppression), and thus fits the review objective. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level contrasts (RNG > counting) with thresholding and coordinate peaks (Talairach), satisfying voxelwise whole-brain evidence and allowing inclusion. Within-group contrasts are explicitly reported (paired t-tests for 1 Hz and 2 Hz conditions). Participants are healthy adults (n=8). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an fMRI task-based study of executive control using the Sustained Attention to Response Task (SART), which probes inhibition and sustained attention (executive function domains). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group analyses (model fit over whole brain) with tables of reported peak coordinates for multiple within-group contrasts (e.g., correct inhibitions, commission errors, tonic activations) explicitly labeled as simple effects within-group. Results are reported with cluster-level thresholding and peak tables. Participants are a healthy adult sample (n=18). All required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group contrasts, empirical data present).

This PET study used [(11)C] raclopride during the Montreal Card Sorting Task (MCST), a canonical executive function (cognitive flexibility/set-shifting) task. NeuroStore records group-level, voxelwise statistical parametric images of change in binding potential with model fit over the whole brain, and reports within-group task contrasts (e.g., retrieval with shift > control; active > control) with coordinate peaks in Talairach space. Although inference was restricted to a region-of-interest, the analysis was voxelwise and reported coordinates, satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Therefore all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (an executive function) using within-subject contrasts (high > low reward) reported at group level. The NeuroStore record shows multiple whole-brain, voxelwise group analyses with reported peak coordinates/tables (analyses 1–8), and at least one within-group task contrast. Participants are healthy adults. Thus the study meets fMRI task requirement, executive-domain task (working memory), whole-brain voxelwise reporting, and within-group contrasts. No exclusion criteria (only-ROI, only-connectivity, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) are triggered.

This PET task-based study directly assesses executive functions (updating, shifting, inhibition) using within-task contrasts and conjunction/interaction analyses. It reports group-level, random-effects voxelwise models fitted over the whole brain and provides peak coordinates/tables of activations. Several analyses are explicitly within-group contrasts (e.g., Analyses 2, 3, 4) and others report corrected voxelwise or cluster-corrected results. Tasks map clearly to established executive domains (working memory/updating, inhibition, cognitive flexibility/shifting). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, and not exclusively between-group contrasts. Therefore all required inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) are satisfied and the study should be included in the meta-analysis.

This paper reports original PET data (63 subjects, 370 scans) and a multigroup conjunction analysis contrasting rest and task states. It meets I5 (PET, task-based paradigms), and includes tasks within executive domains (spatial working memory, mental calculation/reasoning) satisfying I6. Analyses were voxelwise and modeled over the whole brain (Model fit over: whole brain), meeting I7. At least one within-group task contrast is reported (TASK > REST and REST > TASK), meeting I8. Participant groups are healthy adults (within-group contrasts present), meeting I9. Results are reported as coordinate tables/peaks (reported peaks: 24 and 4), satisfying I10. No exclusion criteria apply: analyses are whole-brain and voxelwise (not ROI only), not limited to connectivity or resting-state-only results, and include within-group contrasts (so E3–E5, E6 do not apply). Although the study pools diverse tasks (some non-executive), the presence of executive-function tasks and within-group, whole-brain task contrasts supports inclusion for a meta-analysis of executive function task activations pooled across groups.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study reporting multiple within-subject, within-group task contrasts of executive functions (inhibition: flanker, go/no-go, stop; working memory: spatial and verbal). Analyses were estimated voxelwise across the whole brain with whole-brain inference and results reported as peak coordinates/tables. At least one within-group task contrast is present for multiple tasks. Participant sample (n=11 healthy adults) is reported. Therefore all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met (fMRI task-based, established executive domains, whole-brain voxelwise results, within-group contrasts, participant groups acceptable, and results reported in tables). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) apply.

The NeuroStore record reports only a voxelwise between-group/genotype contrast (Val/Val vs Met/Met) or a group × condition interaction for the one-back task; no within-group task>baseline or main-effect-of-task voxelwise contrast is reported for any group. Therefore the study violates exclusion criterion E5 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions with no within-group activation map). The study does meet I5 (PET task-based study), I6 (working memory N-back), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise results reported), I9 (clinical participant group included), and I10 (coordinates/peaks reported). Inclusion criterion I8 (at least one within-group task contrast) is not met. Full text appears complete in the NeuroStore extraction, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

Excluded under E3: The NeuroStore record reports only an ROI analysis (right medial OFC) with small-volume correction (SVC) and no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-activation map is provided. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (inhibition domain: go/no-go), I8 (within-group task contrast reported), I9 (acceptable participant group). Inclusion criterion not met: I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise group-level results reported). fulltext_incomplete=false

The study reports task-based fMRI (simultaneous fMRI-EEG) of a mental arithmetic task explicitly framed as central executive/working memory, satisfying executive-function domain requirements. Whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed and reported (Talairach coordinates, tables of peaks). A within-group task contrast (Mental arithmetic > Resting) is reported with peak coordinates, meeting the requirement for a within-group task activation map. Participant group is described (n=8 adults). Results are reported as coordinate tables, fulfilling reporting criteria. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the paper meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI task study of working memory (n-back), an established executive function domain, satisfying I5 and I6. Multiple analyses report voxelwise, group-level maps with model fit and inference over the whole brain and reported peak coordinates (e.g. Analyses 0,1,2 etc.), satisfying I7 and I10. The record includes within-group task contrasts (simple effect 1-back, 2-back, 3-back within-group analyses), satisfying I8. Participant groups include patients and healthy controls, and within-group contrasts are reported for at least one group, satisfying I9. No exclusion criteria are met: results are whole-brain voxelwise (not ROI-only), not connectivity-only, and not non-empirical. The study therefore meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive-function task activations.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of executive function (set-shifting using a verbal Trail Making Test). It reports a within-group contrast (vTMTB > vTMTA) estimated voxelwise with the model fit and inference over the whole brain and corrected cluster-level thresholding, with reported peak coordinates (Talairach). Thus it meets inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (cognitive flexibility/set-shifting), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise group analysis), I8 (within-group task contrast), I9 (participant group acceptable), and I10 (results reported as coordinates/table). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical).

This is an empirical task-fMRI study of executive function in ASD (two executive tasks: random number/sequence generation and a stimulus-oriented vs stimulus-independent task). It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (model fit over whole brain; several contrasts including within-group contrasts such as Random>Baseline and SI>SO / SO>SI for ASD and Control groups). At least one analysis (SO>SI in the alphabet task) reports whole-brain corrected inference; multiple contrasts report coordinates/tables of peaks. Thus criteria I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function), I6 (tasks map onto established executive domains), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise results), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported), I9 (participant group acceptable), and I10 (results reported as tables/coordinates) are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears sufficiently represented by the NeuroStore record, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

This study reports task-based fMRI of executive function (N-back working memory, verbal fluency) in healthy volunteers. It includes whole-brain, voxelwise group analyses with inference over the whole brain and cluster-corrected thresholds. Crucially, within-group task contrasts (2-back > 0-back) are reported (Analyses 17828390_analysis_0 and _3), satisfying the requirement for a within-group task activation map. Results are reported as peak coordinates in tables. The task falls within the working-memory executive domain and the paper reports empirical human neuroimaging data. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) are met.

This study reports task-based fMRI of working memory (N-back), an executive function (I5,I6). Multiple within-group, voxelwise contrasts are reported (e.g., 3-back > 1-back and 1-back > 3-back) with model fit and inference performed over the whole brain and cluster-level correction, and peaks reported, satisfying whole-brain, voxelwise evidence and within-group contrast requirements (I7,I8,I10). Participant groups include healthy and clinical samples, and within-group contrasts are available for at least one group (I9). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and not exclusively between-group contrasts. Full text appears available via the NeuroStore record (fulltext_incomplete=false).

Excluded because the study reports only region-of-interest analyses (model fit over: region of interest; region-level thresholding) and does not provide any voxelwise whole-brain group-level statistical maps. This meets exclusion criterion E3. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI assessing executive function - go/no-go inhibition), I6 (task within executive function domain - inhibition), I8 (reports a within-group contrast: go > no-go), and I9 (participant group reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise group-level analysis reported). Therefore the study must be excluded for failing to provide whole-brain voxelwise results required by the review.

This PET study directly assesses executive function (working memory; N-back) using task-based contrasts in a sample of older adults. Multiple analyses report group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task activation contrasts (e.g., spatial/verbal memory search > control; 2-back > control) with voxel-level corrected inference and tables of reported peaks, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise maps. Several contrasts are explicitly within-group. Participant group is acceptable per criteria. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Therefore all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 and I10 are met and the study should be INCLUDED.

This fMRI study used a spatial working memory task (an executive function domain) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task activation contrasts. Multiple within-group simple-effect contrasts are reported for both controls and heavy cannabis users (analyses 0–3) with voxelwise peaks/tables, satisfying the requirement for within-group voxelwise task activation maps. Between-group contrasts are also present but do not prevent inclusion. Reporting includes tables of coordinates (reported peaks). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This fMRI study investigates attentional set-shifting (a cognitive flexibility/executive function domain) using a task-based paradigm. It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (model fit and inference over whole brain) with within-group task contrasts (e.g., alternate > rest, alternate > tie/win/lose) and provides peak coordinates in tables. Participants are healthy adults and the reported maps/coordinates satisfy reporting requirements. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and it is empirical). Therefore all relevant inclusion criteria are satisfied.

This is an event-related fMRI study using a Go/No-Go task (inhibition/executive control) with whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses. The NeuroStore record reports random-effects, one-sample t-tests and conjunction/contrast analyses fit over the whole brain with voxelwise inference and tables of reported peaks (Tables tbl1–tbl6). Multiple within-group contrasts are provided (e.g., Movement Go, Count Go, Movement Go > Count Go, Movement Go > Movement Nogo, Count Nogo > Count Go), satisfying the requirement for within-group task contrasts. Results are reported as coordinate tables and described in the text. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met.

This fMRI n-Back study assesses working memory in MS patients and controls and reports whole-brain voxelwise group-level results. However, the NeuroStore record includes only between-group/group x condition interaction contrasts (e.g., MS 3-Back > HC 0-Back) and no within-group task activation contrasts for any group. Therefore it fails the requirement for a within-group task contrast. (a) Exclusion IDs met: E5. (b) Inclusion IDs met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (working memory task), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise group-level analysis), I10 (whole-brain results reported in table/peaks). (c) Inclusion IDs NOT met: I8 (within-group task contrast). Full text is complete in this record. Conclusion: EXCLUDE because the paper reports only between-group contrasts and interactions with no within-group activation maps available.

This fMRI study used the Tower of London planning task (an executive-function task) and reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain activation analyses. It includes within-group task contrasts for both females and males (Analyses 3 and 4: task > rest, whole-brain, FWE-corrected, reported peak coordinates/tables), satisfying a within-group task contrast requirement. The study provides whole-brain voxelwise results (model fit over whole brain; reported peak tables), and results are reported with corrected statistics and coordinate tables. It is not ROI-only, not a connectivity/resting study, and not exclusively between-group contrasts. Therefore all relevant inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Excluded because the NeuroStore record reports only a between-group contrast (HC MGS > HR; group x condition interaction) and no within-group task activation contrasts for any group. This meets exclusion criterion E5. The study does satisfy several inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (task is working memory—memory-guided saccade), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise model fit), I10 (whole-brain results reported as coordinates/table), and I9 (participant groups are acceptable). However I8 is not met (no within-group task contrast reported). Full text was available in the record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical fMRI study of an inhibitory executive function (go/no-go) with healthy adults. It reports at least one group-level, voxelwise, whole-brain within-group task contrast (state-related task > fixation; model fit over whole brain; voxel-level threshold p<0.001) and reports peak coordinates (Talairach). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for task-based executive-function activations and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This study reports original task-based fMRI data addressing executive functions (switching and inhibition) and therefore fits the review objective. It includes multiple group-level, voxelwise whole-brain statistical maps (Analyses 0–3: e.g., switch>nonswitch, incompatible>compatible, High-Switch>Low-Switch) with voxelwise inference (FDR thresholding) and reported peak coordinates/tables. All qualifying contrasts are within-group task contrasts. Participants are a human sample (n=14 healthy adults). Results are clearly described and reported in tables of peaks. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The fMRI analyses are region-of-interest (ROI) based and report only ROI-level voxelwise results, not whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps; thus the study violates the review's whole-brain requirement. Additionally, the fMRI task was a perceptual lateralization judgment (face location), not a canonical executive-function task (e.g., working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility). Inclusion criteria met: I9 (participant group acceptable). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (fMRI assessing executive function task), I6 (task falls within established executive function domains), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise evidence), I8 (within-group task contrast/main effect of task against baseline not reported). Exclusion criteria met: E3 (only ROI/small-volume-corrected analyses reported). Document appears complete for screening.

This is an fMRI task-based study of working memory (n-back), which falls under executive function. The NeuroStore record reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (1-back>0-back, 2-back>0-back, 2-back>1-back) using a random-effects approach and voxelwise inference; results are reported as coordinate tables. Within-group task contrasts are present for healthy adult participants. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is an empirical fMRI study). Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and the study should be included in the meta-analysis.

The study reports only region-of-interest analyses: 'Model fit over: region of interest' and 'Inference restricted to: region of interest' (prefrontal cortex a priori), with no whole-brain voxelwise task activation map. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only analyses). It does satisfy inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (inhibition domain — go/no-go task), I8 (within-group contrasts reported: no-go>go and go>no-go), and I9 (within-group healthy participants). It does NOT meet I7 (requires at least one whole-brain voxelwise group-level analysis). Full text is complete for screening (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This fMRI study uses an N-back working memory task (I5,I6) with whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses reported (I7) and includes clinical participant groups (I9). Results are reported as peak coordinates (I10). However, the NeuroStore record lists only between-group contrasts (e.g., heavy vs controls, moderate vs controls, group x condition interactions) and does not report any within-group task contrasts (no main-effect-of-task maps for any group). Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E5 (reports only between-group contrasts with no within-group task activation contrasts). Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I7, I9, I10. Inclusion criterion not met: I8 (no within-group task contrast reported). Full text is available in the record, so fulltext_incomplete=false. Because failing I8 and meeting E5 prevents inclusion in the meta-analysis, the study must be excluded.

The study reports an empirical fMRI task-based investigation of spatial working memory (an executive function domain), meeting I5 and I6. Analyses are group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps (Model: Group Z-maps; Model fit over: whole brain) with voxelwise inference and reported peak coordinates in tables, satisfying I7 and I10. Multiple within-group task contrasts are reported (e.g., maintenance > encoding/recognition and simple effects), fulfilling I8. Participant group (n=6 healthy adults) is acceptable under I9. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only (E3), not connectivity- or resting-state-only (E4), and within-group contrasts are present so E5 does not apply; the paper is empirical (E6 not met). Thresholding and methods are reported (FDR p<0.001, cluster criteria for some contrasts). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is a task-based fMRI study of working memory (Delayed Match-to-Sample), which fits executive function domains (I5, I6). Analyses were estimated voxelwise across the whole brain (Model fit over: whole brain) and a within-group task contrast is reported (Delay 4s > Delay 1s; Analysis 16912129_analysis_0) with peak coordinates in tables—satisfying whole-brain evidence and within-group contrast requirements (I7, I8, I10). Participant group (postmenopausal women) is acceptable (I9). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only or connectivity/resting-state-only, and the paper reports within-group task activations (so E3–E5 do not apply); the study is empirical (not E6).

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it is an event-related fMRI study of working memory (I5,I6), reports voxelwise whole-brain model fitting and results (Model fit over: whole brain; reported peaks) (I7), and includes multiple within-group task contrasts (Cue/Delay/Probe > intertrial interval and pergolide > placebo) qualifying as within-group task activation contrasts (I8). Participants are healthy adults (I9). Results are reported as peak coordinates/tables (I10). No exclusion criteria apply: findings are not ROI-only (E3), not connectivity/resting-state only (E4), and not limited to between-group contrasts (E5). Therefore include.

The study reports a task-based fMRI (Go/No-Go) assessing inhibitory control (I5,I6). It includes whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task activation analyses (analyses 6–11; corrected voxelwise maps), satisfying whole-brain evidence (I7). Within-group task contrasts are reported for multiple groups (analyses 0–2), meeting the within-group contrast requirement (I8). Any participant group is acceptable and clinical samples are included (I9). Results are reported as coordinate peaks/tables, satisfying acceptable reporting formats (I10). No exclusion criteria apply: the paper does not report only ROI/SVC results (whole-brain maps are present), is not connectivity/resting-only, and includes within-group contrasts, so it should be included.

This fMRI study uses a Stop-Signal Task (inhibition), an established executive-function paradigm, and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with FDR-corrected inference and MNI coordinates (Table 1). At least one reported contrast is a within-group task contrast (interaction contrast within participants). Participants are healthy adults (n=40). Results are reported as coordinates and peaks. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and not only between-group contrasts. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria are violated.

The study uses task-based fMRI of working memory (meets I5 and I6). NeuroStore indicates whole-brain model fitting and at least one analysis reports whole-brain inference/peaks in tables (meets I7 and I10). Any participant group is acceptable (meets I9). However, all reported contrasts are between-group comparisons or group x condition interactions; no within-group task activation contrast for any group is reported (violates I8). Therefore this study reports ONLY between-group contrasts and meets exclusion criterion E5.

The NeuroStore record reports only region-of-interest model fitting and inference (model fit over: region of interest; inference restricted to: region of interest), with no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation map reported. Therefore exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI/small-volume analyses) is met. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI study of executive function/planning), I6 (task falls within executive domain: planning), I8 (within-group task contrast reported: task > baseline), I9 (participant group reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise group-level task-evoked statistical map reported). Conclusion: EXCLUDED due to E3 (no qualifying whole-brain voxelwise results).

The study reports task-based fMRI of response inhibition (Go/No-go), which is an executive function (inhibition). Group-level, random-effects, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported for within-group task contrasts (Go and No-go simple effects) with reported peak coordinates and cluster inference; both simple and counting tasks include within-group contrasts against baseline/conditions. This satisfies fMRI task activation (I5), executive domain (I6), whole-brain voxelwise results (I7), within-group task contrasts (I8), any participant group allowed (healthy adults; I9), and reporting of whole-brain results in tables/coordinates (I10). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and empirical data present).

This fMRI study examines sentence disambiguation with explicit manipulations of working memory load and planning-related processing, fitting executive function domains (working memory and planning). Analyses are voxelwise, group-level, whole-brain random-effects models (Talairach space) with reported peak coordinates/tables, and multiple within-group task contrasts are listed (e.g., contrasts of disambiguating/terminal vs initial phrases, WM vs no-WM, less-consistent vs more-consistent). Thus it meets I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (executive domains: working memory and planning), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise results), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (participant groups acceptable), and I10 (results reported in tables). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-groups-only, and is empirical).

This fMRI study used the Tower of London planning task (an executive function domain: planning) and reports group-level, voxelwise within-group task contrasts (TOL easy/hard > fixation) for both an autism group and healthy controls. The model was fit over the whole brain with voxel-level thresholding and reported peak coordinates (Table 2, MNI), satisfying whole-brain evidence and acceptable reporting formats. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function), I6 (task = planning), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise group-level analyses), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported), I9 (participant groups acceptable), and I10 (results reported as coordinate tables). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and empirical). Therefore the study should be included in the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This PET study uses a task-based Tower of London planning paradigm (an executive function: planning) with healthy adult participants. It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (inference over whole brain for several contrasts, reported peaks in tables) and multiple within-group task contrasts (e.g., EXPT1 > one-move control; EXPT1 > EXPT10). Coordinate space and peaks are provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5 (PET task-based executive function), I6 (planning), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise results), I8 (within-group contrasts), I9 (participant group acceptable), and I10 (coordinates/tables reported). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text is available in the provided record, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

This PET study uses a task-based Tower of London planning paradigm (executive function domain) with H2(15)O-PET. It reports group-level, voxelwise (voxel-by-voxel ANCOVA) whole-brain analyses and within-group task contrasts (task > rest, rest > task, and parametric modulation by complexity), with coordinates/peak tables. Results are reported at voxel-level thresholds and in tables. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The NeuroStore record documents an empirical task-based fMRI study probing executive control (working memory and episodic source memory) using mixed block/event-related design. Whole-brain, voxelwise group-level contrasts are reported (model fit over whole brain; voxel-level inference reported with p<0.001, cluster extent threshold). Within-group task contrasts (high-load > low-load; two-back vs one-back; source vs item memory) are explicitly listed. Participants are healthy adults (n=16). These features satisfy the meta-analysis requirements for executive-function task activations and do not trigger any exclusion criteria. Therefore the study should be included.

This paper reports task-based fMRI of working memory (executive function) with whole-brain, voxelwise group-level contrasts and within-group task>control contrasts. Specifics: working memory tasks (spatial and nonspatial) meet the executive-domain requirement; model was fit over the whole brain and group mean voxelwise activations are reported (tables of peak coordinates) for group-level within-group contrasts (Analyses 2 and 3, n=6); results are reported as coordinates/peaks. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and within-group contrasts are present). Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10).

This PET study reports task-based activations for an executive function (working memory Operation Span) and meets all required criteria: it uses PET (I5), the task falls within working memory (I6), and several group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses are reported (e.g., Math>Control, Memory>Control, Operation Span>Math/Memory) satisfying whole-brain evidence (I7) and within-group task contrasts (I8). Participant groups include young and senior cohorts (I9), and results are reported as coordinate peaks/tables (I10). Although ROI analyses are also presented, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts are available, so no exclusion criteria apply. The article text is available in the provided record (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This PET study directly assesses executive function using the Wisconsin Card Sorting Task (a cognitive-flexibility/set-shifting executive task) and reports voxelwise, whole-brain group-level activation contrasts. Multiple within-group task contrasts (WCS > sensorimotor control) are reported for different hormonal conditions, with coordinates in Talairach space. The report includes whole-brain voxelwise thresholding and peak tables, satisfying requirements for whole-brain, within-group task activations. Participant characteristics (including some with menstrually related mood disorder) do not disqualify the study because within-group contrasts are provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical).

This is an empirical fMRI study using an N-back working memory task (executive function). The NeuroStore record shows group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses and within-group task contrasts (2-back simple effect) for both controls and cocaine users with inference performed over the whole brain and coordinates reported in tables. Thus it meets fMRI task-based criterion, executive-function task domain, whole-brain voxelwise evidence, and includes within-group contrasts. No exclusion criteria are met (results are not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, and within-group contrasts are reported).

This study reports task-based fMRI in macaque monkeys performing a cognitive set-shifting (executive function/cognitive flexibility) task, with whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses and a within-group contrast (set-shifting simple effect). Results are reported as peaks/coordinates and inference was corrected across the whole brain. Although the sample is small (n=2), inclusion criteria do not impose a minimum N and allow any participant group. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and it is empirical).

This fMRI study reports task-based working memory experiments (executive function domain) with group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses and within-group contrasts. NeuroStore extraction shows whole-brain model fit, one-sample and paired t-tests comparing task > rest and l/r > d/n, reported peak coordinates (tables), and standard voxelwise inference (p<0.005). Participants are healthy adult groups. Thus it satisfies I5 (task-based fMRI assessing executive function), I6 (working memory task), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise results), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (participant groups acceptable), and I10 (results reported as coordinates). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This study reports task-based fMRI data using a Psychological Refractory Period (PRP) task which probes dual-task processing/attentional control and is framed in terms of executive functions. It includes within-group contrasts (e.g., Short SOA > Long SOA) analyzed at the group level using whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects models with reported peak coordinates (Tables/peaks reported). Thus it satisfies requirements for an fMRI task in the executive domain, whole-brain voxelwise analysis, and within-group contrasts. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Full text appears accessible via the NeuroStore record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical PET study using a task-based working memory paradigm (self-ordered object working memory) which falls squarely within executive function. The NeuroStore record reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain contrasts (self-ordered object working memory > control) with voxel-level thresholding and Talairach coordinates and tables of peaks, satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. At least one analysis is a within-group task contrast. Participant sample (healthy adults, n=8) is reported. Thus the study meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 and I10. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical).

Excluded because the report contains only region-of-interest analyses (model fit over: region of interest; inference restricted to: region of interest; regions: entire striatum) and does not provide any group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps. This violates exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (PET study assessing an executive-function task), I6 (task = Wisconsin Card Sorting Task, cognitive flexibility), I9 (a within-group participant sample is reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise results; analyses restricted to ROI), I8 (no standard within-group task contrast vs baseline reported — the reported contrast compares stimulation conditions rather than task>baseline). Full text judged complete for screening.

Excluded because the reported analyses used small-volume correction and inference was explicitly restricted to regions of interest, indicating only ROI/SVC results were reported (meets exclusion criterion E3). The study does meet several inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based PET study of executive function), I6 (working memory and vigilance tasks within established executive domains), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported), and I9 (acceptable participant group: healthy adults). However it fails I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise group-level task activation reported for inference; inference was ROI-restricted), so it does not satisfy all required inclusion criteria. Peaks are reported in tables, but thresholding via SVC indicates results are limited to predefined ROIs. fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an fMRI task study of working memory (delayed match-to-sample for identity and emotion), which falls within executive function domains (working memory). The NeuroStore record reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses with inference over the whole brain (Analyses 18385330_analysis_2 and _3: whole-brain model fit and whole-brain inference, FDR-corrected voxel-level results), and these are within-group task contrasts (DMS delay vs CON delay; DMS stimuli vs CON stimuli). Participant groups are healthy adults (within-group contrasts reported). Results are reported as peaks/tables. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply (e.g., the study is not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical).

This PET study investigates working memory (an executive function) using task-based contrasts and reports multiple within-group, voxelwise whole-brain activation analyses (e.g., SPA > NSPA, NSPA > SPA) with peak coordinates and table references. Model fitting and inference were performed over the whole brain for several contrasts, satisfying the requirement for voxelwise task-evoked maps. Participants are healthy humans and results are reported in tables of peaks. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, and within-group contrasts are present). Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met.

This is an event-related fMRI study using the Stop-Signal Task (an inhibition executive function) with healthy participants (n=40). Group-level, voxelwise whole-brain GLM analyses are reported (model fit and inference over whole brain; voxel-wise FWE-corrected thresholds), and the paper reports within-group task contrasts (SE>SS and pSS>pSE) with peak coordinates in tables. Results are clearly whole-brain voxelwise activation maps reported as tables. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (E3–E6).

This study uses task-based fMRI of working memory (executive function) and reports within-group contrasts, but the NeuroStore record indicates the reported group-level statistical model was fit over a region of interest (bilateral DLPFC). No analysis in the record is described as a whole-brain, voxelwise group-level activation map. Therefore it fails the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise evidence. Exclusion IDs met: E3. Inclusion IDs met: I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function), I6 (working memory task), I8 (within-group task contrast reported), I9 (participant group qualifies). Inclusion IDs not met: I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise group-level analysis reported). Full text is available as the NeuroStore-derived record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study (ASL perfusion) that reports within-group voxelwise group-level contrasts for executive-function tasks: a 2-back working memory task and a sustained attention (oddball) task. Models were fit and inference performed over the whole brain with cluster-corrected thresholds and peak coordinates reported in tables. Participants are healthy adults. All required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This PET study assesses executive function tasks (working memory and planning) in healthy volunteers and reports group-level, voxelwise task activation maps. Multiple within-group contrasts are present (Spatial two-back two-back>control; Planning (TOL) planning>control; Spatial Working Memory rehearsal>control) with model fit and inference over the whole brain and reported peak coordinates/tables. The modality (PET rCBF) and tasks (N-back, Tower of London) meet executive-function domains. Whole-brain voxelwise results are reported (see Analyses 2,3,4), satisfying requirements for voxelwise group maps. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group/interactions, and is empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using an event-related Go/No-Go paradigm (inhibition). The NeuroStore record shows whole-brain model fitting and voxelwise analysis with reported peak coordinates (Talairach), and includes group-level within-group contrasts (go vs no-go and go alone). Thus it meets I5 (fMRI task-based executive function), I6 (inhibition domain), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise results reported as peaks), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (participant group acceptable), and I10 (results reported as coordinates). No exclusion criteria apply: it is not ROI-only (E3), not connectivity-only (E4), not only between-group contrasts (E5), and is empirical (not E6). Small sample size (n=6) does not violate inclusion rules. Therefore INCLUDE.

This is a task-based fMRI study using an emotional Stroop (inhibition/cognitive control) paradigm meeting executive-function domain criteria. It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (Neutral > Fixation, inference over whole brain, voxelwise peaks reported) satisfying whole-brain evidence. Within-group contrasts are reported (Neg > Neutral; Neutral > Fixation). Participants are healthy adults (qualifies). Whole-brain results are reported as coordinates/peaks. Although two contrasts were restricted to an ROI, at least one qualifying whole-brain, voxelwise within-group contrast is present, so the study is eligible for inclusion.

This is a task-based fMRI study using the Wisconsin Card Sorting Task (cognitive flexibility). It reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (event-related GLM; analyses 0 and 1 report whole-brain voxelwise results corrected at p<0.05) and explicitly labels within-group contrasts (RNF>RCF within conditions). Although connectivity (PPI) analyses are present, the paper also provides task activation maps, satisfying the review’s requirements. No exclusion criteria are met.

This fMRI study uses an n-back working memory task (an established executive function domain) and reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain contrasts. It includes a within-group task contrast (2-back > 0-back) with corrected voxelwise thresholding and reported peak coordinates (Table). The task and measures fit task-based fMRI assessing executive function. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and not only between-group contrasts. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria are violated.

The study reports task-based fMRI (n-back working memory and Iowa Gambling Task) with group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise within-group contrasts and parametric modulations. N-back clearly maps to the executive function domain (working memory). Analyses were whole-brain fixed-effects group analyses with reported peak coordinates in tables, satisfying voxelwise reporting. Within-group contrasts are reported for both controls and bipolar patients (1/2/3-back > 0-back; gambling > card selection), meeting the requirement for at least one within-group task contrast. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Therefore the paper meets all inclusion criteria I5–I10 and should be included in the meta-analysis.

The study is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI with group-level, voxelwise within-group contrasts (SHIFT>NO-SHIFT and NO-SHIFT>SHIFT) reported as coordinates in a table. However, the task is a finger-tapping/interval-timing paradigm focused on motor timing and transfer to the untrained hand; it is not described as assessing an executive function domain. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (whole-brain voxelwise group analysis), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (participant group qualifies), I10 (results reported as coordinates/tables). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I5 (study assessing executive function/cognitive control), I6 (task falls within established executive function domains). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Because key inclusion requirements I5 and I6 are not satisfied, the study is excluded from the executive-function meta-analysis.

This fMRI study uses a go/no-go task (inhibition), an established executive function domain, and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task contrasts. It includes within-group contrasts (no-go > go) for both sham and tryptophan-depletion conditions and reports whole-brain inference with tables of peak coordinates. All inclusion criteria for task-based fMRI of executive function (I5, I6), whole-brain voxelwise results (I7), within-group contrasts (I8), participant groups accepted (I9), and coordinate/table reporting (I10) are met. No exclusion criteria apply (results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and within-group contrasts are present). Full text appears complete in the provided record.

This is an fMRI task study of response inhibition (Go/No-Go) meeting the review objective. It reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (model fit and inference over whole brain) and provides within-group task contrasts (NoGo - Go). Results are reported as peak coordinates/tables. Therefore it satisfies I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (inhibition domain), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise evidence), I8 (within-group task contrast), I9 (participant group acceptable), and I10 (coordinates/tables reporting). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only (E3), not connectivity/resting-state only (E4), not only between-group contrasts (E5), and this is empirical human neuroimaging data (not E6).

This is an fMRI task-based study of response inhibition (Stop-Signal Task), an executive function (inhibition) domain. The NeuroStore record reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain contrasts (e.g., StopInhibit > StopRespond and StopRespond > GoTrim) analyzed with random-effects one-sample t-tests, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain, within-group task activation maps. Although some analyses used small-volume correction (SVC), the presence of whole-brain voxelwise results prevents exclusion under ROI-only criteria. Participants are healthy adults (within-group contrasts reported). Therefore all relevant inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study reports task-based fMRI of an established executive function domain (spatial working memory, n-back) in healthy adults. It includes group-level, voxelwise within-group task contrasts (2-back > 0-back) analyzed with whole-brain random-effects one-sample t-tests and reports coordinates/peaks, satisfying whole-brain evidence. Although one analysis (genotype interaction) used an ROI small-volume correction, the presence of multiple whole-brain within-group activation contrasts means the study is not excluded. All required inclusion criteria for the review are met, and no exclusion criteria apply.

This PET study reports a task-based investigation of verbal working memory updating (an executive function). It includes a within-group voxelwise contrast (variable target > fixed target) analyzed with SPM over the whole brain and inference across the whole brain (voxel-level Bonferroni-like correction), with reported Talairach peak coordinates and peaks table. Participants (n=10) are a human group. Thus the study satisfies inclusion criteria I5 (PET task-based EF), I6 (working memory), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise results), I8 (within-group contrast), I9 (participant group acceptable), and I10 (coordinates/tables reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears sufficiently represented in the supplied NeuroStore record.

This study reports task-based fMRI (n-back working memory) assessing an executive function domain (working memory). Group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses are reported (multiple contrasts with FDR-corrected voxelwise thresholds and tables of peak coordinates). Several within-group task contrasts are provided (Sign, Speech, Binding, and contrasts such as Binding>Sign/Speech and Sign>Speech), satisfying the requirement for within-group task activation maps. Participants are human (healthy hearing native signers) and any participant group is acceptable. Results are reported as voxelwise task-evoked maps and peaks, meeting the allowance for coordinate-table reporting. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

The study used fMRI and a working-memory (Sternberg) task (so meets I5 and I6) and reports a within-group contrast (high load > low load) but the reported results are seed-based functional connectivity maps (connectivity strength) rather than voxelwise task-evoked activation maps. The meta-analysis requires at least one whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation map (I7). Because the paper reports only connectivity analyses and no task activation maps, it meets exclusion criterion E4 and cannot be included.

This is a task-based fMRI study that includes an inhibition task (Go/No-Go) and reward/loss tasks (executive/motivational domains). The NeuroStore record reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses and explicitly lists within-group task contrasts (No-Go > Go; Reward > No-Reward; Loss > No-Loss) with reported peak coordinates. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (inhibition within executive functions), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise results), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (any participant group allowed), and I10 (results reported as coordinates). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only results, connectivity-only, or only between-group contrasts) are met. Full text is available in the provided NeuroStore record.

This is an event-related task-based fMRI study of planning (Tower of London), which is an established executive function domain. The report includes group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (ToL > CC1 and ToL > CC2) with FWE-corrected voxelwise inference and tables of peak coordinates. A within-group task contrast is clearly reported; participants are healthy adults (n=17). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) and violates no exclusion criteria (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, or between-group-only results).

The study uses task-based fMRI with an n-back working memory task (I5, I6) and reports within-group task contrasts for both controls and depressed patients (I8). Participant groups are acceptable (I9). However, all reported analyses were modelled and inferred within a region-of-interest (model fit over: region of interest; inference restricted to: region of interest), i.e. ROI-only results. This means the paper does not provide voxelwise whole-brain task activation maps, violating inclusion criterion I7 and meeting exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI/SVC analyses reported). Therefore the study must be excluded.

This PET study reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked activation contrasts for executive domains. It includes N-Back (visuospatial working memory) and a mental arithmetic task, with within-group contrasts (Calculation > Digit Reading; N-Back > 0-Back) reported as whole-brain voxelwise results with thresholding and tables of peaks. These meet inclusion requirements for an fMRI/PET task-based executive function study, established executive-domain tasks (working memory), whole-brain voxelwise analyses, and within-group task contrasts. Participant group (healthy adults) is acceptable, and results are reported in coordinate tables. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, not non-empirical).

The study reports task-based fMRI of an executive function task (modified Stroop—an inhibition/cognitive control task) with group-level, voxelwise whole-brain activation maps and within-group contrasts (activation > rest) for both controls and TBI patients. Peak coordinates are reported (Table 2), and analyses were performed at the whole-brain level. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI/PET of executive function), I6 (task within executive domains: inhibition), I7 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain results), I8 (within-group task contrasts against baseline), I9 (participant groups acceptable), and I10 (results reported as coordinate peaks). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, not non-empirical).

This is a task-based fMRI study of working memory (an executive function), reporting whole-brain, group-level voxelwise within-group contrasts. The NeuroStore record shows random-effects, voxelwise analyses (corrected P<0.05 voxel-level and cluster-level thresholds) for within-group task contrasts (Memory and Arithmetic vs baseline/other conditions) for both high- and low-span groups, with peaks reported in tables. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria (fMRI task assessing executive function; task within working memory domain; whole-brain voxelwise group results; at least one within-group task contrast; participant groups acceptable; results reported in tables). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and empirical human neuroimaging data).

This is a task-based PET study of the Tower of London planning task (an established executive function domain). The NeuroStore record reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (model fit over whole brain) with within-group task contrasts (multiple contrasts comparing plan and control conditions, and parametric modulation by thinking time). Results are reported as peak coordinates/tables. Thus criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 and I10 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply: analyses are not ROI-only (E3), not connectivity- or resting-only (E4), and not only between-group contrasts (E5). Full text is available via the record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

Although this fMRI study uses a stop-signal task (inhibition domain) and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses, all reported whole-brain contrasts are between-group interactions (short SSRT > long SSRT). The only within-group analysis is an ROI-based cross-subject correlation with SSRT. Inclusion criterion I8 requires at least one within-group task contrast (e.g., task > baseline or within-group condition contrast). Because no within-group task activation contrast is reported, the study meets exclusion criterion E5 (only between-group contrasts or interactions with no within-group task activation contrast). Included criteria met: I5, I6, I7, I9, I10. Included criteria not met: I8. Full text appears complete for screening.

The study reports an original task-based fMRI investigation of response inhibition (stop-signal task) in healthy participants (n=30). It includes whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (e.g. analyses 18485743_analysis_0, _1, and _4 report second-level random-effects GLM voxelwise contrasts with whole-brain model fit and voxel-level thresholding), satisfying whole-brain evidence. It also reports within-group task contrasts (stop > go; stop error > stop success) at the group level (analyses 18485743_analysis_2 and _3), meeting the within-group contrast requirement. The task falls within the executive function domain (inhibition). Results are reported as peak coordinates and tables. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, and not non-empirical), so inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10 are all satisfied.

The study uses task-based fMRI of an executive function task (WCST) and reports within-group contrasts (1st-round shifts > 2nd-round shifts) with coordinate peaks. However, inference is explicitly restricted to a region-of-interest with small-volume correction (SVC) despite model fitting over the whole brain; the reported significant results are SVC/ROI-based. Therefore it does not provide unconfined whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results required by I7 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI/SVC-only reporting). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI task), I6 (cognitive flexibility), I8 (within-group contrasts), I9 (participant groups acceptable), I10 (coordinates reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I7 (whole-brain voxelwise evidence).

The NeuroStore record shows this is an fMRI study of working memory (executive function domain) with within-group contrasts (e.g., negative>neutral, neutral>negative) in healthy adults, satisfying I5, I6, I8, and I9. However, all reported analyses that list model coverage specify region-of-interest model fits and region-level thresholding (Analyses 1–3: "Model fit over: region of interest" with region-level thresholding). No analysis is clearly reported as a group-level, voxelwise (whole-brain) task activation map; one analysis (16957605_analysis_0) lacks extracted features but provides no indication of whole-brain voxelwise inference. Because results are reported only for ROIs / region-level tests, this meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only with no voxelwise results) and fails inclusion criterion I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise task map). Therefore the study is excluded.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the review: it is an fMRI task-based study (I5) using a two-back verbal working memory task (I6, executive domain). Analyses were fitted over the whole brain with voxelwise inference and reported peak coordinates (I7, I10). The paper reports within-group task contrasts for both controls and patients (I8), and participant group (clinical) is acceptable (I9). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and within-group contrasts are reported. The NeuroStore record provides group-level voxelwise results (tables of peaks) enabling inclusion in the pooled meta-analysis of executive function activations.

This is a task-based fMRI study using an n-back working memory task (executive function). The NeuroStore record reports a group-level, voxelwise (model fit over: whole brain) within-group omnibus contrast with voxel-level thresholding and reported peak coordinates, satisfying whole-brain, group-level voxelwise reporting. Participants are healthy adults; any participant group is acceptable. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5 (fMRI task), I6 (working memory), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise group results), I8 (within-group contrast), I9 (participant group acceptable), and I10 (coordinates reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears available in the record.

This fMRI study used a task-based n-back working memory paradigm (executive function) and reports within-group contrasts at the group level. Specifically, Analysis 18403120_analysis_1 is a whole-brain, voxelwise paired t-test (random effects, n=31) contrasting After > Before during n-back tasks with reported peak coordinates (p<0.001 voxel-level). Analysis 18403120_analysis_0 is a within-group ROI conjunction analysis in MFG but the presence of the whole-brain group-level voxelwise map satisfies whole-brain requirement. All inclusion criteria are met (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-groups-only, empirical human fMRI data). Full text appears accessible via the provided NeuroStore extract, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The NeuroStore record and abstract identify this article as a review ('review of published studies' in Design and the abstract describes critical evaluation of fMRI findings), so it does not present original human neuroimaging data. Therefore exclusion criterion E6 (non-empirical paper without original imaging data) applies. No inclusion criteria are met: the paper itself is not an fMRI/PET task-based empirical study (I5 not met), does not provide its own within-group, voxelwise task activation maps (I7, I8 not met), and thus does not satisfy I6, I9 or I10 either. Although an analysis entry is present in the record, the study-level Design explicitly indicates this is a review rather than an original task-based fMRI/PET experiment, so it cannot be included.

Exclusion applied: E3. The NeuroStore record shows this is an fMRI study of spatial working memory (I5) within the executive domain (working memory; I6). It reports within-group contrasts (e.g., No-HF > No-LF; No-LF/No-HF > match; I8) and a qualifying participant group (healthy adults; I9). However, the record indicates that the reported key analyses were conducted as region-of-interest (model fit over: region of interest; region-level thresholding) and lists regions defined a priori. No analysis is explicitly reported as a group-level, voxelwise whole-brain activation map (I7 not met). Several analyses have “no features extracted” despite reporting peaks in a table, but the record does not confirm voxelwise/whole-brain model fitting. Because the study appears to report only ROI analyses without voxelwise whole-brain results, it meets exclusion criterion E3 and must be excluded.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It is an fMRI task-based study using the Stroop Color-Word Task, an established inhibition/executive function paradigm (I5, I6). The reported analysis was fit over the whole brain and used voxelwise inference (model fit over: whole brain; voxel-level thresholding; reported peaks), providing group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (I7). The contrast is a within-group task contrast (interaction within-subject: tryptophan depletion vs placebo for incongruent Stroop), satisfying the within-group requirement (I8). Participants are healthy adults (eligible under I9). Results are reported as peak coordinates (Table-2), which is acceptable (I10). No exclusion criteria apply: analyses are not ROI-only (E3), not connectivity/resting-state only (E4), and not exclusively between-group contrasts or interactions without within-group task contrasts (E5). The document appears complete for screening. Therefore INCLUDE.

This is an fMRI Go/No-Go study reporting a within-group No-Go>Go contrast and a negative correlation with BIS-11 motor impulsiveness. However, the reported correlation analysis was performed within a region-of-interest (model fit over and inference restricted to ROI) rather than as a whole-brain voxelwise task activation map. Therefore the study lacks qualifying whole-brain voxelwise results required by I7 and meets exclusion E3 (ROI-only analyses). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (inhibition task), I8 (within-group contrast No-Go>Go), I9 (healthy participant group). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (whole-brain voxelwise evidence).

This PET study reports task-based executive-function (working memory) contrasts (spatial span, spatial manipulation/2-back) and therefore addresses the review objective. It includes group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (model fit and inference over whole brain; peak-level thresholding with RFT) and reports coordinates/peaks (Table 1). Several contrasts are explicitly labeled as within-group task contrasts (e.g., spatial span > visuomotor control; spatial manipulation > visuomotor control; spatial manipulation > spatial span). Participants are human (n=5 adults) and any participant group is acceptable per criteria. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Therefore all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study using an n-back working-memory task (executive function). The NeuroStore record lists within-group task contrasts (1-back>0-back, 2-back>0-back, 2-back>1-back) with reported whole-brain peaks and an explicit whole-brain model fit for the between-group interaction; voxelwise peak coordinates are reported in tables. Thus the paper provides voxelwise, group-level task-evoked activation maps for an executive function task. No exclusion criteria are met: analyses are not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, and within-group contrasts are reported (so it is not only between-group contrasts). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

Excluded because the NeuroStore extraction reports only between-group contrasts (group x condition interactions) for both tasks (ALS < controls and ALS > controls) and does not report any within-group (task > rest or task > control) voxelwise activation contrast for either group. Therefore exclusion criterion E5 applies. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (letter fluency is an executive initiation task), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I9 (participant groups acceptable), and I10 (coordinates/peak tables reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I8 (no within-group task contrast reported). Because E5 is met (only between-group contrasts), the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an event-related fMRI study using a stop-signal task (inhibition), meeting the executive-function domain. Group-level, voxelwise analyses were performed (voxelwise single-sample t tests/regressions) with whole-brain model fit and reported peak coordinates/tables. Multiple within-group task contrasts are reported (e.g., SST>NST, UST>SST), satisfying a within-group task contrast requirement. Participants are healthy adults. Results are reported as whole-brain coordinates/tables. No exclusion criteria are met (analyses are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and the paper is empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It is an fMRI study of executive function (inhibitory control: Stop-Signal and Go/No-Go tasks), satisfying I5 and I6. Multiple group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task activation maps are reported (Model fit over: whole brain; inference over: whole brain) with voxel-level permutation thresholds for within-group contrasts in both controls and patients (Analyses 0–3), satisfying I7 and I8. Any participant group is acceptable (I9) and results are reported in standard formats (I10). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is a PET task-based study of planning (Tower of London), which is an executive function. Whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed (model fit over whole brain; voxel-level thresholding) and the paper reports group-level within-group task contrasts (parametric modulation within-group analyses for normals and for Parkinson’s patients). Results are reported as peak coordinates in tables. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I5–I10). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and within-group contrasts are reported).

The study used task-based fMRI of an executive function (N-back working memory) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise results with coordinates (meets I5, I6, I7, I9, I10). However, the NeuroStore record only lists omnibus between-group contrasts (group x condition; patient vs control) and group comparisons — no within-group task activation contrasts for any participant group are reported. This violates inclusion criterion I8 and matches exclusion criterion E5 (reports only between-group contrasts). Therefore the study must be excluded.

This is an fMRI task-based study using a Sternberg verbal working memory task in healthy adults (n=14). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise analyses (one-sample t-test) with model fit over the whole brain and within-group contrasts (experimental > control) for encoding, maintenance, and retrieval, with peaks reported in tables. These satisfy the requirements for task domain (working memory), whole-brain voxelwise evidence, within-group contrasts, and allowable reporting formats. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and it is empirical). Therefore the study should be included.

This fMRI study uses a task-based Stroop paradigm probing informational conflict (executive control/inhibition). It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (model fit over whole brain; voxel-level threshold p<0.001) and multiple within-group task contrasts (e.g., incongruent > nonconflict; error > correct). Results are reported as peak coordinates/tables. Participants are a healthy adult sample. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5 (fMRI task-based executive function), I6 (task within executive domains - inhibition/conflict), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise results), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (participant group acceptable), and I10 (results reported in coordinate tables). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text is sufficiently represented by the NeuroStore record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical fMRI study using an overt verbal fluency task (an executive domain: initiation/word generation). It reports a group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analysis (Analysis 16228196_analysis_0: model fit over whole brain; inference over whole brain) and also a within-group task contrast (Analysis 16228196_analysis_1: hard > easy, within-group). Peaks are reported. Thus the study meets inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (task in executive function domain), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise results), I8 (within-group task contrast), I9 (participant groups acceptable), and I10 (results reported as peaks/coordinates). No exclusion criteria apply: it is not ROI-only (E3), not connectivity-only (E4), not only between-group contrasts (E5), and is empirical (not E6).

This fMRI study examines central executive working memory with a task-based mental-arithmetic paradigm and reports multiple group-level, voxelwise within-group contrasts (e.g., High>Low, Task>Rest). Model fitting was performed over the whole brain with standard SPM second-level random-effects analyses and results are reported as peak coordinates/tables. These meet inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (working memory/executive domain), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise results), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (participant group acceptable), and I10 (coordinates/tables reported). No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, no connectivity-only, and within-group contrasts are present).

The study reports an event-related fMRI saccade inhibition task (inhibition domain) with group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses, but the only extracted analysis is a between-group interaction (controls ANT>FIX > patients PRO) and no within-group task contrasts are reported for any group. This violates the requirement for at least one within-group task activation (I8). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (inhibition falls within executive function), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analysis present). Inclusion criteria not met: I8 (no within-group contrast reported), I9 (conditional on I8 — no within-group contrast for any group). Exclusion criterion E5 is therefore triggered (only between-group contrast/group×condition interaction reported). Full text is sufficiently represented by the NeuroStore record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study uses PET and reports whole-brain, voxelwise, within-group contrasts (SO>OS) and parametric within-group analyses, satisfying whole-brain voxelwise evidence and within-group contrast criteria. However, the task is a sentence comprehension/syntactic processing paradigm (plausibility judgments), not an established executive-function task (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Although the authors examine individual differences in working memory and processing speed, the experimental manipulation targets syntactic complexity in language comprehension rather than an executive function domain. Therefore it does not meet inclusion criteria I5 and I6.

This study reports task-based fMRI of the Stop-Signal Task, an inhibition executive-function paradigm. It provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (Talairach coordinates) with reported contrasts and peak tables (several within-group contrasts: cognitive go-phase X vs O, successful stop > X/O, unsuccessful stop (fail) etc.). Results are reported across the whole brain with cluster-level correction and detailed peaks, satisfying whole-brain voxelwise reporting. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (inhibition executive domain), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise group analyses), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (participant group acceptable), and I10 (results reported as coordinate tables). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, no connectivity-only, no only between-group contrasts, and it is empirical). Full text is available in the provided record. Inclusion is appropriate.

This study reports task-based fMRI of an inhibition task (stop-signal) in cocaine-dependent and healthy male participants, with whole-brain voxelwise group-level analyses and reported peak coordinates (meets I5, I6, I7, I9, I10). However, the NeuroStore record and extracted analyses only report between-group contrasts / an interaction (HC SS > PCD SE) and region-of-interest comparisons; no within-group task activation contrast for any group (e.g., main effect of stop vs baseline, or stop-success vs go within a single group) is provided.
