Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E5 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions with no within-group activation map) and must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

The study reports task-based fMRI of an executive function task (n-back working memory with face stimuli), meeting I5 and I6. NeuroStore indicates voxelwise group-level SPM maps fitted over the whole brain (Model fit over: whole brain) and reports peaks/tables, satisfying I7 and I10. The record includes within-group task contrasts for both the autism and control groups (0-/1-/2-back > fixation), fulfilling I8. Any participant group is acceptable (clinical high-functioning autism and healthy controls), satisfying I9. No exclusion criteria are met: results are whole-brain voxelwise activation maps (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only), and within-group contrasts are reported, so E3–E6 do not apply. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an event-related fMRI study of response inhibition (stop-signal task), an executive function domain (inhibition). The NeuroStore record reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (random-effects second-level models) and within-group contrasts (e.g., successful stop > failed stop for men and women) with voxel-level thresholding and reported peak coordinates (Talairach). Results are reported in tables of peaks. These features satisfy all inclusion criteria for task, domain, whole-brain voxelwise evidence, and within-group contrasts; no exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears available via the extracted analyses. Hence the study should be INCLUDED.

The study is a PET task-based investigation of short-term verbal maintenance (working memory), and reports multiple within-group task contrasts (e.g., maintenance > fixation), so it meets I5 (PET task study), I6 (working memory executive domain), I8 (within-group contrasts), and I9 (participant groups qualify). However, all extracted analyses in the NeuroStore record report model fitting and inference restricted to region-of-interest (ROI) analyses; no analysis is described as a whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task activation map. Therefore the study violates exclusion criterion E3 (reports only ROI / small-volume-corrected analyses with no voxelwise results) and fails inclusion criterion I7 (whole-brain evidence). Based on the provided document, exclusion is warranted because a qualifying whole-brain voxelwise contrast is not available in the extracted records.

The study reports task-based fMRI of an executive function (working memory) training paradigm, with whole-brain voxelwise model fits and reported peak coordinates. At least one qualifying within-group task contrast is present (analysis 3: scan 3 working memory task > scan 1/2 control; within-group interaction). Group-level analyses are reported (second-level random-effects for analyses with n=8, and fixed-effect within-subject contrasts), and results are reported as peaks/tables. This satisfies all inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only (E3), not connectivity/resting-state-only (E4), and within-group task contrasts are reported (not only between-group; E5). Full text appears complete for screening. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This is an event-related fMRI study of response inhibition (Go/No-go), an executive function task. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (model fit and inference over whole brain; voxel-level Gaussian-field correction) with tables of reported peak coordinates. Within-group contrasts are present (Go vs baseline, No-go vs baseline, No-go > Go, Go > No-go). These satisfy inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (inhibition domain), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise results), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (participant group acceptable), and I10 (results reported in coordinate tables). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group contrasts, empirical data).

The study uses task-based fMRI of working memory in postmenopausal women and reports whole-brain, voxelwise results (peaks) from N-back contrasts, satisfying I5, I6, I7, I9, and I10. However, all reported analyses are drug-condition comparison interactions (drug × load) rather than a within-group main effect of task (e.g., 3-back > 0-back) for any group. This means the paper reports only group-by-condition interaction contrasts and no within-group task activation contrast, which meets exclusion criterion E5. Therefore the study must be excluded.

The study reports task-based BOLD fMRI of voluntary breath holding, described as a volitional inhibitory behavior and linked by the authors to response-inhibition networks, satisfying the executive function domain (inhibition). Analyses are group-level, voxelwise, whole-brain (model fit and inference over whole brain) with within-group simple-effect contrasts for breath hold and peaks reported in a table. This meets I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 and I10. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study should be included.

The NeuroStore record shows this is a task-based fMRI study of executive function (N-back, Continuous Performance Task) with whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses reported; however, all extracted contrasts are omnibus between-group contrasts (patient vs. control or interactions). No within-group task activation contrasts for any group are reported in the document. This violates inclusion criterion I8 and therefore meets exclusion criterion E5 (only between-group contrasts reported). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (tasks are established executive function domains: working memory, inhibition/vigilance), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise analyses), I10 (results reported as coordinate tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I8 (no within-group task contrast reported), I9 (participant-group provision depends on I8; no within-group contrast reported so the requirement that a within-group contrast be present is not satisfied). fulltext_incomplete=false

This fMRI study used task-based contrasts assessing temporal storage and comparison (duration identification and discrimination), which constitutes working memory-type processing (an executive function domain). It reports within-group contrasts (discrimination > identification and identification > discrimination). At least two analyses were estimated and tested voxelwise over the whole brain with volume-corrected voxel-level thresholding and tables of reported peak coordinates, satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement. Participants were a within-group sample of healthy adults (n=12). Although one analysis used an ROI, whole-brain voxelwise results are also reported, so E3 is not met. All inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

Excluded because the reported analyses are ROI-restricted and only between-group interaction contrasts are provided. Exclusion criteria met: E3 (analyses were fit and inference restricted to a region of interest; no voxelwise whole-brain results reported) and E5 (the reported contrasts are between-group comparisons/interactions - musicians vs non-musicians - with no within-group task>control or task>baseline contrasts reported for any group). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (task involves mental arithmetic with stated links to working memory/executive processes), I9 (healthy adult participants). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise group-level task activation map reported), I8 (no within-group task contrast reported). Full text is complete as provided.

This is an fMRI empirical study reporting task-evoked activations for eye movement paradigms including an oculomotor delayed response (ODR) task that assesses spatial working memory (an executive function domain) and anti/visually guided saccade contrasts involving inhibitory control. Multiple group-level, voxelwise, whole-brain statistical maps are reported (model fit and inference over whole brain; peaks reported in tables) and several within-group contrasts are provided (e.g., Smooth pursuit > fixation; Visually guided saccades > fixation; ODR > visually guided saccades) for patient and healthy groups. Reporting includes coordinate tables of peaks. Therefore all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The NeuroStore record reports a task-based fMRI N-back study (working memory) with whole-brain, voxelwise group-level maps (meets I5, I6, I7). However, the only extracted contrast in the document is labeled as a between-group contrast (3-back > 0-back [between-group]) and no within-group task activation contrast for any group is provided in the study document. Therefore the study appears to report ONLY between-group contrasts, triggering exclusion criterion E5. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (working memory task), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise analysis). Inclusion criteria not met: I8 (no within-group task contrast reported). I9 is not satisfied because it depends on I8. Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

This is an fMRI task study of mental rotation (working memory/manipulation), fitting the review’s executive-function domain. Group-level, voxelwise whole-brain GLM analyses are reported (Model fit over: whole brain; coordinate space Talairach) with within-group task contrasts (e.g., simultaneous matrix rotation > simultaneous 3-D cube rotation) and peak coordinates in tables. Results are voxelwise and not ROI-only or connectivity-only. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (working memory task), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise results), I8 (within-group contrasts), I9 (participant groups acceptable), and I10 (results reported as coordinate tables). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Sample size is small (n=11) but does not violate inclusion rules. Full text is sufficiently represented in the provided NeuroStore record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical PET study of verbal working memory (2-back) that reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise SPM99 analyses. Analyses are described as 'cross subject regression, within-group' (i.e., within-group correlation of rCBF with task accuracy) with model fit over the whole brain and reported peak coordinates. Thus it meets the meta-analysis requirements: task-based PET (I5), working memory domain (I6), whole-brain voxelwise group maps (I7), within-group task contrast via within-group regression (I8), any participant group acceptable (I9), and coordinates reported (I10). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical).

The study reports task-based fMRI of working memory (executive function domain) with group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses and voxelwise inference (FDR voxel-level). It includes within-group task contrasts (structured > unstructured and unstructured > structured) and parametric modulation analyses, with reported peak coordinates. Participant groups are described. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

Exclusion E5 applies: the NeuroStore record reports an age group x task x drug interaction (between-group) and a drug>placebo contrast during the task but does not report any within-group task>rest (or task vs baseline) voxelwise activation map for any group. Inclusion met: I5 (PET task-based study), I6 (working memory task), I9 (healthy adult participant group). Inclusion not met: I7 (no clear whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task-evoked map reported) and I8 (no within-group task contrast reported). The available analysis is ROI-based or between-group/interactions, so the study does not provide the required within-group whole-brain task activation contrast for inclusion.

This study reports task-based fMRI using an n-back working-memory paradigm (I5,I6). Whole-brain voxelwise model fitting and whole-brain inference are reported (model fit over: whole brain; inference over: whole brain; voxel-level SnPM correction), satisfying whole-brain evidence (I7). It includes within-group task contrasts (2-back > 0-back) for both controls and patients, meeting the within-group contrast requirement (I8). Participant groups include clinical (cerebellar infarct) and healthy controls; within-group contrasts are present for groups, so participant group type is acceptable (I9). Results are reported as peak coordinates/tables for whole-brain analyses, satisfying reporting criterion (I10). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes within-group contrasts, empirical fMRI data).

This is an fMRI study of spatial working memory (an executive function domain) that reports whole-brain, voxelwise, group-level within-group contrasts. NeuroStore extractions list multiple whole-brain voxelwise analyses (model fit over: whole brain) described as omnibus within-group contrasts with FDR-corrected voxelwise inference and tables of reported peak coordinates. Participants (n=16) are a human cohort. Results are reported as coordinate tables and described in the abstract. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

This fMRI study uses a task-based working memory paradigm (feature binding), which falls under executive function (working memory). The NeuroStore record reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (object>location and location>object; omnibus Age×Condition) satisfying the whole-brain requirement. The study also reports within-group task contrasts (combination>object and combination>location in young adults), satisfying the within-group contrast requirement, even though these within-group contrasts were ROI-limited. The study is empirical, task-based fMRI, and reports coordinate results. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10.

This study reports task-based fMRI of working memory (WM updating and maintenance), an executive function domain. Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses are explicitly reported (model fit over: whole brain; inference over: whole brain; second-level random-effects ANCOVA), with voxelwise FDR thresholding and tables of reported peaks. Crucially, within-group contrasts are present (e.g. FT>FIX and VT>FT for Control and PTSD groups), satisfying the requirement for a within-group task activation map. It is empirical human neuroimaging work and not ROI-only or connectivity-only. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective.

This study reports an fMRI task (n-back) probing working memory (executive function), meeting I5 and I6. It includes a group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analysis (model fit and inference over whole brain; mapwise correction; Talairach coordinates and a table of peaks reported), satisfying I7 and I10. It reports a within-group contrast (2-back > 0-back) using a random-effects analysis, meeting I8. Participant sample is acceptable (n=9 adults), satisfying I9. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and the paper is empirical. Full text is available in the extracted record, so fulltext_incomplete is false. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This study reports task-based fMRI (Go/No-Go inhibition) in healthy adults and directly assesses an executive function domain (inhibition). Analyses are group-level voxelwise (model fit and inference over whole brain using one-sample t-tests and multiple regression), and at least one contrast is a within-group task contrast (successful No-go vs baseline). Whole-brain results are reported as peak coordinates (tables) in Talairach space. These facts satisfy all inclusion criteria (I5–I10). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, and include within-group task contrasts. Full text is available in the provided record.

The study reports a task-based fMRI N-back working memory paradigm (an established executive function) with group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses and voxelwise inference (cluster-corrected). It includes within-group task contrasts for healthy participants (analysis_15804721_analysis_0) and patients (analysis_15804721_analysis_1). Results are reported as whole-brain peak coordinates/tables. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5 (fMRI task-based), I6 (working memory), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise evidence), I8 (within-group contrasts), I9 (participant groups acceptable), and I10 (coordinates/tables reporting). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Based on the provided document I am confident this paper should be included in the meta-analysis of executive-function task activations.

This is an event-related fMRI study of inhibitory control/interference resolution (executive function) using a Sternberg item recognition task (letters and objects), reporting group-level, voxelwise whole-brain contrasts comparing interference versus control trials with peak coordinates (Table tbl1). The analyses are group random-effect GLM voxelwise maps (model fit over whole brain) and report within-task interference > control contrasts (letter and object tasks). Results are reported as coordinates and tables. Therefore it meets the fMRI task-based executive function requirement, uses established EF domains (working memory/inhibition), includes whole-brain voxelwise group analyses, reports within-group task contrasts, and provides coordinate-table reporting.

This PET study reports task-based activations for executive domains (go/no-go inhibition and short-term memory/working memory), using whole-brain voxelwise analyses and within-group task > control contrasts. NeuroStore indicates whole-brain model fitting and inference, group-level within-group contrasts (auditory and visual go/no-go; auditory and visual STM), and reported peak coordinates/tables. All required inclusion criteria are met (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, no connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and it is empirical).

This fMRI study used a Go/No-Go inhibition task (task-based fMRI) and reports within-group, voxelwise whole-brain contrasts (go>visual control; go/no-go>visual control; go/no-go>go) with tables of peak coordinates. The task probes inhibition (an executive function domain). Whole-brain SPM analyses are reported at group level. Participants are healthy volunteers. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study uses task-based paradigms probing reasoning and a maintenance (working memory) condition, meeting the executive-function domain (working memory) and task-based imaging requirement. Analyses are whole-brain, voxelwise, group-level contrasts (e.g., reasoning>rest, maintenance>rest, reasoning>maintenance) with cluster-level correction and coordinates reported in tables. At least one within-group task contrast is present. Participants are healthy adults. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and it is empirical). Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

This is an fMRI task-based study of cognitive control (task switching) with mixed blocked/event-related design. It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise random-effects GLM analyses (model fit and inference over whole brain) and provides within-group task contrasts (transient and sustained task-switch vs single-task/repeat contrasts) with reported peak coordinates. Results satisfy executive-function domain (cognitive flexibility) and whole-brain within-group contrast requirements; reported coordinates/tables suffice. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore include.

This fMRI study examines working memory (an executive function) with within-group task contrasts, but all reported analyses are region-of-interest (model fit and inference restricted to ROIs) rather than whole-brain voxelwise results. That violates the requirement for voxelwise whole-brain evidence and matches exclusion criterion E3. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI assessing executive function), I6 (working memory task), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported), I9 (acceptable participant group), I10 (results reported as coordinate table). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise group-level activation maps reported). Therefore the study is excluded under E3.

The NeuroStore record reports only a between-group interaction contrast (APOE ε4 vs non-ε4: two-back > zero-back) with whole-brain voxelwise inference and no within-group task activation contrast for any group. Exclusion criterion E5 applies (reports ONLY between-group contrast/interaction). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (working memory/N-back within executive function), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise analysis), I9 (participant groups acceptable), I10 (whole-brain results reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I8 (no within-group task contrast reported). fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study is a PET (and EEG) task-based neuroimaging study of an auditory continuous performance task (CPT), which maps to executive function domain of vigilance. It reports whole-brain, voxelwise, group-level within-group contrasts (multiple Active>Rest and Rest>Active contrasts) with voxelwise inference and reported peak coordinates (Talairach/MNI). Results are reported in tables of peaks. Participants are healthy adults. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 and I10; no exclusion criteria apply.

This PET study uses a task-based continuous performance task (CPT), which is an established vigilance/sustained-attention executive function domain. It reports multiple group-level, voxelwise within-group contrasts (Active > Rest; Rest > Active) with whole-brain inference and voxelwise FDR thresholding and tables of reported peak coordinates. At least one analysis is a within-group task contrast and results are reported as whole-brain voxelwise maps/peaks. Therefore all inclusion criteria for task type, domain, whole-brain voxelwise group results, and within-group contrasts are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study of verbal working memory (executive function domain). The NeuroStore record reports at least one group-level, voxelwise, within-group whole-brain task contrast (analysis 16846859_analysis_5: pseudoword maintenance > word maintenance; model fit over: whole brain; voxel-level), estimated with a random-effects one-sample t test and reported peaks. Other within-group contrasts and connectivity analyses are also present. Participants are human (n=11). Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and empirical).

This PET study reports a working memory task (executive function) with whole-brain voxelwise analyses and at least one within-group task contrast. It uses task-based PET (H2 15O) during a working memory (faces) block design (I5,I6). Model was fit over the whole brain and reported peaks (voxelwise, cluster-thresholded), satisfying whole-brain evidence (I7,I10). Analysis 9177249_analysis_1 is a within-group drug effect on task (off drug WM task > on drug rest / interaction within-group), providing a within-group task contrast required (I8). Participant groups are healthy adults (I9). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only (E3), not connectivity/resting-state only (E4), and the paper reports a within-group contrast (so E5 does not apply); it is empirical human neuroimaging data (not E6). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

The study reports task-based fMRI of executive function (response inhibition via a go/no-go task) and selective attention. Whole-brain voxelwise group analyses are reported (model fit over: whole brain) with voxelwise thresholding and tables of reported peaks. Multiple within-group contrasts are present (no-go > go; nine stimuli > one stimulus) for both children and adults, satisfying the requirement for at least one within-group task contrast. Reporting includes peak coordinates/tables. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of working memory (delayed recognition of faces and voices), which falls within executive function domains (working memory). This is a task-based fMRI study using a Stop-Signal Task that probes inhibitory control (an executive function). Thus all inclusion criteria are satisfied: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (inhibition domain), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise group analyses), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported), I9 (participant group acceptable), I10 (results reported as coordinates). No exclusion criteria (E3-E6) apply: analyses are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and within-group contrasts are present. This study is excluded because it reports only region-of-interest (region-level) analyses and an omnibus between-group ANOVA with no evidence of a group-level, voxelwise within-group task activation map. Exclusion IDs met: E3 (ROI-only analyses, no voxelwise whole-brain results) and E5 (only between-group/interaction contrasts reported, no within-group task contrast shown). Inclusion IDs met: I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function—Go/No-Go inhibition), I6 (task falls within inhibition domain), I9 (clinical and healthy participant groups are acceptable). Inclusion IDs not met: I7 (no group-level voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked statistical map reported; model fit over = region of interest), I8 (no within-group task contrast reported in the extraction; contrast listed is omnibus between-group). Therefore the paper fails required inclusion criteria and is excluded.

The study is an empirical task-based fMRI investigation of working memory (n-back), an executive function domain, satisfying I5 and I6. Analyses were whole-brain, voxelwise (model fit over: whole brain) and report coordinates/peaks, satisfying I7 and I10. The paper reports within-group task contrasts (longitudinal within-patient contrasts: fMRI-2 > fMRI-1 for 2-back and 3-back), meeting I8. Clinical participants are permitted, so I9 is satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only (E3), not connectivity/resting-only (E4), and within-group contrasts are present so E5 does not apply; the paper is empirical (not E6). Thresholding details do not negate voxelwise whole-brain results. Therefore include.

This PET study examines working memory (face memory) performance and task-evoked regional cerebral blood flow, reporting voxelwise, whole-brain, group-level within-group analyses (cross-subject regressions of rCBF changes vs RT) with Talairach coordinates. The report includes whole-brain voxelwise results (model fit over whole brain, peaks reported), uses an executive function task (working memory), and presents within-group contrasts. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, and not only between-group contrasts. Full text is available in the provided NeuroStore record.

The study reports task-based fMRI using the Tower of London (planning) task, an established executive function paradigm. Results are reported as peak coordinates. Participants are human healthy adults. Therefore the study satisfies all inclusion criteria for task-based executive-function whole-brain within-group activation reporting.

This PET task-based study reports multiple whole-brain, voxelwise, group-level within-subject contrasts (e.g., 0back>2back, TSDslow>IDslow) with reported peaks and Talairach coordinates. Tasks include working memory (2-back) and perceptual discrimination within an executive-function domain (working memory). Therefore it meets inclusion: I5 (PET task-based study), I6 (working memory task), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise analyses), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (participant group reported), and I10 (voxelwise results reported as peaks/coordinates). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group contrasts, empirical human neuroimaging). Full text appears available in the provided NeuroStore record.

The study reports task-based fMRI of response inhibition (Go/No-Go), satisfying executive-function domain (inhibition). Analysis 15203175_analysis_0 is a group-level, voxelwise whole-brain regression (model fit over and inference over whole brain, corrected voxelwise), demonstrating whole-brain task-evoked results. Analyses 15203175_analysis_2 and _3 report Press for Non-X > Press for X peaks (within-group task contrast), indicating a within-group task activation map is available. The task and results are reported for an observational cohort of young adults; results include coordinate-space peaks. Therefore inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 and I10 are met. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only (E3), not connectivity/resting-state only (E4), and not only between-group contrasts (E5) since within-group contrasts are reported; study is empirical human neuroimaging (E6 not applicable).

This fMRI study directly assesses working memory (an executive function) using task-based N-back style manipulations for prosodic and lexico-semantic emotion, reporting group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effects second-level and voxelwise thresholding with reported peak coordinates and tables). Multiple within-group contrasts and parametric within-group associations are reported (e.g. lexico-semantic > prosodic; parametric modulation for prosodic and lexico-semantic emotion), satisfying the requirement for within-group task contrasts. Participants are healthy adults (n=26), and results are reported as voxelwise peaks/tables. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5–I10 and should be included in the executive-function activation meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study of working memory (spatial WM) that reports group-level, voxelwise within-group contrasts with whole-brain model fitting and peak coordinates (several analyses: maintenance > nonmemory, selection from memory; thresholding and Talairach coordinates reported). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for modality (I5), task domain (working memory; I6), whole-brain voxelwise results (I7), within-group task contrasts (I8), participant eligibility (healthy adults; I9), and reporting of coordinates/tables (I10). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not limited to ROIs or connectivity-only, and the study is empirical. Full text is available in the provided record.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a Stroop word-color interference task (an inhibition/conflict executive function paradigm) with within-group contrasts (congruent > incongruent). A group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analysis is reported (Model fit over: whole brain; n=34; reported peaks in Table 1a), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps. Partial ROI analyses are also present but do not negate the whole-brain result. Results are reported in coordinate space with tabulated peaks. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears available through the NeuroStore record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

Excluded because all reported analyses were modeled over regions of interest rather than as group-level voxelwise whole-brain maps, so the study does not meet the requirement for whole-brain evidence (I7). Exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI/SVC analyses with no voxelwise results) applies. The study does meet several inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (working memory task within executive-function domains), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported), and I9 (participant group reported). Inclusion criterion I7 (whole-brain voxelwise analysis) is not met. No other exclusion criteria appear to apply. The NeuroStore record explicitly states 'Model fit over: region of interest' for all analyses and reports peaks from ROI analyses; therefore the paper must be excluded from the whole-brain activation meta-analysis.

The study reports task-based fMRI of executive domains (Sternberg working memory and a selective-attention SAT task), satisfying I5 and I6. NeuroStore lists multiple analyses with reported peak tables (Tables 2, 4, 6), which indicates group-level voxelwise task-evoked results reported as coordinates (satisfying I7 and I10). Although one analysis explicitly reports an ROI model, the presence of coordinate peak tables for other task analyses implies whole-brain voxelwise results and within-group task-related contrasts (I8). Any participant group is acceptable (I9). No exclusion criteria are met: the paper does not report only ROI/SVC analyses, only connectivity, or only between-group contrasts. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective.

This fMRI study uses an N-back working memory task (executive function) and reports a group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analysis (Analysis 17021168_analysis_0: model fit and inference over whole brain with cluster-level correction). Participant sample and task domain meet inclusion, and although ROI analyses are also reported, the presence of whole-brain voxelwise results means the study is not ROI-only. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study satisfies all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study of working memory (N-back) that reports voxelwise, whole-brain group-level statistical maps and includes at least one within-group task contrast (Analysis 17010573_analysis_0: controls 2-back > 0-back). This is a task-based fMRI study of response inhibition (Go/No-Go), an established executive function (inhibition). This is a task-based fMRI study of working memory (executive function domain) reporting whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses. This is an event-related fMRI study that examines motor intention (high-level movement plans), which maps onto executive domains of planning/initiation. This fMRI study tests executive tasks (WCST) and reports coordinate peaks, but ALL extracted analyses were fit over regions-of-interest (Model fit over: region of interest) rather than voxelwise whole-brain group maps. That violates inclusion criterion I7 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results). Furthermore, the reported contrasts are drug vs placebo effects / drug×task interactions rather than a within-group main effect of task (no clear within-group task>baseline voxelwise contrast reported), so the study also meets exclusion criterion E5. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (WCST = cognitive flexibility), I9 (participant group acceptable), I10 (results reported as coordinates/tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (whole-brain voxelwise group-level map) and I8 (within-group task contrast). Therefore the study must be excluded.

This fMRI study used an established executive-function task (N-Back working memory) and reports a group-level, within-subject (within-group) task contrast (acute smoking x test session x task load interaction). The model was fit voxelwise over the whole brain and reported peak coordinates (even though inference was restricted via small-volume correction), satisfying the requirement for voxelwise task-evoked results. Participants include a clinical sample (nicotine dependence), which is acceptable. Therefore inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 and I10 are met. Exclusion E3 (only ROI/SVC results) does not apply because the model was estimated over the whole brain and coordinate results are reported; although inference used SVC, voxelwise mapping was performed and peaks are provided. No other exclusion criteria apply. Full text is available in the NeuroStore record provided, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

The study reports task-based fMRI of working memory (2-back), an executive function domain, with whole-brain voxelwise analyses and group-level results. Whole-brain model fit and inference are explicitly stated; results are reported as peak coordinates (Table 1). This meets all inclusion criteria and does not violate any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group contrasts).

This is an event-related fMRI study of working memory (an executive function domain) using a Sternberg item-recognition task. Participant group-level contrasts are present and clearly described. Therefore the paper meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 and I10 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This fMRI study examined working memory (N-back) and reports voxelwise whole-brain and ROI regression results relating prenatal marijuana exposure to task activation, but it does not report any within-group main effect (within-group task contrast) for any participant group. Inclusion met: I5 (task-based fMRI executive function), I6 (working memory), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise group-level results), I10 (whole-brain results clearly reported). Inclusion not met: I8 (no within-group task contrast reported), I9 (conditional requirement of a within-group contrast not satisfied). Exclusion criteria met: E5 (reports only between-subject regression/associations and ROI SVCs, with no within-group task activation contrast). Therefore exclude.

This is an fMRI task-based study of working memory (executive function), reporting a within-group contrast (high working memory load > low-demand baseline) with whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (model fit over whole brain; voxel-level threshold p<0.0001) and reported peak coordinates. Participants (n=9) and BOLD measures are clearly reported. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I5 (fMRI task assessing executive function), I6 (working memory task), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise evidence), I8 (within-group task contrast), I9 (participant group acceptable), and I10 (results reported as coordinates/peaks). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical).

This is a task-based fMRI study of verbal working memory (N-back), an executive function. The study is a task-based fMRI investigation of working memory (n-back), an established executive function domain, and reports voxelwise whole-brain group-level results (MNI coordinates, tables of peaks). Importantly, it includes at least one within-group voxelwise contrast (analysis 17544015_analysis_3: interaction of working memory and emotion within males), satisfying the requirement for a within-group task contrast (the interaction contrast is a within-group task-related contrast). Results are reported as whole-brain voxelwise maps and coordinates, and participants are healthy adults. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, or only between-group contrasts with no within-group contrasts) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

Excluded because the study does not meet the group-level whole-brain voxelwise result requirement (I7). Although this is an fMRI task study of working memory (meets I5, I6), it reports a within-group contrast (delay > control) and whole-brain coordinates/peaks (meets I8 and I10) and includes a participant group (healthy; meets I9), the reported analysis appears to be based on a single participant (n=1). The meta-analysis requires at least one group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical map; a single-subject result does not satisfy I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are otherwise met.

This is an fMRI study of working memory using an n-back task (meets I5 and I6). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise second-level contrasts fit over the whole brain (Model fit over: whole brain), and reports peak coordinates (Table 2), satisfying whole-brain evidence (I7 and I10). It includes a within-subject/within-group task contrast (3-back > 0-back within medication-free vs post-medication sessions; an interaction specified as within-group), meeting I8. Any participant group is acceptable (I9). Although inference was restricted to an ROI with SVC, the analysis was not limited to ROI-only reporting, so E3 does not apply. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

This PET study directly assesses an executive-function domain (working memory) using a task-based paradigm (I5,I6). Analyses were estimated over the whole brain (Model fit over: whole brain) with voxelwise results reported as coordinate peak tables (reported peaks in Tables) satisfying whole-brain evidence (I7,I10). The paper reports within-group task contrasts (WM > baseline and Sign > Speech within-group contrasts), meeting the within-group contrast requirement (I8). Participant sample is acceptable per criteria (I9). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical). Hence the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included.

The NeuroStore record reports an fMRI Stroop task (inhibition) so it meets I5 and I6, and coordinate results are reported (I10). However, all extracted analyses are group comparisons or group x condition interactions and no within-group task contrast is listed, so inclusion criterion I8 (within-group contrast) is not met and exclusion E5 (only between-group contrasts/interactions reported) applies. Additionally, the extraction states 'Model fit over: region of interest' (with inference described over the whole brain), indicating the models were estimated within ROIs rather than as group-level voxelwise maps; therefore I7 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain results) is not satisfied and exclusion E3 (ROI-only/SVC with no voxelwise results) applies. Because at least one inclusion criterion is unmet and exclusion criteria are triggered, the study is excluded.

Exclusion criteria met: E3 and E5. The NeuroStore record indicates all reported analyses are region-of-interest (Model fit over: region of interest; region-level thresholding; anatomically defined ROIs), so no voxelwise whole-brain task-activation maps are reported (E3). The documented contrast is an omnibus between-group comparison; no within-group task activation contrast for any group is provided in the extracted analyses (E5). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (working memory task—n-back), I9 (participant groups including clinical sample). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise group-level activation map reported), I8 (no within-group task contrast reported). Therefore the study must be excluded.

The study reports task-based fMRI BOLD data collected during a task that involves switching between mouse types (internal models), which corresponds to cognitive flexibility (an executive function). Therefore the study satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This fMRI study reports task-based executive function (response inhibition) activations across three canonical inhibition tasks (go/no-go, flanker, stimulus-response compatibility). Thus all inclusion criteria are met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (working memory), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise results), I8 (within-group contrasts), I9 (participant group acceptable), and I10 (results reported as coordinate tables). The study is an fMRI task-based experiment using a verbal working memory paradigm (an established executive function domain). Results and inference were performed over the whole brain. Participants are a human sample (healthy adults). Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This PET study uses an immediate serial recall task (working memory), which falls within executive function domains. This fMRI task-switching study assesses cognitive flexibility (an executive function) using a task-based paradigm (I5,I6). The study reports an event-related fMRI task probing working memory (faces and scenes) with attention cues, fitting the executive function domain. This study is an empirical fMRI task-based investigation of verbal working memory, which is within the executive function domain (working memory). This fMRI study used an event-related working-memory task (retro-cue paradigm) assessing spatial orienting within working memory, an executive-function domain (working memory). This is a task-based fMRI study using an n-back working memory task (executive function domain) with emotional stimuli. This fMRI study used a task-based N-back working memory paradigm (executive function domain) and reports multiple group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (GLM and voxelwise ANOVA) including within-group task contrasts (e.g., 2-back > 1-back). This is a task-based fMRI study of working memory (listening-span task), an established executive function domain. This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using an n-back working memory paradigm (executive function). Group-level, voxelwise random-effects analyses were fit over the whole brain and multiple within-group task contrasts are reported (e.g., identity match vs comparison; lag contrasts). Voxelwise inference is reported (FDR-corrected and uncorrected voxel-level thresholds) with peak coordinates in tables, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps. Participants are a within-group sample (n=13 healthy adults). Therefore all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met, and no exclusion criteria apply.

The NeuroStore record reports only between-group contrasts comparing chronic cocaine users to controls for successful inhibitions (STOPS) and failed inhibitions (ERRORS). Therefore the study violates exclusion criterion E5 (only between-group contrasts reported with no within-group task activation). The study reports an event-related fMRI investigation of verbal working memory (an executive function domain) with a within-subject manipulation (HOLD vs RELEASE) and provides group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (model fit over: whole brain) with reported peak coordinates. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This PET study used a task-based N-back working memory paradigm (meets I5,I6). Multiple group-level, voxelwise within-group contrasts (2BT > control) were reported with whole-brain voxel-by-voxel analyses and coordinate peaks in tables (meets I7,I8,I10). Participant groups are acceptable (smokers and ex-smokers; within-group contrasts reported) meeting I9. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group contrasts, empirical data).

This is an empirical fMRI study of working memory (haptic orientation WM), a canonical executive function domain. The record reports multiple group-level, voxelwise, within-group task contrasts with whole-brain model fit and whole-brain inference (e.g., exploration > ITI, matching > ITI, epoch contrasts 2–4s, 4–6s, 6–8s), thresholding and tables of reported peaks. Analysis description specifies a group fixed-effects GLM and Talairach coordinates (tables), satisfying whole-brain voxelwise reporting. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis objective and inclusion criteria and does not meet any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group contrasts, empirical data present).

This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) using a modified Guilty Knowledge Test that requires participants to suppress truthful responses and produce lies, engaging inhibitory/cognitive-control processes (I6). The paper reports within-group contrasts (Lie > Truth; Lie > Control) meeting I8. A second-level, random-effects, voxelwise GLM was run across the whole brain (model fit over whole brain), and peak coordinates are reported in a table (I7, I10). Participant sample and reporting meet I9. Although inference was restricted to a priori ROIs and small-volume correction was used, voxelwise group-level maps and coordinate tables are reported, so this does not meet the exclusion criterion for ROI-only reporting (E3). Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive-function task activations.

The study reports task-based fMRI of working memory (executive function), using a task that manipulates maintenance vs manipulation and content type, satisfying I5 and I6. NeuroStore shows voxelwise whole-brain model fits and whole-brain inference with voxel-level FDR thresholding and tables of reported peak coordinates, satisfying I7 and I10. Multiple analyses are explicitly described as within-group contrasts (contrast, within-group), satisfying I8. Participant data are reported (n=13), and any participant group is acceptable, satisfying I9. No exclusion criteria are met: analyses are not ROI-only (E3), not connectivity/resting-state only (E4), and not only between-group contrasts (E5); the paper is empirical (not E6). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and violates none, and should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This study reports task-based fMRI of executive function (verbal working memory: Sternberg and n-back), satisfying I5 and I6. Analyses were whole-brain (model fit over: whole brain) and group-level random-effects voxelwise contrasts with reported peak coordinates/tables, satisfying I7 and I10. Multiple within-group task contrasts and parametric (load) modulations are reported (Sternberg, n-back, encoding, responding), satisfying I8. Participants are healthy adults (I9 satisfied). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not limited to ROIs/SVC only (E3 not met), not connectivity/resting-state only (E4 not met), and include within-group task contrasts rather than only between-group contrasts (E5 not met); the paper is empirical (E6 not met). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and violates none, and is appropriate for inclusion in the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an fMRI task study of response inhibition using go/no-go tasks (letter and emotional faces), which falls within executive function (inhibition). The NeuroStore record shows group-level, voxelwise whole-brain random-effects analyses (model fit over: whole brain; Talairach coordinates reported; peaks listed) with within-group contrasts (letter go > letter no-go; emotional go > emotional no-go). Participants are healthy humans (n=13). Results are reported as coordinates/peaks. Therefore all inclusion criteria for task-based whole-brain within-group activation maps are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study that reports whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise task-evoked activation maps (model fit over whole brain; voxel-level inference; reported peak coordinates in tables). Within-group task contrasts are reported (active > inactive for FT, SRT, 4CRT), satisfying the requirement for within-group contrasts. The tasks include simple and four-choice reaction time paradigms that map onto established executive domains (vigilance/response initiation and tasks with planning/cognitive load as described in the abstract), and the paper explicitly reports recruitment of planning-related areas for the higher-load 4CRT task. Participants are healthy volunteers (acceptable per I9). Results are reported as coordinates/tables (I10). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is suitable for inclusion in a meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an fMRI, task-based study of working memory (Sternberg task) addressing retrieval (executive function). Whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (model fit over: whole brain; reported peaks; MNI coordinates), and multiple within-group contrasts are provided (e.g., L1>Control, L2>L1, L3>L2, non-targets>targets). Participants: healthy n=15. Thus the study meets inclusion criteria: I5 (fMRI task-based), I6 (working memory), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise results), I8 (within-group contrasts), I9 (participant group acceptable), and I10 (results reported as coordinates/peaks). Note a minor ambiguity: the extraction lists “fixed effects model of one single subject” for some model lines, but the presence of group-level reported peaks across 15 subjects and explicitly labeled within-group contrasts supports inclusion. Full text is sufficiently complete for screening.

The study reports an empirical fMRI task-based investigation of working memory (an executive function domain) with whole-brain voxelwise model fitting and reported peak coordinates. Multiple within-group task contrasts are reported (e.g., SOMT > CT, stimulus position contrasts). Participants are a healthy sample (n=17). Results are reported as peaks/coordinates. Thus all inclusion criteria are satisfied (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10) and no exclusion criteria apply. The NeuroStore record appears complete for screening purposes, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

This fMRI study uses a task-based delayed-recognition paradigm assessing kinesthetic working memory (an executive function). It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (second-level one-sample t-tests) with coordinate peaks/tables for within-group contrasts (Set 3 > baseline for encoding, maintenance, recognition) and parametric modulation by memory load. Results are reported as peaks/tables, satisfying whole-brain reporting. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group contrasts, empirical data).

This fMRI study tests working memory (Sternberg item-recognition) and reports within-group task contrasts, so it meets inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (working memory domain), I8 (within-group contrasts), and I9 (participant group acceptable). However, all reported analyses are region-of-interest (ROI) analyses with small-volume correction (model fit over and inference restricted to ROIs: left IFG and ACC), and no whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps are reported. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I7 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (studies reporting only ROI/SVC analyses). Because I7 is not met, the study must be excluded.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of verbal working memory (an executive function). The record reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLM analyses with corrected thresholds and tables of peak coordinates (satisfying whole-brain evidence and coordinate reporting). Within-group task contrasts and interactions are explicitly reported (interaction, within-group), and at least one qualifies as a within-group task contrast. Participants are a human group (n=11 adults). Thus all inclusion criteria for the review are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI task-based study of working memory (executive function domain) with healthy adult participants (n=26). It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (model fit over whole brain) including within-group contrasts: ON>OFF for phonological and spatial working memory, a conjunction, and direct Phonological>Spatial and Spatial>Phonological contrasts. Results are voxelwise and whole-brain, thresholded (FWE p<0.001 for main contrasts) with peak coordinates reported in tables. These features satisfy inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears available via the NeuroStore record, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

This is an event-related task-based fMRI study of working memory (auditory delayed recognition of voice identity and location), meeting the executive-function domain (I5, I6). The paper reports multiple group-level, voxelwise whole-brain contrasts (e.g., Location>control, Voice>control) with whole-brain model fit and inference and tables of peak coordinates, satisfying whole-brain voxelwise reporting (I7,I10). There are explicit within-group task contrasts (Location>control; Voice>control), meeting I8. Participant group (n=14 adults) is reported, satisfying I9. While some analyses used ROI-restricted inference for direct comparisons, the presence of whole-brain group-level activation maps means the study is not ROI-only (E3 not met). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete as provided.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using an N-back working memory task (executive function). Analyses include group-level voxelwise model fitting across the whole brain with reported voxelwise peak coordinates (despite inference being restricted via small-volume correction). A within-group task contrast (2-Back > 0-Back) is reported. Results are reported as coordinates/peaks. These satisfy the review objective and inclusion criteria for task, domain, voxelwise group analysis, within-group contrast, and reporting format. No exclusion criteria (only-ROI/SVC without voxelwise maps, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met.

The study reports task-based fMRI of verbal working memory (digit span), an executive function domain, with whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses and within-group task contrasts (e.g., revised lag 1 digit span (on) > digit span (off)). Results are reported as peak coordinates/tables. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This fMRI study reports within-group, voxelwise task activation contrasts for an executive function task (verbal working memory; Sternberg task). Model was fit over the whole brain and contrasts (high load > low load) are reported at the group level with tables of peak coordinates, satisfying voxelwise whole-brain evidence. The task falls squarely within the working memory domain. Thus all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and include within-group contrasts. NeuroStore entries list whole-brain model fit, within-group contrasts, and coordinate tables of peaks.

This study reports only between-group contrasts (HC > REL) and uses small-volume correction with inference restricted to regions of interest; no within-group (task > baseline or active control) voxelwise activation contrasts are reported for any group. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (only between-group contrasts reported with no within-group task activation contrasts) and E3 (reported results rely on ROI/SVC inference with no voxelwise whole-brain results reported). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function - working memory) and I6 (task falls within executive function domain - working memory). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (no reported whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps for inclusion), I8 (no within-group task contrast reported), and I9 (requires at least one within-group contrast for any group; none presented). Therefore the study is excluded.

This is an fMRI study of response inhibition with whole-brain voxelwise results reported as peak coordinates, so it meets I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (inhibition is an executive function), I7 (model fit over whole brain), and I10 (coordinates reported in tables). However, all extracted analyses are labeled as between-group contrasts or group x condition interactions; no within-group task contrast for any group (e.g., main effect of RED>GREEN within controls or relatives) is reported in the document. Therefore the study violates exclusion criterion E5 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions with no within-group task activation), and does not meet I8 (within-group task contrast). I9 (acceptability of participant groups) also cannot be confirmed as satisfied because its conditional requirement (a within-group contrast for at least one group) is not met. Based on E5, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

The NeuroStore record reports only a voxelwise cross-subject regression of BMI against baseline (passive viewing) metabolism; it does not report any within-group task activation contrast of an executive-function task. This study therefore fails key inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I8, I7) and meets exclusion criterion E5 (only cross-subject/ between-group-style analyses with no within-group task activation). No inclusion criteria are satisfied.

The study reports only connectivity (coherence) analyses (seed-based coherence contrasts Match>Non-Match and Non-Match>Match) rather than task-evoked activation maps. Exclusion criteria met: E4 (reports only connectivity analyses without also reporting a task activation map). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI study), I6 (task within executive function domain: working memory), I8 (reports within-group task contrasts: Match > Non-Match, Non-Match > Match), I9 (provides a participant group). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (no group-level, voxelwise task-evoked statistical map of task activation was reported). Because the meta-analysis objective is pooling task activation maps, and this paper provides only connectivity results, it must be excluded.

This fMRI study explicitly investigates executive working memory using a WM span dual-task and reports multiple within-group contrasts (Read>Control, Remember>Control, Read+Remember>Control). Models were fit and inference performed over the whole brain with voxelwise, multiple-comparisons-corrected results (p<0.05 voxel-level) and peak coordinates reported in tables. These facts satisfy inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (working memory/executive domain), I7 (voxelwise whole-brain results), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (participant groups acceptable), and I10 (results reported in coordinate tables). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical study).

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it is an fMRI study of working memory (N-back) (I5,I6), reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain within-group activation contrasts for controls and patients (Analyses 2 and 3: model fit and inference over whole brain) satisfying whole-brain evidence and within-group contrast requirements (I7,I8). Participant groups include clinical and healthy samples, which is acceptable (I9). Results are reported as peaks/tables and described (reported peaks, Tables tbl1/tbl2), satisfying acceptable reporting formats (I10). No exclusion criteria apply: the paper includes whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps (not only ROI), is not a connectivity-only study, and includes within-group contrasts (so E3–E5 do not apply), and it is an empirical human neuroimaging study (not E6).

This is an fMRI study of working memory (an executive function) using a task-based paradigm, satisfying I5 and I6. The paper reports a group-level, voxelwise analysis with cluster-level correction and peak coordinates in a table (Analysis 17597168_analysis_1 reports group analysis with peaks and multiple-comparison correction), meeting I7 and I10. Within-group contrasts are reported: single-subject (within-subject) analyses for each participant (Analyses 2–4) test WM task after vs before training (interaction within-group), satisfying I8. Any participant group is acceptable (these are healthy adults), so I9 is met. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only (E3), not connectivity/resting-state only (E4), and the paper does not report only between-group contrasts (E5) because within-group contrasts are present. Full text appears accessible via the NeuroStore record, so fulltext_incomplete is false. Therefore the study should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is a task fMRI study of verbal working memory (Sternberg task), which falls within executive function domains (working memory). The NeuroStore record reports multiple group- and within-group voxelwise contrasts: within-group high>low load contrasts for alcoholics and controls (analyses 12948707_analysis_2 and _3) were modeled over the whole brain (voxelwise maps reported in tables), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain, group-level task-evoked statistical maps. Although some ROI/SVC results are reported, the presence of whole-brain, within-group contrasts means the study meets inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria (only-ROI, only-connectivity, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an fMRI lexical-semantic priming (lexical decision) study reporting whole-brain, group-level voxelwise within-group contrasts (semantic > orthographic; orthographic > semantic). However, the task assesses lexical-semantic processing (automatic and strategic semantic priming), not an executive function or cognitive-control task within the review’s defined domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Although the abstract mentions ‘inhibition of competitors’ as a semantic component, the paradigm and contrasts are language/semantic in nature rather than canonical executive-control tasks. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I5 (assesses executive function/cognitive control) and I6 (task within established executive function domains). It does satisfy whole-brain voxelwise reporting and within-group contrasts. Inclusion criteria met: I7, I8, I9, I10. Inclusion criteria not met: I5, I6. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered.

This study reports task-based fMRI of a Sternberg working memory task (executive function domain: working memory), provides whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (model fit over whole brain; reported peak coordinates in MNI), and reports within-group contrasts (four items > one items for encoding and maintenance). Results are reported as peaks/coordinates. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (working memory), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise results), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (participant group acceptable), and I10 (coordinates reported). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group contrasts, empirical imaging data).

This is an fMRI study with whole-brain, within-group voxelwise contrasts reported (peaks in tables) in a sample of n=10, but the task is a simple motor execution (opposing finger tapping) manipulating pacing/temporal modulation. The study does not assess an established executive function domain (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation) in a way that meets the review objective — the focus is on motor execution and temporal regulation rather than cognitive control. Therefore it fails the core content inclusion criteria. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I7 (whole-brain voxelwise results reported), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (participant groups acceptable), I10 (results reported in tables/coordinates). Inclusion IDs not met: I5 (fMRI study assessing executive function/task-based executive assessment — while it is fMRI, it does not assess executive function per review definition), I6 (task does not fall within established executive function domains as operationalized). Full text is complete in the provided record.

The study reports a task-based fMRI working-memory paradigm (working memory span; block design) — satisfying I5 and I6. Model fitting and inference were performed voxelwise across the whole brain (model fit over: whole brain; inference over: whole brain) and peaks are reported (Talairach coordinates, tables), satisfying I7 and I10. Analysis "15221201_analysis_10" reports the main effect contrast DMT > IMT across both groups (a within-task contrast / main effect of condition), which meets I8. Any participant group is acceptable (MDMA users and controls), so I9 is met. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not limited to ROIs/SVC only (E3 false), not only connectivity/resting-state (E4 false), and the paper reports at least one within-group task contrast (so E5 false). Therefore all inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

This PET study used a task-based auditory oddball paradigm (a vigilance/attention executive domain) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group analyses. It includes within-group contrasts for both controls (B>A) and patients (B>A), meeting the requirement for at least one within-group task contrast. Results are reported as peaks/coordinates (table), satisfying whole-brain reporting. Participant groups (healthy and schizophrenia patients) are acceptable per criteria. No exclusion criteria are met: analyses are not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, and within-group contrasts are present (so not only between-group).

This is a task-based fMRI study of sustained attention (Mackworth Clock Test = vigilance), reporting whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses with coordinates (tables) and at least one within-group task contrast (correct detections > baseline). Participants are healthy volunteers (n=10). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5 (fMRI task), I6 (vigilance = executive domain), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise inference), I8 (within-group task contrast), I9 (participant groups acceptable), and I10 (results reported as coordinates/tables). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met.

This fMRI study reports task-based within-group contrasts of executive-function tasks (N-back working memory and visual attention tracking). Whole-brain, voxelwise group analyses are reported (Talairach coordinates, tables of peaks), and several within-group contrasts (e.g., two-back > zero-back; 4 balls > 2 balls) are explicitly listed. Thus it meets: I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function), I6 (working memory and vigilance/visual attention tasks within executive domains), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise results reported), I8 (within-group task contrasts present), I9 (participant groups are reported and acceptable), and I10 (results reported as coordinate tables). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and empirical). Full text is available via the NeuroStore record representation provided, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This study reports task-based fMRI of executive function (Go/No-go inhibition, oddball target detection, response selection), meeting the domain requirement. NeuroStore extraction shows at least one group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analysis (voxelwise random-effects ANOVAs) with whole-brain inference and reported peak coordinates (Analysis 11532888_analysis_4: error > correct, model fit over whole brain, inference over whole brain). The contrast is a within-group task contrast. Results are reported as peaks/tables (Talairach coordinates). Therefore all required inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study reports task-based working memory (an executive function) with group-level, voxelwise random-effects analyses fit over the whole brain and a within-group task contrast (e.g., PLUS > control). Results include reported peak coordinates (Talairach). Methods and contrasts satisfy the meta-analysis requirements (working memory domain, whole-brain voxelwise map, within-group contrast). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and it is empirical).

This fMRI study uses an antisaccade/prosaccade task (inhibition domain) and reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses comparing trials preceded by antisaccades vs prosaccades. It includes within-group contrasts (paired t tests) and reports whole-brain inference (cluster-level, p<0.001) as well as ROI analyses. Thus it meets criteria for task-based fMRI of executive control (I5), an inhibition task (I6), provides at least one whole-brain group-level voxelwise map (I7), reports within-group task contrasts (I8), and participant groups are acceptable (I9). Reporting of peaks/coordinates satisfies I10. No exclusion criteria are met (e.g., the study is not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and not non-empirical).

The study reports task-based fMRI using a verbal Sternberg working memory task (executive function domain). It includes multiple group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (FLAME voxelwise GLM) with reported peak coordinates (tables), satisfying whole-brain reporting. Several within-group contrasts are present (high vs low WM load for children, adolescents, and young adults), meeting the requirement for within-group task contrasts. Results are reported for developmental samples and in tables of coordinates. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, empirical task-activation maps present).

This is an event-related fMRI study using a Categorical N-back (working memory) task (meets I5,I6). Multiple analyses report whole-brain, voxelwise group- and within-group contrasts (Model fit over: whole brain; Analyses 6–8: within-group contrasts correct n-back responses > baseline for young adults, 10-year-olds, and 6-year-olds), with thresholding and tables of peak coordinates (meets I7,I8,I10). Participant groups include developmental samples and adults (meets I9). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and within-group task activations are reported). Therefore the study satisfies all required inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This fMRI study uses task-based, event-related paradigms assessing working memory (an executive function domain) and episodic memory in the same subjects. Group-level, voxelwise (whole-brain) random-effects analyses are reported, with multiple within-group task contrasts (e.g., WM delay, WM encoding, WM recognition, LTM encoding, LTM recognition) and tables of peak coordinates. Thresholding and inference were whole-brain and corrected for multiple comparisons. All required features for inclusion are present: task falls within executive domains (working memory), imaging modality is fMRI, at least one group-level whole-brain voxelwise contrast is reported, and within-group contrasts are explicitly listed. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and it is an empirical human neuroimaging study).

This is an event-related fMRI study of phonological working memory (an executive-function domain). The record reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with cluster-corrected inference and tables of reported peaks for within-group contrasts (e.g., S1 WM > S1 Ctrl, ISI WM > ISI Ctrl, S2 WM > S2 Ctrl). Thus it provides task-evoked, within-group activation maps for a working memory task. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) apply based on the provided document. The study therefore meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI task contrasting semantic vs phonological processing of written word lists (language attention task). Inclusion criteria met: I7 (whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported: semantic>phonological and phonological>semantic), I9 (participant group reported, within-group contrasts present), I10 (whole-brain results reported as coordinate tables). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I5 and I6 — the study does not assess executive function or cognitive control nor does the task fall within established executive function domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation); it is a language/semantic/phonological attention task. No exclusion criteria apply (E3–E6 not met). Therefore the study is excluded because it fails to meet the requirement that the task assesses executive function/cognitive control (I5/I6).

This study must be excluded because it reports only region-of-interest / small-volume-corrected results and only between-group contrasts. Exclusion criteria met: E3 (only ROI/SVC reported) and E5 (only between-group contrasts/interactions reported; no within-group task activation contrast is provided). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI assessing executive function — N-back working memory), I6 (task is within executive function domain — working memory), I9 (participant groups acceptable, developmental/clinical samples allowed), I10 (results reported as coordinates/peaks in a table). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (no clear whole-brain voxelwise task activation map reported — inference was restricted to an ROI with small-volume correction), I8 (no within-group task contrast reported for any group; only an interaction/between-group contrast is listed). Full text appears available in the NeuroStore record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is a task-based fMRI study using an N-back working memory task (executive function). Analyses were fit across the whole brain with voxelwise thresholding and reported peak coordinates. Critically, Analysis 5 reports a within-group contrast of increasing verbal working memory load (one-back vs two-back), fulfilling the requirement for a within-group task activation. Participants are healthy humans. Results are reported as peaks/tables (reported peaks: 9). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group).

The study is a task-based fMRI experiment of verbal working memory (Operation Span), an established executive function domain. It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (model fit over whole brain, cluster-corrected thresholds) and provides within-group task contrasts (Concrete > Abstract and simple effects with reported peaks/tables). Results are reported as coordinates/peaks and tables. Participants are a within-group healthy cohort (n=12). Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical).

This is an fMRI study of an auditory N-back working memory task (meets I5 and I6). Participants and results are group-level and coordinates are reported (meets I9 and I10). However, all reported statistical inference is restricted to region-of-interest small-volume-corrected results (Inference restricted to ROI; SVC voxel-level), and no whole-brain voxelwise task-activation map (task vs baseline) is reported—so the study effectively provides only ROI/SVC results (meets exclusion E3). Furthermore, the reported contrasts are light-condition by session interaction effects rather than a within-group task activation contrast (fails I8). Because I7 and I8 are not satisfied and E3 applies, the study must be excluded.

This paper is a meta-analysis/methods study (coordinate-/image-based meta-analytic approach) rather than an original human fMRI/PET empirical study. Exclusion E6 applies: a non-empirical meta-analysis/methods paper without original participant neuroimaging data.
