Inclusion criteria met: I6 (task domain = verbal working memory, an executive function). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (not an original fMRI/PET study reporting primary empirical data), I7 (no group-level, voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps from an original study), I8 (no within-group task contrast reported from original participant data), I9 (no participant group-level data reported as original results), I10 (while coordinates are reported for the meta-analysis, these are secondary/meta-analytic peaks, not primary whole-brain group maps). Fulltext is complete for decision-making (no access issues). Given E6, the study must be excluded from the review.

This fMRI study explicitly investigates the role of articulatory rehearsal (a subcomponent of verbal working memory) in sentence comprehension and includes task conditions manipulating articulatory rehearsal (speech articulation vs finger-tapping). NeuroStore reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (model fit over: whole brain; coordinate space: Talairach) with within-group task contrasts (e.g., object-relative > subject-relative; contrasts during concurrent tasks), and tables of peak coordinates (17 peaks reported). The study therefore (1) is an fMRI task-based study addressing an executive function domain (working memory), (2) provides whole-brain voxelwise results, (3) reports within-group contrasts, and (4) reports coordinates. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met. Based on the provided document, all required inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10) are satisfied, so the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This is an event-related fMRI study of working memory and distraction (executive function domain). The NeuroStore record shows whole-brain model fitting and whole-brain inference (Gaussian random field correction) and reports group-level voxelwise contrasts with peak coordinates in tables. Multiple within-group task contrasts are reported for adults and for children (cue, delay, distraction, selection), satisfying the requirement for at least one within-group voxelwise activation map. Results are reported in tables of peaks. Therefore inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 and I10 are met. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and empirical human fMRI data are reported).

The study is excluded because it reports only between-group contrasts (SZ > Con interaction) and does not report any within-group task activation contrasts for any group, which violates exclusion criterion E5. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (working memory task — N-back), I7 (group-level voxelwise models were fit over the whole brain), I9 (clinical participant group allowed), I10 (results reported as peak coordinates in tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I8 (no within-group task contrast reported). Although models were fit over the whole brain, inference was restricted to regions of interest with small-volume correction; however the decisive reason for exclusion is E5: only between-group contrasts / group x condition interactions are reported with no within-group contrasts.

This is an fMRI task-based study of cognitive control/task selection (task switching) reporting whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise contrasts. NeuroStore shows a random-effects one-sample t-test on participant contrast maps (n=16) comparing informative (congruent+incongruent) vs neutral conditions, reported in Talairach space with thresholded peaks and corrected voxelwise inference. Thus it satisfies fMRI task-based executive function (I5), falls within executive domains (cognitive control/flexibility, I6), provides whole-brain voxelwise results (I7), includes a within-group task contrast (I8), any participant group is acceptable (I9), and coordinates/peaks are reported (I10). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Full text is available via the NeuroStore record; fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of visual working memory and attention (executive-domain WM). It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (model fit and inference over whole brain; voxel-level FDR q<0.05) and multiple within-group task contrasts (analyses labelled omnibus within-group and specific within-group contrasts). Results are reported as coordinate peaks (tables). Participants are healthy adults (n=18). These elements satisfy all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study manipulating working memory load (an established executive function domain) and examining neural responses. Analyses were whole-brain, third-level group (subjects as random factor) voxelwise GLMs with cluster-corrected thresholds and reported peak coordinates/tables. The paper reports within-group task contrasts (e.g., main effect of load, low>unprimed; and within-group cross-subject regression), meeting the requirement for a within-group task contrast. Participants are an adult sample. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and empirical human neuroimaging data are reported).

This fMRI study uses a working memory task (meets I5, I6) and reports a within-group contrast (correct > incorrect) (meets I8) in a healthy sample (meets I9). However, all task-evoked activation results are reported only within pre-defined ROIs (Analysis 1: ROI-level, p<0.05), and the only whole-brain voxelwise analysis reported is a PPI connectivity analysis (Analysis 0), not a task-evoked voxelwise activation map. Therefore the study does not provide a group-level, voxelwise task activation map (violating I7) and effectively reports only connectivity/ROI activation rather than whole-brain task activations, so exclusion criterion E4 applies. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I8, I9. Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise task activation reported). Full text appears complete for screening.

The study reports a task-based fMRI experiment of working memory (verbal/sign rehearsal) in deaf participants, satisfying executive-function domain criteria. It includes a group-level, voxelwise within-group contrast (perception vs covert rehearsal intersection) with whole-brain model fit and whole-brain inference, and reports peak coordinates (Table tbl1). Therefore it meets I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study using an N-back working memory paradigm (executive function domain). Whole-brain, voxelwise group analyses are reported (model fit over whole brain; coordinates/peaks in tables). Multiple within-group task contrasts are presented (working memory vs reference conditions and conjunction analyses). Participants are healthy adults (but any sample would be acceptable). Results are reported as voxelwise peaks/tables. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) and none of the exclusion criteria (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, or between-group-only analyses; it is empirical).

This fMRI study examines a visuospatial working memory task (executive function domain) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise, group-level task activation maps (VSWM > CTL) tested with one-sample t-tests. NeuroStore extraction shows model fit and inference over the whole brain with voxelwise thresholding and cluster correction, and coordinates/tables of peaks are provided. Thus all inclusion criteria are met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (working memory), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise results), I8 (within-group task contrast), I9 (participant group reported), and I10 (results reported as coordinates/tables). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, not non-empirical). fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study is an empirical fMRI experiment using the Stroop Color-Word Task, a canonical inhibition/executive-control paradigm. It reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses (model fit over whole brain; Talairach coordinates) and explicitly includes a within-group contrast (Stroop > Neutral). Results are reported as voxelwise peaks (Table) and voxel-level thresholding. Participants are healthy adults (n=14). Thus it meets inclusion criteria I5 (fMRI task-based executive function), I6 (task within executive domain: inhibition), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise group analysis), I8 (within-group task contrast), I9 (participant group acceptable), and I10 (coordinates/tables reporting). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text is available in the provided NeuroStore record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an fMRI task-based study using an N-back working memory paradigm (verbal and spatial) in healthy participants. Group-level, voxelwise (whole-brain) analyses are reported with corrected cluster-level inference and Talairach coordinates (Table peaks). A within-group task contrast is reported (verbal > spatial; interaction within-group, 2-back vs 0-back), satisfying the requirement for a within-group task contrast. Results are reported as coordinates, which is acceptable. No exclusion criteria are met: the paper is not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and not exclusively between-group contrasts. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an fMRI task-based study using a Go/No-Go inhibition paradigm (I5,I6). It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (Analysis 19120444_analysis_0: model fit over whole brain; cluster-corrected threshold, reported peaks), providing a within-group task contrast (cue periods prior to successful inhibitions; simple effect within-group) meeting I7 and I8. Participant sample is acceptable (n=15 adults) so I9 met. Results are reported as peaks/coordinates, meeting I10. No exclusion criteria apply: not ROI-only (E3), not connectivity-only (E4), not only between-group contrasts (E5), and it is empirical (E6). Therefore all inclusion criteria I5-I10 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

The paper reports task-based fMRI of verbal working memory (an executive function) using within-subject WM vs control contrasts (auditory and visual). Analyses are whole-brain, voxelwise, random-effects GLM with cluster-level multiple-comparison correction and reported peak coordinates (table). These features satisfy the review’s requirements for executive-function task activation, whole-brain voxelwise group contrasts, and within-group contrasts. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Sample (n=14) is acceptable per criteria. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

The study reports task-based fMRI of an executive function (auditory N-back working memory) in humans (MS patients and controls). It provides group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (model fit over: whole brain) using one-sample t-tests for within-group two-back activation in both controls (n=10) and MS patients (n=17), with peak coordinates reported in a table. Thus it meets I5 (fMRI task), I6 (working memory domain), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise group analyses), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (participant group acceptable), and I10 (results reported as coordinates/table). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group contrasts, empirical data). Full text appears complete in the NeuroStore record. Inclusion criteria applied and exclusions are encoded below.

This fMRI study includes task-based executive function paradigms (working memory; visual attention) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level maps. NeuroStore shows within-group, task contrasts for working memory, visual attention, and episodic retrieval (analyses 15028641_analysis_0–2), satisfying the requirement for at least one within-group task contrast. Model fit was over the whole brain and voxelwise results/peak coordinates are reported (Tables), meeting whole-brain evidence requirements. Participant groups are acceptable per inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and the paper reports within-group activation contrasts (so it is not limited to between-group contrasts). Therefore all applicable inclusion criteria are met (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10) and no exclusion criteria are met.

This fMRI study examines working memory (Delayed Match-to-Sample), an executive function domain, using task-based, event-related design. NeuroStore extraction reports whole-brain voxelwise model fitting and voxel-level inference with reported peaks (Tables) for within-group contrasts (cue, delay, probe periods), meeting group-level task activation requirements. Participants are healthy adults (n=10). Results are reported in MNI coordinates. All required inclusion criteria are satisfied (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical).

The study reports an event-related fMRI investigation of planning (Tower of Hanoi), which falls within executive function domains. It provides group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (voxel-wise regression model; model fit over: whole brain) and reports within-group task contrasts (parametric modulation, within-group) with peak coordinates in tables. Results are BOLD task-evoked activations reported in Talairach coordinates. Thresholding and cluster criteria are specified. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) and no exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group, not non-empirical).

This study reports an empirical task-based fMRI experiment of working memory (Sternberg task) with a group-level, voxelwise within-group contrast assessing load sensitivity (Forward 5 > Forward 2). The analysis was performed over the whole brain and reports peak coordinates; thresholding is voxelwise (p<0.001). These elements satisfy the meta-analysis requirements for executive-function task activations. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group contrasts, and is empirical). The document appears complete for screening purposes.

This study reports task-based event-related fMRI of a working memory task (executive function domain), meeting I5 and I6. Multiple group-level, whole-brain voxelwise second-level analyses are reported (Model fit over: whole brain; second-level ANOVA), satisfying I7. The NeuroStore record includes analyses labelled for individual groups (healthy controls, schizophrenia, depression) with reported peaks, indicating within-group task contrasts are present (I8). Any participant group is acceptable (clinical samples present), fulfilling I9. Results are reported as voxelwise peaks/tables, acceptable per I10. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only (E3), not connectivity-only (E4), and not exclusively between-group contrasts (E5) since within-group contrasts are reported. Therefore the paper should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

The study reports original human fMRI data using executive-function tasks (N-back = working memory, Go/No-go = inhibition) and analyzes GLM-derived activation results from those tasks. The abstract explicitly states group-level activation results were extracted and compared (thresholded cluster size and maximum t) across motion-correction methods, which implies voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps. Thus inclusion criteria are met: I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function), I6 (tasks are within established executive domains: working memory and inhibition), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise analyses implied by GLM-derived activation maps and cluster/t-value comparisons), I8 (within-group task contrasts/main effects of task against baseline are reported), I9 (participant group acceptable—40 human subjects), and I10 (results reported in text/tables). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and not non-empirical). Confidence is moderate (0.75) because the NeuroStore extraction explicitly lists only phantom analyses, but the abstract clearly describes human group-level activation analyses.

This is an fMRI task-based study of working memory (n-back), which is an executive function domain. The NeuroStore record reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain second-level analyses for within-group task contrasts (2-back>0-back and 1-back>0-back) with voxelwise FWE correction and reported peak coordinates (Tables). Participants are healthy (n=49). Although some genotype interaction analyses used SVC/ROI, the study nevertheless provides qualifying whole-brain within-group contrasts reported voxelwise. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study examines working memory manipulation (an executive function) using task-based contrasts. It reports within-group task contrasts (manipulation > maintenance) for younger and older groups (analyses 0 and 1), satisfying I8, and a whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analysis (analysis 2), satisfying I7. Task and domain meet I5 and I6; participants are acceptable per I9. Results are reported as coordinate peaks (Table tbl1), meeting I10. No exclusion criteria are met: ROI-only reporting is not limiting because a whole-brain voxelwise analysis is present (E3 not met); connectivity-only or between-group-only exclusions do not apply. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

The NeuroStore record reports only omnibus between-group contrasts (patient vs control; group x condition terms) with no within-group task activation contrasts for any group. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of executive/context processing), I6 (task falls within executive domains: context processing/working memory/vigilance), I7 (voxelwise whole-brain analyses reported), I9 (participant groups acceptable), I10 (results reported as peak coordinates in tables). Inclusion criterion not met: I8 (no within-group task contrast reported). Exclusion criterion met: E5 (only between-group contrasts reported). Full text is available in the NeuroStore-derived record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The NeuroStore record indicates this is an fMRI working-memory study (meets I5 and I6) but the reported analyses are region-of-interest / region-level only and the extracted contrasts are between-group (High vs Low anxiety) and interactions. Exclusion criteria met: E3 (only ROI/region-level analyses with no voxelwise whole-brain task activation map reported) and E5 (only between-group contrasts/interactions are reported with no within-group task activation contrast available in the document). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI) and I6 (working memory task). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (no group-level voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked map reported) and I8 (no within-group task contrast reported for any group). Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI task study of working memory updating (executive function). It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (Analysis 17239618_analysis_1 and _2: whole-brain model fit and whole-brain inference with FDR-corrected voxelwise thresholds), and within-group task contrasts including a delay-period main effect and a parametric modulation of updating load. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (task-based fMRI, working memory domain, whole-brain voxelwise results, within-group contrasts, and acceptable reporting). Although one analysis is ROI-based (analysis_0), at least one qualifying whole-brain voxelwise result is present. Full text is available via the NeuroStore record provided, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

This study reports an event-related fMRI experiment using a working memory task (faces), which falls within executive function domains (working memory). It provides group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (model fit and inference over whole brain) with reported peak coordinates (Table), and reports a within-group task contrast (early > late). Participant sample is reported (n=10). Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria and does not meet any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-groups-only, and is empirical).

Study uses task-based fMRI (BOLD) of an inhibition executive-function task (Go/No-Go), meeting I5 and I6. Multiple group-level, voxelwise, whole-brain analyses are reported (no-go > go, go > no-go, parametric modulation) satisfying I7. At least one within-group task contrast is reported for groups (several no-go > go and go > no-go within-group contrasts), satisfying I8 and I9. Results are reported as peak coordinates/tables and ROI analyses are supplemental, so presentation of whole-brain voxelwise results in tables/figures meets I10. Although some between-group ROI analyses are present, the paper includes whole-brain within-group contrasts and voxelwise results, so no exclusion criteria are triggered (E3–E6 not met). Therefore the study should be included for the meta-analysis of executive-function task activations.

This study reports task-based fMRI of an antisaccade task (a response-inhibition executive function), with group-level, voxelwise whole-brain contrasts (antisaccade > rest) reported for within-group analyses in both healthy controls and schizophrenia patients (coordinate peaks in tables). Thus it meets the review’s requirements for fMRI/PET task activation, executive-function domain (inhibition), whole-brain voxelwise analysis, and within-group contrasts. No exclusion criteria are triggered (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and includes within-group contrasts).

This is an event-related fMRI study of working memory (executive function) that reports group-level within-group task contrasts with voxelwise model fitting over the whole brain and voxel-level thresholding; peaks are reported in tables. It assesses working memory (I5,I6), includes group-level voxelwise analyses (model fit over whole brain) and within-group simple-effect contrasts (I7,I8). Participants are healthy adults (I9). Results are reported as coordinate peaks/tables (I10). Although inference is described as restricted to ROIs, the model was fit voxelwise across the whole brain and voxel-level corrected peaks are reported, so this does not appear to be ROI-only reporting. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and within-group contrasts are present).

The NeuroStore record reports only between-group contrasts (Control > Schizophrenia; Schizophrenia > Control) and does not present any within-group task activation contrast for either group. Inclusion criteria I5 (fMRI task-based), I6 (working memory task), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise analysis), and I10 (results reported as coordinates/tables) are satisfied. However, I8 (at least one within-group task contrast) and I9 (within-group contrast for at least one group) are not met. This violates exclusion criterion E5 (studies that report ONLY between-group contrasts with no within-group task activation). Therefore the study must be excluded.

The study reports task-based fMRI of working memory (Sternberg task) in schizophrenia with voxelwise whole-brain model fits and at least one within-group contrast (5t > Arrows) reported as peak coordinates (Table 4). The task falls squarely within executive function (working memory). Whole-brain inference is reported (inference restricted to a priori DLPFC regions and whole brain) and voxel-level multiple-comparison correction is described. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text is available via the NeuroStore-derived record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study reports a task-based fMRI experiment probing initiation and inhibition (explicitly listed among acceptable executive domains). It provides a group-level, voxelwise within-group contrast (whole-brain model fit and whole-brain inference) comparing movement conditions, with reported peak coordinates (Talairach), satisfying requirements for whole-brain evidence. Tasks map onto executive domains (inhibition and initiation). Participants are a within-group sample (n=21). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Therefore all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study reports only seed-based functional connectivity analyses during the PASAT (left BA45/46 seed) and does not report any within-group voxelwise task-evoked activation contrast. Exclusion criterion E4 applies (connectivity-only study without a task activation map). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function), I6 (task = working memory/PASAT), I9 (participant groups include clinical and healthy; within-group analyses are reported but as connectivity). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked activation map reported), I8 (no within-group task contrast of activation vs baseline reported). Therefore the study must be excluded.

The study reports task-based fMRI BOLD data using a working memory paradigm (Delayed Match-to-Sample/Sternberg), which falls within executive function domains. Multiple group-level, voxelwise within-group contrasts are reported (2nd-level one-sample t-tests) with whole-brain model fitting and reported peak coordinates/tables. Thus it provides whole-brain task-evoked activation maps and within-group contrasts for at least one participant group. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not limited to ROIs, connectivity-only analyses, or between-group contrasts, and the study is empirical. Therefore all inclusion criteria relevant to the meta-analysis are satisfied.

This PET study uses an auditory Continuous Performance Task (vigilance) and reports seed-based whole-brain connectivity (between-group comparisons of metabolic correlations) rather than task-evoked activation contrasts. Inclusion met: I5 (PET task-based study), I6 (task within executive domain: vigilance). Inclusion not met: I7 (no group-level voxelwise task-evoked activation map reported), I8 (no within-group task contrast reported for any group), I9 (conditional within-group contrast requirement not satisfied). Exclusion criteria met: E4 (reports only connectivity analyses without a task activation map) and E5 (reports only between-group connectivity contrasts with no within-group task activation contrast). Therefore the study does not provide the within-group, voxelwise task activation maps required for the meta-analysis and must be excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task-based paradigm (Wisconsin Card Sorting Task) that probes executive functions (set-shifting and inhibition). NeuroStore reports a group-level, whole-brain random-effects GLM with a within-group contrast (inhibition > control) and reported peak coordinates (Talairach). The analysis is voxelwise (model fit over whole brain) and thus provides whole-brain task-evoked statistical results. Participants (n=36) are a valid participant group. Therefore all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study used a Sternberg verbal working memory task (an executive function domain) and reports multiple group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (model fit over: whole brain) with voxel-level thresholding and tables of coordinate peaks. Several within-group task contrasts are reported (e.g., load 6 > 2). Participants are healthy adults (n=16). Results are reported as coordinate peaks and meet the requirement for whole-brain, within-group task activation maps. No exclusion criteria apply.

Exclusion E5 applies: the NeuroStore extraction lists only between-group contrasts and group x condition interactions (voxel-wise ANOVAs and between-group contrasts such as SCZ>CON, SCZ=SCZ sibs>CON, etc.) and does not report any within-group task activation contrast (e.g., WM>fixation or WM>baseline) for any participant group. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (working memory task = n-back), I7 (group-level voxelwise analyses reported across the whole brain). Inclusion criteria not met: I8 (no within-group task contrast reported), I9 (conditional on I8 — a within-group contrast for at least one group is required but absent). Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis. Full text is complete in the provided record (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an empirical PET study using a task-based paradigm of sustained attention (vigilance), which falls within executive function domains. The study reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (model fit over whole brain; voxel-level thresholding reported) and provides within-group task contrasts for both patients and controls (multiple within-group contrasts listed). Results are reported as peak coordinates/tables. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and it is empirical).

This is an event-related fMRI study using a Go/No-Go task (inhibition), an established executive-function domain. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (model fit and inference over whole brain) with voxelwise multiple-comparison correction and reports peak coordinates for within-group contrasts (Errors of commission, Correct rejects, Correct hits, and Errors>Correct rejects). These satisfy the requirements for a task-based executive-function fMRI study with within-group voxelwise results reported. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met.

The study reports an fMRI within-group 2-back > 0-back contrast (working memory) but the reported analysis is ROI-only (model fit over: region of interest; left planum temporale). No whole-brain voxelwise group-level activation map is provided, so it fails the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise results. Exclusion based on E3 (ROI-only reporting).

This fMRI study uses a Sternberg working memory task (executive function: working memory) and reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses with voxelwise FDR thresholding and tables of coordinates. Multiple within-group contrasts are reported (WM task > sensorimotor control; main effects of load and delay; load contrasts), analyzed with one-sample t-tests and random-effects ANOVA on n=17 healthy participants. Results are voxelwise and whole-brain (not ROI-only), and coordinates/peaks are provided in tables. These features satisfy inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Hence the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This study reports task-based fMRI of cognitive flexibility (task-switching) in OCD and controls, meeting the meta-analysis objective. It includes whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (model fit over whole brain) and reports peaks; it also contains within-group task contrasts (control: task-switch > task-repeat; patients: task-repeat > task-switch). Tasks fall within executive function (cognitive flexibility). Thus all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study used a verbal working memory (Sternberg) task—a validated executive function domain—acquired BOLD data and reports a group-level, voxelwise t-map fit over the whole brain (Model fit over: whole brain; Inference over: whole brain; coordinate space MNI-305; reported peaks). The reported contrast (NT > CT) is a task contrast reported for the combined participant sample (i.e., a within-group/group-level task activation), satisfying the requirement for a within-group task contrast. Results are reported as voxelwise peaks/t-map (Table tbl2). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 and is eligible for inclusion.

This fMRI study investigates a working memory task (an executive function domain) using task-based, event-related fMRI in healthy volunteers. The NeuroStore record reports group-level, voxelwise (whole-brain) statistical maps and multiple within-group task contrasts (e.g., manipulation vs maintenance; high vs low load), with peak coordinates reported in tables. Partial ROI analyses are present but not exclusive. Participants are human healthy adults and results are reported as whole-brain coordinates/tables. These elements satisfy all inclusion criteria (I5–I10). No exclusion criteria are triggered: the study does not report only ROI/small-volume results (E3), nor only connectivity/resting-state analyses (E4), nor only between-group contrasts without within-group effects (E5), and it is empirical (not E6). Full text appears sufficiently represented in the NeuroStore record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study reports task-based fMRI of an executive function (working memory N-back) and includes at least one within-group, voxelwise whole-brain task contrast (analysis 17448450_analysis_6: 2-back > 0-back for all 21 participants, whole-brain model fit, FDR-corrected voxelwise results). Thus it meets inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (working memory), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise results), I8 (within-group task contrast), I9 (participant group acceptable), and I10 (results reported in tables/peaks). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and empirical).

This is an fMRI Go/No-Go task (inhibition), meeting executive-function domain criteria (I5,I6). The NeuroStore record reports at least one group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analysis (Analysis 14568507_analysis_2: paired t test, model fit over whole brain, cluster-level inference, reported peaks), satisfying whole-brain evidence (I7) and providing a within-group task contrast (Time1 > Time2 paired within-subject contrast) (I8). Participant groups are acceptable (healthy older and younger adults) (I9). Results include reported coordinate tables/peaks (tables 3–4), consistent with acceptable reporting formats (I10). Although several analyses used ROI-based thresholding, the presence of the whole-brain, voxelwise within-group contrast prevents exclusion under E3/E5. Therefore the study meets all applicable inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

This PET study reports task-based activations for the central executive component of working memory (an executive function domain). It includes group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses with reported coordinates/peaks for within-group contrasts (main effects of manipulation and storage and specific task contrasts), satisfying the requirement for within-group task activation maps. The methods indicate whole-brain model fitting and voxel-level thresholding; results are reported as peaks/tables. Participants are healthy humans and a within-group contrast is presented. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and not non-empirical). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This study should be excluded. It reports an fMRI N-back working-memory task (satisfies I5 and I6) and includes clinical and healthy groups (I9). However, the reported analysis is a between-group interaction/contrast (siblings 2-back > comparison 0-back) and the model was fit within a region-of-interest (dorsolateral prefrontal cortex) rather than as a whole-brain voxelwise analysis. Therefore it does not provide a within-group task activation contrast (violates I8) and does not provide whole-brain voxelwise results (violates I7). Exclusion criteria met: E3 (ROI-only analyses with no voxelwise whole-brain results) and E5 (only between-group contrasts/group x condition interaction with no within-group task contrast). Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I9. Inclusion criteria not met: I7, I8.

The study reports an fMRI N-back working memory task (executive function) with a group-level, voxelwise within-group task contrast (2-back > 1-back) analyzed across the whole brain (voxelwise FDR threshold). Participants are healthy (n=29). These facts satisfy inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (working memory), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise results), I8 (within-group task contrast), I9 (participant groups acceptable), and I10 (results reported as peaks). Although the paper also reports an ROI-restricted connectivity conjunction, this does not exclude the study because a qualifying whole-brain activation map is present. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears sufficiently represented in the document.

This study reports task-based fMRI of an executive function (set-shift/hypothesis generation) in healthy adults, using within-group contrasts and group-level voxelwise GLMs. Model fit was performed over the whole brain and multiple within-group task contrasts are reported (Match Problems > baseline; Successful > Unsuccessful; parametric modulation), with peaks tabulated (Table 1) and thresholding described (voxelwise FDR p<0.05). Although inference is noted as restricted to regions of interest, the model was estimated voxelwise across the whole brain and coordinate peaks are reported, so the study provides voxelwise task-evoked activation maps rather than only ROI results. Thus it satisfies I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 and I10 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the executive-function activation meta-analysis. It used event-related fMRI during a verbal working memory task (I5,I6), reports voxelwise whole-brain analyses (model fit over whole brain; voxel-level thresholding reported) and peak coordinates (I7,I10), and includes a within-group contrast testing changes over time in patients (paired/session contrast, within-group interaction) satisfying the requirement for a within-group task contrast (I8). Participants are a clinical sample (schizophrenia), which is acceptable (I9). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and not only between-group contrasts. The documented analysis (paired t-test, BOLD response, whole-brain voxelwise inference) supports inclusion.

This study is excluded because it reports only region-of-interest functional connectivity (beta-series correlation) analyses and does not provide any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked activation maps. Exclusion criteria met: E3 (only ROI/small-volume analyses with no voxelwise results) and E4 (only connectivity analyses without a task activation map). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (task is working memory, an executive-function domain), I8 (reports within-group contrasts), and I9 (participant group reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (no whole-brain, voxelwise task activation map reported). Because at least one exclusion criterion (E3 and E4) is met and the required whole-brain evidence (I7) is absent, the study does not meet the review’s eligibility requirements.

This is an empirical PET study of working memory (an executive function) with within-subject drug/placebo manipulations. The record reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (WM > sensorimotor control) with peaks reported (Analyses 0 and 1), satisfying requirements for task-evoked voxelwise maps. The task is a parametrically varied working memory span task, meeting the executive domain. At least one within-group task contrast is reported. Participant sample (n=10 healthy adults) is acceptable. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and not only between-group contrasts. The study therefore meets all inclusion criteria required for the meta-analysis.

All reported analyses are task-based within-group fMRI contrasts of the Wisconsin Card Sorting Task (I5, I6, I8, I9, I10 satisfied). However, NeuroStore indicates that although the model was fit over the whole brain, inference was restricted to a region of interest for the reported contrasts (inference restricted to: region of interest) and only ROI-restricted peaks are reported. This indicates the paper reports only ROI/small-volume-corrected voxelwise inference rather than whole-brain voxelwise results, violating the requirement for whole-brain evidence (I7). Therefore E3 applies and the study is excluded.

This fMRI study used task-based auditory working memory comparisons (pseudowords and tones), which fall within the executive function domain (working memory). It reports voxelwise whole-brain group- and within-group contrasts with coordinates/peak tables, satisfying requirements for whole-brain, voxelwise task activation maps and within-group contrasts. Participant groups include both clinical (developmental phonological dyslexia) and control samples, which is acceptable. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and within-group contrasts are reported). Therefore all inclusion criteria for this review are met (see inclusion_criteria_applied).

This is an event-related fMRI study of working memory (executive function) using a task-based paradigm (mental arithmetic with integration/segregation of a WM preload). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise random-effects GLM analyses are reported (model fit and inference over whole brain) with within-group task contrasts (e.g., IN > SG, SG > IN, IN;SG > MO;RO). Results are reported as peak coordinates/tables. Thus all inclusion criteria are met (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10). No exclusion criteria apply: analyses are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and include within-group contrasts (so E3–E6 do not apply). Full text appears available in the provided NeuroStore record.

The study reports task-based fMRI of working memory for faces (an executive function domain), with whole-brain, voxelwise group-level contrasts and within-group task contrasts. Specifically: (1) It is an fMRI task study of working memory (I5, I6). (2) Model fit was performed over the whole brain with voxelwise thresholding and reported peak coordinates (I7, I10). (3) It includes within-group contrasts (WM maintenance > ITI; subsequent memory contrasts) at the group level (I8). (4) Participants are healthy adults but any participant group qualifies (I9). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not limited to ROIs or connectivity-only analyses, and within-group voxelwise activations are reported. Therefore the study meets all specified inclusion criteria and violates none.

This is an fMRI study using a 1-back working memory task (an established executive function domain). The NeuroStore record reports voxelwise, whole-brain, group-level mixed-effects GLM analyses and reports coordinates/tables for within-group task contrasts (e.g., category > location for younger and older groups). Therefore it provides whole-brain, within-group task activation maps and meets the meta-analysis objective of pooling executive-function task activations across participant groups.

This is an fMRI task-based study of working memory (delayed matching-to-sample), which falls within executive function domains. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group analyses (model fit and inference over whole brain) with within-group task contrasts (e.g., correct recognition > fixation; 12,000 ms > simultaneous), and peaks/tables are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and it is empirical). Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and the study should be included.

This fMRI task-switching study assesses cognitive flexibility (meets I5 and I6), reports a within-group contrast (switch > repeat; meets I8) and uses a healthy participant group (meets I9). However, NeuroStore shows the primary reported analysis was fit and thresholded over regions of interest (Model fit over: region of interest; Thresholding: region-level) with peaks reported from ROIs. No group-level voxelwise/whole-brain task activation map is reported. Therefore it violates exclusion E3 (only ROI/SVC analyses with no voxelwise results) and does not meet inclusion I7 (requires at least one group-level voxelwise task-evoked map). Conclusion: EXCLUDED due to E3; included criteria met: I5, I6, I8, I9; inclusion not met: I7.

The study reports task-based fMRI working memory within-group contrasts (faces, houses, spatial vs object delays), meeting inclusion for fMRI executive-task (I5), executive domain (working memory) (I6), presence of within-group contrasts (I8), and qualifying participant groups (I9). However, NeuroStore indicates that model fitting and statistical inference were confined to regions of interest ("Model fit over: region of interest"; "Inference restricted to: region of interest") for all reported analyses, i.e. no voxelwise whole-brain task activation maps are provided. This fails inclusion criterion I7 (whole-brain voxelwise evidence) and meets exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI/small-volume-corrected analyses reported). Therefore the study is excluded.

This is an event-related fMRI task study with voxelwise whole-brain group contrasts (satisfies I5, I7, I8, I9, I10). However the task manipulates spatial orienting/attention (endogenous vs exogenous cueing), which does not fall within the review's required executive function domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I6 and must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I7, I8, I9, I10. Inclusion criterion not met: I6. Exclusion criteria met: none.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation manipulating working memory load (distance) within sentence comprehension and explicitly tests working memory effects (an executive function) in Broca's area. It reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (model fit over whole brain; reported peak tables) and includes within-group contrasts (parametric modulation and BIND>MOV, MOV>BIND contrasts). Reporting of coordinates/peaks satisfies reporting requirements. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Therefore it meets the review’s inclusion criteria for executive function task activations.

This study reports a task-based fMRI investigation of working memory (Sternberg paradigm), which is an executive function domain. It includes a group-level, voxelwise whole-brain contrast (negative trials > positive trials) with model fit and inference over the whole brain and reports Talairach coordinates/peaks. The contrast is a within-group task comparison. Participants are a healthy sample (n=8), which is acceptable per criteria. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Therefore it satisfies I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 and should be included.

This fMRI study reports a within-group, voxelwise task contrast (2-back > 0-back) of a working memory (executive function) task in healthy participants, with model fit and inference conducted over the whole brain and peaks reported. These elements satisfy the review’s requirements for task-based executive-function fMRI, whole-brain group-level voxelwise results, and a within-group contrast. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and not only between-group contrasts).

The NeuroStore record describes an fMRI dual-task executive-control study with whole-brain, voxelwise Time x Group x Condition interaction results (cluster-corrected). However, the document only reports a between-group interaction contrast (posttraining: training > pretraining; control) and does not report any within-group task activation contrasts for either group. Thus it fails inclusion criterion I8 and meets exclusion criterion E5. Other inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function), I6 (task is dual-task/divided attention, an executive domain), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise analysis and inference), I9 (participant sample acceptable), and I10 (whole-brain results reported as coordinates). No ROI-only or connectivity-only exclusion criteria apply. Full text is complete as represented in the NeuroStore record.

This study reports task-based fMRI whole-brain, voxelwise within-group contrasts that probe executive function (working memory). Specifically, the n-back analysis (2-back > 0-back) is a within-group, whole-brain, voxelwise GLM contrast using BOLD fMRI and reports peak coordinates. The analysis meets the meta-analysis objective of executive function activations. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Therefore the study should be included.

The study is excluded because it reports only region-of-interest (ROI) voxelwise model fitting (Model fit over: region of interest) and the extracted analyses are exclusively between-group contrasts (omnibus and group comparisons: HP>SZ, RL>SZ) with no within-group task activation contrast reported. Exclusion criteria met: E3 (ROI-only analyses with no voxelwise whole-brain results) and E5 (only between-group contrasts, no within-group task contrast). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function: antisaccade/ODR tasks), I6 (tasks fall under executive domains: inhibition/working memory), and I9 (participant groups include clinical samples; within-group contrasts in such groups would qualify but none are reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise group-level task maps reported; model was fit over ROI), I8 (no within-group task contrast reported for any group). fulltext_incomplete=false.

This fMRI study uses an N-back working memory task (executive function domain) and reports within-group, voxelwise group-level contrasts (e.g., two-back > one-back) with whole-brain model fitting and whole-brain inference for several analyses (Analysis 0 and 1). Peaks are reported in tables. Therefore it satisfies: I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function), I6 (working memory), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise group analyses), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (participant group acceptable), and I10 (coordinates/peaks reported). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains within-group contrasts, empirical). Full text is complete for screening purposes.

This is an empirical PET study that tests inhibitory control and movement selection—domains of executive function (inhibition/selection). It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (model fit and inference over whole brain, cluster-level thresholding) with within-group contrasts (index-finger vs full-hand; rest vs movements), and peak coordinates are reported in tables. Participants are healthy adults (n=10). Therefore it satisfies task modality (PET), executive domain, whole-brain voxelwise results, within-group contrasts, and reporting of coordinates.

The study used PET to measure cerebral blood flow during the Stroop Color-Word Task (an inhibition executive-function task). It reports whole-brain, voxelwise, group-level analyses (voxel-by-voxel t-tests; model fit and inference over the whole brain) and includes within-group task contrasts (incongruent > congruent) for both healthy controls (n=46) and depressed patients (n=41). Results are reported as peak coordinates. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I5 (PET task-based study), I6 (task within executive function - inhibition), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise evidence), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (participant groups acceptable), and I10 (results clearly described as coordinates). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an event-related fMRI study of task switching (an executive function: cognitive flexibility) that reports a within-group, voxelwise contrast (task switch > task repetition) with whole-brain model fitting and reported peak coordinates (n=16). The analysis meets requirements for task-based fMRI (I5), an established executive domain (I6), whole-brain voxelwise results (I7), a within-group task contrast (I8), and permissive participant inclusion (I9). Results are reported as peaks in a table (I10). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and this is empirical human neuroimaging data. Full text is available in the provided record. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This fMRI study reports event-related, task-based activations for a spatial working memory task (an executive function domain). It includes group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (model fit over whole brain; second-level random-effects analysis reported with voxelwise threshold p<0.001 and tables of peak coordinates). Several within-group contrasts are reported (e.g., Delayunfilled RVF > Delayunfilled LVF and the converse; within-group simple effects), satisfying the requirement for within-group task contrasts. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, and not exclusively between-group contrasts. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included.

This is an fMRI task-based study using an N-back working memory paradigm (executive function). The NeuroStore record reports voxelwise, whole-brain group-level analyses (model fit over whole brain) and multiple within-group task contrasts (3-back > OFF) for participant groups, with coordinates/peaks reported in tables. Thus it meets inclusion criteria for fMRI/PET task activation (I5), executive-domain task (I6), whole-brain voxelwise results (I7), presence of within-group task contrasts (I8), any participant group allowed (I9), and reporting of whole-brain results in coordinate tables (I10). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, empirical human data). Full text appears complete in the NeuroStore record.

This study reports task-based fMRI (N-back working memory) assessing an executive function domain (working memory). NeuroStore extraction shows whole-brain model fitting and whole-brain inference (voxelwise analyses with cluster-level permutation statistics). It reports within-group task contrasts (parametric modulation of task repetition and task difficulty in placebo data) and group-level results in tables of coordinates. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 and I10. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and the paper is empirical human neuroimaging. Sample and design (crossover, double blind) are clearly reported. Therefore INCLUDE.

This PET study uses a Stroop task (inhibition/executive control) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise multivariate analyses with within-group task contrasts (e.g., incongruent > congruent; early > later). Results are reported as peaks in a table (coordinate reporting). Participants and methods are appropriate. Although the analysis is covariance-based (multivariate functional connectivity/CVA), the paper provides task-evoked, voxelwise contrast maps/peaks rather than only connectivity or ROI results, so it does not meet exclusion E4 or E3. All inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study reports task-based fMRI (BOLD) during a Sternberg working memory task, which falls within the executive function domain (working memory). Group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses and inferences are reported (model fit and inference over whole brain; cluster-corrected results with reported peak coordinates/tables). Multiple within-group task contrasts are present (e.g., 6 digits > 2 digits during encoding and delay), meeting the within-group contrast requirement. EEG–fMRI correlations are additional but do not preclude inclusion. Participants and results are reported. Therefore all applicable inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI numerical Stroop study assesses interference/inhibition (meets I5,I6) and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates in tables (meets I7 and I10); participants include MCI patients and controls (meets I9). However, the NeuroStore record lists only between-group contrasts (MCI > controls; interaction contrasts) and does not report any within-group task contrasts for either group. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I8 and meets exclusion criterion E5 (only between-group contrasts reported). Full text appears complete for screening.

This fMRI study uses an N-back working memory task (an executive function domain) and reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task activation (2-back > 0-back) with FWE-corrected peaks (Table tbl2). It also includes within-group contrasts (one-sample t-test for 2-back > 0-back), meets task-domain and modality requirements, and reports coordinates. Although additional analyses are ROI/SVC for interactions, at least one qualifying whole-brain, within-group task contrast is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

This fMRI study uses a task-based Sternberg working memory paradigm (executive domain) and reports whole-brain, group- and within-group voxelwise task activation contrasts. Specifically, within-group contrasts are reported for patients and controls (analyses 17707869_analysis_6 and _7: alphabetize > forward, whole-brain inference, p<0.05 FWE), and multiple group-level voxelwise contrasts are provided (between-group and within-group), with coordinates/tables of peaks. Thus it meets criteria I5 (task fMRI of executive function), I6 (working memory/executive manipulation), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise results), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported), I9 (participant groups acceptable), and I10 (coordinates/tables reported). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and empirical). Full text is available via the NeuroStore record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This fMRI study used an N-back working memory task (an executive function domain) and reports group-level, voxelwise task activation maps. Whole-brain model fitting and whole-brain inference are reported for the main effect of task (2-back > 0-back; Analysis 18554874_analysis_2) and the Middle Frontal Gyrus (Analysis 18554874_analysis_4). Multiple within-group task contrasts are reported (Healthy controls T1/T2, Patients T1: Analyses 5–7). Therefore it meets fMRI task-based executive function (I5,I6), contains whole-brain voxelwise group-level results (I7), includes within-group task contrasts (I8), and qualifies across participant groups (I9). Reporting of coordinates/peaks is present (I10). No exclusion criteria apply: the paper does not report only ROI/SVC results nor only between-group contrasts or connectivity/resting analyses. Full text appears complete in this record. Hence INCLUDE.

The study reports task-based fMRI BOLD activations for a working memory paradigm (verbal and non-verbal visual WM), satisfying executive-function scope. Group-level random-effects, voxelwise whole-brain analyses are reported (model fit over: whole brain; coordinate space MNI) with peak coordinates in tables, and multiple within-group task contrasts versus baseline and direct within-group condition contrasts are listed (e.g., verbal 2s ISI > baseline; verbal 2s > non-verbal 2s). Thus inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 and I10 are met. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and within-group contrasts are present. Full text appears complete in the provided NeuroStore record (no access issues).

This fMRI study examines spatial attention and spatial working memory (executive function domain) using task-based paradigms and reports group-level, voxelwise task activation contrasts. Multiple analyses indicate whole-brain model fitting and voxelwise (and whole-brain-corrected) inference (e.g., placebo: attention delay > control; physostigmine effects) as well as within-group contrasts and one-sample t tests. Results are reported as peaks/tables. Participants are healthy adults (n=18). Although some ROI analyses are present, whole-brain voxelwise within-group task contrasts are clearly reported, satisfying inclusion. No exclusion criteria are met.

This fMRI study reports voxelwise, group-level task contrasts of a reflective ‘refreshing’ task versus perception, consistent with executive processes. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI assessing an executive/reflective process), I6 (task taps working-memory–related refreshing, described by authors as a component of working memory), I7 (model fit over whole brain with voxelwise results and reported peak coordinates), I8 (within-group contrasts reported, e.g., Ref > Rep and Scene>Face), I9 (healthy participant group reported), and I10 (whole-brain results reported as peaks). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and empiric). Report provides sufficient detail (group random-effects, thresholds, reported peaks). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This study reports task-based fMRI of inhibitory executive function (stop-signal task) with group-level, voxelwise whole-brain GLM analyses and reported peak coordinates. Multiple within-group contrasts are provided (e.g., GO/STOP > GO ONLY, correct STOP > incorrect STOP, parametric modulation), satisfying the requirement for a within-group task contrast. Results are whole-brain and reported as peaks/tables. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

All required inclusion criteria are met: this is an fMRI task-based study of executive function (visuo-spatial working memory; I5,I6). Results are reported as whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (model fit over whole brain; coordinates/peaks reported; I7,I10). At least one within-group task contrast is reported (WM > control; within-group cross-subject regression; I8). Participant group (developmental sample, ages 7–22) is acceptable (I9). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only (E3), not connectivity-only (E4), and not limited to between-group contrasts (E5), and it is empirical human imaging data (not E6). The NeuroStore record provides voxelwise peaks, task details (2-back), and corrected cluster-level inference, supporting inclusion in the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

The NeuroStore record shows this is an fMRI working-memory (n-back) study (I5,I6) with whole-brain, voxelwise analyses reported as peak coordinates (I7,I10). Participants are healthy adults (I9). However, all extracted statistical contrasts in the document are between-group contrasts / group x condition interactions comparing alcohol vs control at different BACs; no within-group task-versus-baseline or other within-group voxelwise task contrast is reported. Therefore the study reports only between-group/interaction contrasts and does not provide a within-group task activation map, violating exclusion criterion E5. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I7, I9, I10. Inclusion criterion not met: I8 (no within-group task contrast reported). Full text appears available in this record (no access notice), so fulltext_incomplete is false.

This fMRI study reports within-group, voxelwise whole-brain task activation contrasts for an executive function task (Go/No-Go; inhibition). Specifically, the No-go > Go within-group contrast is reported with whole-brain model fitting and voxel-level inference (p<0.001, cluster extent 10) and peak coordinates in tables. The study uses a task-based fMRI paradigm assessing inhibition (an established executive function domain), meeting I5 and I6. Whole-brain voxelwise results are presented (I7) and at least one within-group task contrast is reported (I8). Participant sample (healthy adults) is acceptable (I9), and results are reported as coordinates/tables (I10). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-groups-only, and empirical human data). Full text appears readable in the NeuroStore record. Hence the study should be INCLUDED for meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

The study reports task-based fMRI of the Stroop task (an inhibition executive function task) in native Japanese speakers with within-group contrasts (e.g., Incongruent > Congruent for kana and kanji). Model fitting was performed over the whole brain and results are reported as voxelwise peaks/tables (Talairach coordinates). Multiple within-group voxelwise task contrasts are listed, satisfying the requirement for a group-level voxelwise task-evoked map. Participants are healthy adults. Therefore all inclusion criteria for executive-function task activations are met (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains within-group contrasts, and is empirical).

This is an event-related fMRI study of the Stroop Color-Word task (executive function/cognitive control). It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain statistical maps (model fit over: whole brain; Talairach coordinates; reported peak coordinates and clusters) and two within-group contrasts (incongruent > congruent; color > word). Participants (n=12, adults) are an acceptable group. Results are reported as voxelwise peaks/coordinates. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study investigates inhibition (executive function) using task-based paradigms (Stroop and imitation-inhibition). It reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level contrasts (model fit over whole brain; SPM{z} across subjects) with coordinates/peaks listed. It includes within-group contrasts (incongruent > congruent) for both tasks (n=10 per task) and provides reported peaks/tables. Participants are healthy adults. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for task-based executive function, whole-brain voxelwise analysis, and within-group contrasts; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI task-based study of working memory (Sternberg task) reporting whole-brain, voxelwise group-level contrasts (encoding, maintenance, retrieval; and load linear contrasts). Within-group task contrasts are reported (average across loads; 8>2 letters), coordinates and peak tables are provided. These meet inclusion criteria for executive function domain (working memory), whole-brain voxelwise analysis, within-group contrasts, and acceptable reporting of results. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical).

This PET study reports a task (conscious successive odor discrimination) that requires brief storage and comparison of odors (working memory), meeting the executive-function domain requirement. Multiple within-group contrasts (e.g., Disc > Base, Disc > DetM) are reported. Several analyses are whole-brain, voxelwise group-level maps with voxel-level thresholding and reported peak coordinates (e.g., Analyses 7, 8, 9, 10 and reported tables), satisfying the whole-brain evidence criterion. The study uses a task-based PET paradigm (I5), and healthy adult participants are reported (I9). No exclusion criteria apply: the paper includes voxelwise whole-brain results (not ROI-only), is not a connectivity-only or non-empirical paper, and reports within-group contrasts. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

This study uses task-based fMRI of an executive function task (stop-signal) so I5 and I6 are met; the participant sample (healthy adolescents and adults) is acceptable (I9), and results are reported as peaks so reporting format is acceptable (I10). However, all reported analyses are ROI-based ("Model fit over: region of interest" and "Inference restricted to: region of interest"), so there are no whole-brain voxelwise group-level activation maps (violates I7) — therefore E3 applies. In addition, the NeuroStore record lists only between-group contrasts (adults>adolescents, adolescents>adults) with no within-group task activation contrasts for any group, so it violates I8 and E5 applies. Because it fails I7 and I8 and meets exclusion criteria E3 and E5, the study must be excluded.

This is an fMRI task-based study addressing cognitive control (I5) and the task is interpretable within executive-function domains (authors link DLPFC activity to maintaining intentions/implementing cognitive control, satisfying I6). It reports within-group task contrasts (e.g., inconsistent > consistent; I8) in a healthy adult sample (I9). However, all analyses in the NeuroStore record indicate the model was fit over regions of interest (shared field: 'Model fit over: region of interest'), and no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map is reported. This meets exclusion E3 (only ROI/small-volume analyses). Although some analyses note voxel-level thresholding or 'voxelwise ANOVA', the global "model fit over: region of interest" indicates results were confined to ROIs rather than whole-brain voxelwise maps, so inclusion criterion I7 (whole-brain voxelwise evidence) is not met. Therefore the study must be excluded.

The study used fMRI and reports a within-group working memory task contrast (EARLY > LATE), so I5 (fMRI), I6 (working memory), I8 (within-group contrast), and I9 (participant group) are satisfied. However, the reported analysis is explicitly a region-of-interest analysis with region-level thresholding and model fit over ROIs (STG/STS; Spt). No group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task activation map is reported in the provided record. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I7 (whole-brain voxelwise results). This meets exclusion criterion E3 (studies that report only ROI or small-volume-corrected analyses with no voxelwise results). Full text appeared complete for this record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This PET study reports task-based, within-group voxelwise activation contrasts of executive processes (Hayling Test: initiation and suppression/inhibition) in healthy adults. Analyses were fit over the whole brain with reported peak coordinates in tables (voxelwise group-level contrasts such as Initiation>Rest, Suppression>Rest, Initiation>Suppression), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain, group-level task activation maps. All inclusion criteria I5–I10 are met. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only (E3), not connectivity/resting-state only (E4), and not only between-group contrasts (E5); the paper is empirical human neuroimaging data (not E6). Although sample size is small (n=6), that does not violate the review’s inclusion criteria. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

The study reports task-based fMRI of working memory (allocentric/egocentric spatial recall), which falls under executive function (working memory). Group-level, voxelwise whole-brain second-level analyses are reported (e.g. AlloSpace > EgoSpace; AlloSpace simple effect; one-sample t-test and random-effects analyses), satisfying whole-brain evidence and within-group task contrast requirements. Participants are a human sample (n=20 adults). Results reported as voxelwise peaks. No exclusion criteria apply: analyses are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and within-group contrasts are present. Therefore it qualifies for inclusion in the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

The study reports an fMRI stop-signal task (inhibition), meeting the executive-function domain. It includes group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (Analyses 17884586_analysis_0 and _1: model fit and inference over whole brain, FWE-corrected, reported peaks) and reports within-group contrasts (pre-SE > pre-SS and pre-G > pre-SS). Participants are described (n=40 healthy adults). Thus it satisfies I5 (task fMRI), I6 (inhibition task), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise group results), I8 (within-group contrasts), I9 (participant groups acceptable), and I10 (results clearly reported). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and empirical fMRI data are present). Full text is available in the provided NeuroStore record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study is excluded because the task is a motor sequence learning paradigm focused on motor preparation, sequencing and execution, which does not fall within the review's defined executive function domains (I6 not met). Evidence: task-based fMRI was used (I5), multiple whole-brain voxelwise group analyses are reported (I7), within-group/main-effect task contrasts are present (e.g., movement preparation/execution collapsed across groups) satisfying I8, participants are healthy (I9), and results/coordinates are reported (I10). No exclusion criteria are triggered (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only). Thus exclusion is based on failure to meet I6 (task domain).

The study investigates Stroop cognitive control using fMRI and reports within-group task contrasts, but all task-activation contrasts were modeled and reported within a priori regions of interest rather than as group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task activation maps. Only the PPI connectivity analysis was fit over the whole brain, but this is a connectivity result (not a task-evoked voxelwise activation map). Therefore it fails the requirement for at least one whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task contrast. Exclusion criterion met: E3. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI task assessing cognitive control), I6 (task in executive function domain: inhibition/cognitive control), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported), I9 (participant group acceptable). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (no group-level voxelwise whole-brain task activation map reported), I10 (not applicable since no whole-brain activation map provided).

The study reports task-based fMRI (3T) of initiation of motor sequences, which falls under the executive function domain 'initiation'. It includes multiple group-level, voxelwise (whole-brain) contrasts with voxelwise inference and coordinate tables, and reports within-group task contrasts (internally- vs externally-initiated planning and execution phases). Participants are a healthy adult sample. Results are reported as whole-brain voxelwise peaks (tables), satisfying reporting requirements. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Thus all inclusion criteria are satisfied and the study should be INCLUDED.

This fMRI study used a 2-back working memory task (executive function domain) in patients with schizophrenia and matched controls, fulfilling I5 and I6. NeuroStore indicates voxelwise whole-brain model fitting and cluster-level inference with reported peak coordinates, satisfying I7 and I10. The record includes within-group task contrasts (verbal WM > spatial WM and spatial WM > verbal WM in healthy participants, and other within-group effects), meeting I8. Participant groups include clinical and healthy samples, meeting I9. No exclusion criteria apply: the paper reports whole-brain voxelwise activation maps (not ROI-only), is not connectivity-only, and includes within-group contrasts (so E3–E5 do not apply), and it is empirical (E6 not met). Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

The study uses PET during an N-back (working memory) task, and reports group-level, voxelwise contrasts comparing exposure conditions (EMF vs sham). While it meets I5 (PET; task-based executive function), I6 (working memory), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise group analyses reported), I9 (acceptable participant group), and I10 (results reported as table coordinates), it does NOT report any within-group task activation contrast (e.g., task vs baseline or active control). All extracted analyses are contrasts of exposure condition (EMF > sham or sham > EMF). Inclusion criterion I8 (at least one within-group task contrast) is not satisfied. No exclusion criteria E3-E6 apply. Therefore the study must be excluded for failing to meet I8.

The study used resting-state PET (scanned at rest) rather than a task-based, executive-function paradigm and reports group comparisons and correlations with clinical/neuropsychological scores rather than any within-group task-evoked activation contrasts. Therefore it does not meet the requirement for a task-based within-group activation (I5, I8) or task-evoked whole-brain maps for executive tasks (I6, I7). Exclusion criteria E4 (resting-state/no task activation map) and E5 (no within-group task activation contrast reported) apply. Included: I9 (any participant group qualifies). Not met: I5, I6, I7, I8.

The study reports task-based fMRI using a Stroop Color-Word Task (classic inhibition/executive function) with experimental heat pain distraction. It provides whole-brain, voxelwise, group-level within-subject contrasts (multiple within-group contrasts reported, inference over whole brain, and tables of peak coordinates). Thus it satisfies executive-function task domain (I5,I6), whole-brain voxelwise results (I7), within-group contrasts (I8), participant inclusion (I9) and acceptable reporting of coordinates/tables (I10). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and not between-group-only. Fixed-effects model and small sample size noted but do not conflict with the review inclusion criteria.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using a Sternberg working memory task (executive function domain). Group-level, voxelwise whole-brain FIR models were estimated and voxel/vertex-level thresholding reported, with multiple within-group task contrasts (Encode, Delay, Probe vs fixation/trial types) presented as coordinates. Participants are healthy human subjects (n=12). Results are reported in tables of peaks and the model was fit over the whole brain. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 and I10. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group contrasts, and is empirical).

The study is an empirical PET task-based study measuring cerebral blood flow during a prospective memory task. Prospective memory involves holding an intention and monitoring for target cues, which maps onto established executive domains (planning/vigilance/initiation). Neuroimaging analysis is group-level, voxelwise with model fit over the whole brain and reported Talairach peaks. A within-group task contrast is reported (omnibus, within-group). Thus it satisfies I5 (PET task-based executive/cognitive control), I6 (task falls within executive domains: planning/vigilance/initiation), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise analysis), I8 (within-group contrast), I9 (participant group acceptable), and I10 (results reported as coordinates). No exclusion criteria apply. Sample size (n=6) noted but not exclusionary.
