NeuroStore extraction shows all reported analyses were fitted and inferred within predefined ROIs ("Model fit over: region of interest"; "Inference restricted to: region of interest"). Although the study used task-based fMRI of working memory (mPASAT) and reports within-group contrasts (analyses 2–7) and coordinate peaks, there is no evidence of any group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation map. This violates inclusion criterion I7 (whole-brain voxelwise results required) and meets exclusion E3 (only ROI analyses reported). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (working memory/executive domain), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported), I9 (participant groups acceptable). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise group-level map). Full text is available from NeuroStore record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This study reports task-based fMRI during a Sternberg working memory task (executive function) with whole-brain, voxelwise second-level group analyses and within-group contrasts (e.g., Emo > Face, Face > Emo). Results are reported as thresholded voxelwise maps with peak coordinates/tables. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for fMRI task activation in an executive function domain (working memory), whole-brain voxelwise analyses, and at least one within-group task contrast. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains within-group contrasts, empirical data reported).

This study reports task-based fMRI during an N-back working memory task (an executive function domain) and provides whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses. NeuroStore extraction shows within-group cross-subject regressions of fMRI signal against cognitive reserve with model fit and inference performed over the whole brain, and coordinates/peaks are reported. These meet criteria I5 (task fMRI), I6 (working memory), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise results), I8 (within-group task contrast/regression), I9 (participant group acceptable), and I10 (coordinates reported). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and not only between-group contrasts). Although sample size is small (n=14), that does not violate inclusion rules. Therefore include.

The study is an fMRI Stroop task investigating inhibition and aging and reports whole-brain, voxelwise, group-level results (satisfying I5, I6, I7, I9, I10). However, all extracted analyses in the document are between-group contrasts (incongruent > neutral labeled between-group), an interaction (age-related changes), and a cross-subject regression (RT-related changes). The document does not report any within-group task contrast (e.g., incongruent > neutral computed within a single participant group). Therefore the study reports ONLY between-group contrasts/interactions with no within-group task activation contrast, meeting exclusion criterion E5. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I7, I9, I10. Inclusion criteria not met: I8. Exclusion criteria met: E5.

This NeuroStore record reports an empirical fMRI study using the PASAT (a working memory/executive function task) with task-based activation contrasts. Within-group, voxelwise, group-level contrasts are reported for both MS patients (n=15) and controls (n=10) with model fit over the whole brain and peak coordinates listed (Table tbl3). These satisfy the review’s requirements for fMRI task activation (I5), executive-domain task (working memory, I6), whole-brain voxelwise results (I7), and within-group task contrasts (I8). Participant groups are acceptable (I9) and results are reported as coordinates/tables (I10). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, or non-empirical study).

This is a task-based fMRI study of response inhibition (nogo vs saccade), an executive function domain. The NeuroStore record reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (model fit and inference over whole brain) with within-group contrasts (nogo > saccade; instruction and response contrasts) and peak coordinates (tables). Participants are healthy adults. Results are reported in tables of peaks. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply.

EXCLUDED because the reported analyses were fit over an a priori region of interest (frontal cortex) rather than as whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps, thus failing inclusion criterion I7 and meeting exclusion E3. The study does satisfy I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (working-memory task falls under executive function), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported), I9 (participant group acceptable), and I10 (results reported as peaks/coordinates). However because voxelwise results were confined to an ROI (no whole-brain voxelwise analysis reported), it must be excluded.

This fMRI study examines task switching (cognitive flexibility), an executive function domain, using event-related task paradigms and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (switch > stay and stay > switch) with peak coordinates in tables. Analyses are within-group contrasts in healthy participants (n=10 and n=8). Whole-brain model fitting and whole-brain inference are explicitly reported. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for task-based fMRI executive-function activations and does not meet any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical).

The NeuroStore record reports an fMRI Go/No-Go task (executive function: inhibition) with voxelwise whole-brain group analysis, satisfying I5, I6 and I7; participants are a clinical sample so I9 is applicable. However, the document only reports a between-group/inter-group contrast (HC Go/NoGo > AHD Go) and does not report any within-group task contrast for either group. This violates inclusion criterion I8 and meets exclusion criterion E5 (only between-group contrasts reported). Therefore the study must be excluded.

This PET study reports task-based, whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts comparing simultaneous interpreting versus shadowing. The tasks clearly engage verbal working memory and cognitive control (authors report engagement of verbal working memory, lexical search and semantic processing), fitting established executive function domains. Multiple within-group contrasts are reported (English→Finnish > shadowing English; Finnish→English > shadowing Finnish), with coordinates/peaks reported and cluster-level correction for multiple comparisons. No exclusion criteria are met (results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and within-group contrasts are present). Therefore all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are satisfied.

This NeuroStore record reports an empirical fMRI study using a task of sustained attention (vigilance), an executive function domain. Whole-brain, voxelwise analyses were performed and inference was carried out over the whole brain with corrected voxelwise thresholds; peak coordinates (reported peaks) are provided. The document lists within-group contrasts (N > P) for both the cocaine and control groups (voxelwise, group-level analyses). Thus all required inclusion criteria are satisfied (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Full text is available as a derived NeuroStore record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This study reports a task-based fMRI experiment using a working memory (Sternberg delayed item recognition) paradigm (meets I5,I6). Analyses were fit over the whole brain with inference conducted over the whole brain and reported peak coordinates (group-level, voxelwise task-evoked maps), satisfying I7 and I10. The reported contrasts are omnibus within-group effects (explicitly labeled within-group), satisfying I8. Participant sample is a healthy adult group (I9). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and empirical). Thus all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

Study reports task-based fMRI of cognitive flexibility (task switching/Stroop), meeting executive function domain. Multiple group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise within-group contrasts are reported (e.g., incongruent color naming > neutral color naming; reverse-Stroop early segment; parametric modulation), with corrected thresholds and Talairach coordinates/tables of peaks. Participants are healthy humans (n=12). Results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and include within-group task contrasts. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of cognitive control/task switching and working memory (meets I5 and I6). Analyses are group-level, voxelwise whole-brain GLM results with voxel-level FDR thresholding and reported peak coordinates in tables (meets I7 and I10). At least one within-group task contrast is reported (e.g., target switching > non-switching; first third > second third) (meets I8). Participant group is an eligible sample (healthy adults; meets I9). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, and not limited to between-group contrasts. All inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met. Full text is available as a NeuroStore-derived record, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

Exclusion met: E5 — the paper reports only between-group contrasts/group × condition interactions (all three extracted analyses are interaction/between-group contrasts). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (inhibition Go/No-Go task falls within executive function), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise analyses and whole-brain inference reported), I9 (clinical participant group is allowable), I10 (results reported as peaks/tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I8 (no within-group task contrast reported for any group in the provided document). Therefore the study is excluded because it fails I8 and meets exclusion E5. Full text appears complete for screening (fulltext_incomplete=false).

Exclusion E5 met: the NeuroStore record reports only between-group contrasts and group x condition interactions (e.g. ‘between group analysis’ and interaction contrasts for encoding and recognition) with no within-group task activation contrast reported for any group. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI study), I6 (working memory task falls within executive function), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I9 (participant groups are acceptable clinical sample), I10 (results reported in tables/peaks). Inclusion criterion not met: I8 (no within-group task contrast reported). Therefore the study must be excluded under E5.

This is an fMRI task-based study of task-switching (executive control/cognitive flexibility) reporting a within-group contrast (switch > repeat). The NeuroStore record shows a group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analysis with voxel-level Bonferroni thresholding and reported peak coordinates, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked results. All relevant inclusion criteria are met (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10). No exclusion criteria apply (the study does not report only ROI or connectivity analyses nor only between-group contrasts). Although the sample size is small (n=9), no exclusion criterion disqualifies on that basis. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

The study is task-based fMRI of working memory (meets I5 and I6), reports within-group task contrasts (e.g., J>M, CJ>J) (meets I8), and uses healthy participants (meets I9). However, all reported analyses are region-of-interest (model fit over: region of interest; inference restricted to ROIs) with no whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps reported, so it fails inclusion criterion I7 and therefore meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results). Consequently the study is excluded.

This fMRI study reports whole-brain, within-group voxelwise analyses of a visuomotor tracking/motor learning task. It therefore satisfies I7 (whole-brain voxelwise results reported), I8 (within-group task contrast), I9 (participant group reported), and I10 (results reported in tables/coordinates). However, the task is a visuomotor adaptation/tracking motor-skill learning task and not an established executive function domain (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). The study does not assess executive function or cognitive control per the review’s domain criteria, so it fails I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Conclusion: EXCLUDED because inclusion criteria I5 and I6 are not satisfied.

This is an fMRI study of task-switching in verbal fluency (meets I5, I6). It reports within-group contrasts (SWITCH > single-category) and provides voxelwise single-subject whole-brain analyses and coordinates (meets I8, I9, I10). However, the NeuroStore record only lists single-subject (individual) voxelwise analyses; no group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical map is reported in the provided document. Inclusion criterion I7 (at least one group-level, voxelwise map) is not satisfied. No exclusion criteria E3–E6 explicitly apply based on the available record. Therefore the study must be excluded for failing to meet I7.

This is an event-related fMRI study of inhibition using somatosensory go/no-go tasks (executive function domain: inhibition). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise within-group contrasts (Movement Nogo and Count Nogo; random-effects one-sample t-tests; FDR-corrected maps reported with peak tables) and additional between-condition contrasts. Results are reported as coordinate tables. Participants are healthy adults (n=15). Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I5–I10). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes within-group contrasts, empirical data present). Full text is available via the NeuroStore record, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

This is an fMRI study using a Go/No-Go (inhibition) task (I5,I6). Analyses were estimated voxelwise over the whole brain and reported peaks/tables (Model fit over: whole brain; voxel-level thresholds), satisfying whole-brain evidence (I7,I10). The paper reports within-group task contrasts (one-sample t tests for control subjects: unexpected vs expected stimulus contrasts; Analyses 5–7), meeting the requirement for a within-group task activation (I8). Participant groups (adolescents, ADHD patients, unaffected siblings, controls) are acceptable (I9). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not limited to ROIs or SVC only (E3), are not connectivity/resting-state only (E4), and the paper includes within-group contrasts (so E5 does not apply); it is empirical human neuroimaging data (not E6). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using a Tower of London planning paradigm (an executive function: planning). The NeuroStore record reports whole-brain, voxelwise, group-level within-group contrasts (planning > baseline) for participant groups (OCS low and OCS high) with voxelwise FDR correction and tables of reported peaks, satisfying whole-brain and reporting requirements. At least one within-group task contrast is present for each group. No exclusion criteria are met (results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and within-group contrasts are reported). Therefore all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 and I10 are satisfied.

The NeuroStore record documents a task-based fMRI study of task switching (cognitive flexibility) with n=39 healthy participants, reporting whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses. Multiple reported contrasts are task contrasts (e.g., object switch > no switch) and an omnibus brain–behavior association is reported at the second level, all thresholded voxelwise across the whole brain. Therefore the study meets: I5 (fMRI task-based executive function), I6 (task in executive domain: cognitive flexibility), I7 (whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results), I8 (group-level task contrasts of switch > no-switch), I9 (participant group acceptable), and I10 (results reported as tables/peaks). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and within-group task contrasts are present. Based on these facts from the provided document, the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This fMRI study reports within-group, task-evoked voxelwise contrasts of an executive function task (N-back working memory). Analyses 11960021_analysis_2 and _3 are whole-brain GLM contrasts (high reward > no reward and no reward > high reward) with voxelwise inference corrected for multiple comparisons (p<0.05) and reported peak coordinates (Table 1). The task is an established executive domain (working memory), and results are reported as whole-brain, group-level activation maps (voxelwise). Participant group (n=6) is explicitly described. Coordinate space is provided (Talairach). Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion requirements (task-based fMRI of executive function; whole-brain, voxelwise group contrasts; within-group contrasts reported) and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This task-based fMRI study explicitly examines visuospatial working memory (an executive function domain) using a within-subject task contrast (multiple PoV conditions > table task). Group-level, random-effects voxelwise analyses (one-sample t-tests) were reported with coordinates/peaks and cluster-level thresholding, indicating whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps (MNI coordinates, reported peaks in tables). Although some inferences used small-volume correction for specific parametric analyses, main contrasts report voxelwise group results rather than ROI-only outcomes. Participants and experimental design are clearly described. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis requirements for executive-function task activations and provides within-group, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps suitable for inclusion.

The study reports PET task-based activations during the Tower of London planning task (an executive function: planning), satisfying modality and task domain (I5,I6). Multiple analyses are reported with group-level, voxelwise whole-brain model fits and whole-brain inference and coordinate tables (I7,I10). Importantly, within-group voxelwise task contrasts/parametric modulations are reported for both healthy controls and PD patients (analyses 2–5), meeting the requirement for a within-group task contrast (I8). Clinical participants are included but that is permitted (I9). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not limited to ROI/SVC, not connectivity-only, and include within-group contrasts. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This study reports only seed-based functional connectivity contrasts comparing rest vs two-back working memory. NeuroStore extraction shows 'Result: connectivity' with seed PCC/precuneus and two analyses of correlational activity (21 and 7 peaks), and no task-evoked activation (GLM task > baseline) maps are reported. The meta-analysis requires voxelwise task-evoked activation maps (I7). Exclusion criterion E4 (studies reporting only connectivity analyses or resting-state analyses without task activation maps) therefore applies. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI task-based study), I6 (working memory task — executive function), I8 (within-group contrast reported: rest > WM), I9 (participant group acceptable), I10 (results reported as coordinates/tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked activation map reported). Thus exclude per E4.

The study is an fMRI task-based investigation of semantic event sequencing (an executive function/planning task) and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise between-group task contrasts and connectivity. However, no within-group task activation contrast for any participant group is reported in the provided document; all reported task contrasts are between-group (Control>HIV+, HIV+>Control) or connectivity analyses. This violates exclusion criterion E5 (only between-group contrasts with no within-group task activation). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI task study), I6 (task maps to executive function/planning), I7 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain results reported), I9 (participant groups acceptable), I10 (results reported in tables/coordinates). Inclusion criteria not met: I8 (no within-group task contrast reported). Therefore the study must be excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study using an n-back working memory task (executive function domain) in healthy participants. The NeuroStore record reports whole-brain, voxelwise within-group task contrasts (Analyses 2 and 3: simple effects across 0-,1-,2-,3-back with whole-brain model fit and inference, voxelwise corrected p<0.05) satisfying the requirement for at least one group-level voxelwise task activation map. A within-group task contrast is present, task falls within established executive function domains, and results are reported as peak coordinates. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-groups-only, and is empirical).

Excluded for E5: The NeuroStore record indicates the reported analyses are cross-subject regression / between-group multivariate (canonical variates) maps relating load-evoked activation to cognitive reserve. Although the study uses task-based fMRI (Sternberg working memory) and reports whole-brain voxelwise results and peak coordinates, the document does not present any within-group task contrasts (e.g., task > baseline or set-size main effect within a single group). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (working memory task), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise analyses), I9 (participant groups acceptable), I10 (coordinates/peaks reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I8 (no within-group task contrast reported). Therefore the study is excluded under E5.

This PET study meets multiple methodological inclusion criteria (I5: PET task-based imaging; I7: whole-brain, voxelwise model fit and voxel-level thresholding with reported coordinates; I8: within-group task contrasts reported [conditional/power/precision > rest]; I9: acceptable participant group; I10: whole-brain results reported as coordinate tables). However it does not meet I6: the experimental paradigm is a sensorimotor conditional grasping/reach task probing stimulus-guided motor selection rather than an established executive function domain (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, or initiation) as defined by the review. The reported contrasts and description focus on motor selection and parietal/premotor activation rather than cognitive control/executive processes. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore the study is excluded because I6 is not satisfied.

The study reports an event-related fMRI Stroop task (an inhibition-related executive function paradigm) with group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses over the whole brain (MNI). Multiple within-group contrasts are reported (e.g., RI; SI > CO, CO > SU) with peak coordinates and thresholding (p<0.005, cluster extent), satisfying voxelwise whole-brain reporting. Participants are healthy adults (n=9) and the analyses are task-based activation contrasts. These facts satisfy inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 and I10. No exclusion criteria apply: the study is not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, and includes within-group task contrasts. Full text appears available in the NeuroStore-derived record.

The study reports a task-based fMRI investigation of response inhibition (Go/NoGo), an executive function (inhibition). It includes a group-level, voxelwise whole-brain within-group contrast (NoGo > Go; Analysis 14572528_analysis_1) with voxel-level thresholding and reported coordinate peaks, satisfying whole-brain evidence and a within-group task contrast. Participants are healthy adult males (eligible per I9). Results are reported as coordinates/tables. Although some secondary analyses used ROIs, the presence of a whole-brain voxelwise task contrast means E3 does not apply. Therefore all inclusion criteria for the review are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

This is an fMRI task-based study (Tower of London planning) assessing planning, an established executive function. The NeuroStore record reports voxelwise whole-brain model fitting and whole-brain inference with cluster-level correction, and multiple within-group task contrasts (e.g., planning vs easier planning, correctly vs erroneously solved trials; movement execution contrasts). Results are reported in tables of peak coordinates. Participants are a within-group sample (n=22). These facts meet inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 and I10. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) are met.

This study reports event-related fMRI task-based data (Stroop and Simon), both classic inhibition/executive-control tasks, satisfying I5 and I6. Analyses were voxelwise with model fit over the whole brain and reported group-level contrast peaks (incongruent > congruent), meeting I7, I8, and I10. Participant group is healthy adults (n=10), which is acceptable per I9. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only (E3), not connectivity/resting-state only (E4), and include within-group contrasts (not only between-group; E5). The NeuroStore record lists whole-brain, voxelwise, within-group task contrasts with tabulated peaks, providing sufficient task activation evidence for inclusion in a meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is a task-based fMRI study of task-switching (executive function/cognitive flexibility) with healthy adults (n=20). It reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level contrasts (model fit over whole brain) and provides peak coordinates/tables for multiple within-group contrasts (bivalent>univalent; rule switch>rule repetition). These features satisfy inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria apply (analyses are not ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical).

This is a task-based fMRI study using an N-back working memory paradigm (executive function domain). Group-level random-effects GLM contrasts (within-subject) are reported, with model fit over the whole brain and reported peak coordinates (tables). Although inference used small-volume correction/ROIs, voxelwise group-level maps were estimated and peaks are reported, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results. Multiple within-group task contrasts are provided (e.g., high vs low WM load, pain × visibility × WM interactions). No exclusion criteria (only-ROI/SVC-only, connectivity-only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5–I10.

The study reports a task-based fMRI group analysis of a working memory (Sternberg) task, which falls within executive function. Analysis 14568473_analysis_2 is a within-group contrast (load L6 > L1) estimated over the whole brain (group-level voxelwise GLM; Talairach coordinates) with results reported in tables (Table 2) and a stringent threshold (p<0.0001). Participants are healthy adults (n=8). These elements satisfy inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria apply: the study is not ROI-only (voxelwise whole-brain results are reported), not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical. Full text is available in the provided NeuroStore record representation.

This is an fMRI task-based empirical study reporting within-group task contrasts (Melody Discrimination > control; Harmony Discrimination > control; Melody Listening > rest) with group-level, voxelwise whole-brain statistical maps (Talairach coordinates and peak tables). The discrimination tasks involve same/different judgments across brief melodies and the authors explicitly report activation in working-memory-related regions (cingulate, DLPFC), supporting that the tasks engage the executive function domain of working memory. Participant sample is reported (healthy adults, n=11 for discrimination analyses), and results are reported as coordinates/tables. All required inclusion criteria are met (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and empirical).

The study reports task-based fMRI (BOLD) examining action planning (planning is an executive function domain). It provides group-level, within-subject voxelwise contrasts (Final>Immediate and Immediate>Final) with whole-brain model fit and whole-brain inference, and reports peak coordinates/tables. The task is event-related, n=16 adults, and results are thresholded and reported (MNI). These features meet the meta-analysis requirements for executive-function task activations and do not trigger any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and includes within-group contrasts). Full text appears sufficiently represented in the NeuroStore record.

Excluded because the study reports only region-of-interest-restricted voxelwise inference despite fitting models over the whole brain. This violates exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI/SVC analyses with no whole-brain voxelwise results). The study does meet inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI examining executive function), I6 (working memory task), I8 (reports within-group task contrasts for groups), and I9 (includes clinical and healthy participant groups). However it does NOT meet I7 (does not provide whole-brain voxelwise task-activation maps; inference was restricted to predefined ROIs), so it cannot be included. Reported peaks derive from ROI-restricted inference (thresholding and inference limited to regions of interest), indicating absence of qualifying whole-brain activation maps.

This fMRI study used a task-based paradigm (Iowa Gambling Task) assessing decision-making processes related to executive function. The NeuroStore record includes a within-group task contrast (decision > no decision) with reported peak coordinates (13 peaks), indicating voxelwise task-evoked results. A group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise between-group analysis is also reported (Control vs SD, whole-brain model fit). Results are reported as coordinates/tables, acceptable per I10. Therefore the study meets: I5 (fMRI task-based), I6 (IGT maps to executive function domain—decision-making/planning), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise results reported), I8 (within-group task contrast present), I9 (participant group acceptable), and I10 (coordinates reported). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group contrast, empirical data). Full text appears sufficiently represented in the NeuroStore record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an fMRI task-based study directly investigating suppression of a mental image (cognitive control/inhibition). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects contrasts (multiple within-group task contrasts such as suppressing > free thinking, erasing > free thinking, imagining > free thinking) with peak coordinates in tables, and voxelwise thresholding. Participants are a healthy adult sample (n=12). These features satisfy all inclusion criteria for executive-function task activations (fMRI, task falling under inhibition/executive control, whole-brain voxelwise group analyses, within-group contrasts, results reported in tables). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, empirical data reported).

This fMRI study used a Simon task probing response inhibition (an executive function) and reports a within-group, voxelwise whole-brain contrast (incongruent > congruent) with group-level statistical inference (GRFT cluster correction). The analysis is a group-level, voxelwise task-evoked map suitable for meta-analysis. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (inhibition domain), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise results), I8 (within-group task contrast), I9 (participant group acceptable), and I10 (results reported as voxelwise/coordinates). No exclusion criteria apply. The reported sample was healthy adults (n=14) and results include reported peak coordinates for the whole-brain contrast.

This fMRI study reports within-group, whole-brain, voxelwise task activation contrasts of task switching (executive function/cognitive flexibility). Analyses include S>NS and SC>OS contrasts (reported peaks in Table 1) using whole-brain inference, meeting requirements for task-based fMRI, executive domain, voxelwise group-level results, and within-group contrasts. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, empirical human imaging data).

This is an empirical 3T fMRI study using a working memory (digit-sorting) task, an established executive-function domain. NeuroStore indicates a group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise contrast (model fit and inference over whole brain) with a within-group simple effect (4-digit vs 5-digit). Thus the study provides task-evoked voxelwise activation maps from an event-related executive task. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not limited to ROIs or connectivity-only, nor are they only between-group contrasts, and this is original empirical human neuroimaging data. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

The study is an empirical fMRI task-based investigation that includes an inhibition-related task (inhibited eye blinking) which falls within the executive function domain of inhibition. It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (model fit over: whole brain) and provides within-group task contrasts for both voluntary and inhibited eye blinking (simple effect, within-group). Peak coordinates are reported (tables), and thresholding and random-effects group analysis are described. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, not only between-group contrasts, and the paper is empirical. Therefore all required inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

The study reports an fMRI working-memory (N-back) task (I5, I6) and includes healthy participants (I9). However, the reported analysis is a between-group genotype x condition interaction (no within-group task activation reported), so it fails I8 and meets exclusion E5. Although the model was fit over the whole brain, inference and thresholding were restricted to a predefined region of interest with ROI-corrected voxelwise thresholds and only ROI peaks reported, so it does not provide voxelwise whole-brain results and meets exclusion E3. Therefore the study should be excluded.

The study is an affective picture viewing (emotion) paradigm (IAPS) and investigates correlations between striatal dopamine synthesis and BOLD responses to positive/negative vs neutral stimuli. Although it reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise within-group contrasts (satisfying I7 and I8), includes an acceptable participant group (I9) and reports coordinates/tables (I10), it does not assess executive function or cognitive control and the task does not fall within established executive-function domains (violates I5 and I6). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Therefore exclude because key inclusion criteria I5 and I6 are not satisfied.

The study is excluded because the task is an Old/New recognition memory task (episodic memory/deception), which does not fall within the meta-analysis’ defined executive function domains (violation of inclusion criterion I6). The paper does meet several other inclusion requirements: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5), reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (I7), includes within-group task contrasts (I8), participant sample is acceptable (I9), and results are reported in coordinate/peak tables (I10). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore exclusion is based solely on failure to meet I6.

This paper reports task-based fMRI of executive control (Eriksen Flanker and go/no-go) in children and adults, examining interference suppression and response inhibition. Multiple group-level, voxelwise within-group contrasts are reported (e.g., incongruent > neutral and no-go > neutral for children and adults) with whole-brain model fitting (Talairach coordinates) and tables of peaks. Thus it meets the meta-analysis requirements: I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function), I6 (inhibition/interference suppression within established EF domains), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise results reported), I8 (within-group task contrasts present), I9 (participant groups acceptable, developmental sample included), and I10 (results reported as coordinates/peaks). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, not non-empirical). Full text is available in the provided record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

Exclusion criterion met: E3. The paper reports an fMRI Eriksen Flanker task with within-group contrasts (INC>NEU, NOGO>NEU) and coordinate tables, but all inference is reported as region-of-interest results using FWE small-volume correction (inference restricted to ROI). Thus the study provides only ROI/SVC-corrected inferential results with no whole-brain voxelwise inference reported, violating the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise evidence. (a) Exclusion ID met: E3. (b) Inclusion IDs met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (inhibition executive domain), I8 (within-group contrasts reported), I9 (healthy participant group reported), I10 (coordinates/tables reported). (c) Inclusion ID not met: I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise inferential map reported; inference restricted to ROI/SVC). Therefore exclude.

The study reports task-based fMRI of inhibition (Stroop-like tasks), matching the executive function domain. Whole-brain voxelwise group-level analyses were performed (model fit over: whole brain) with thresholded coordinate tables reported (peaks in Tables). Multiple within-group task contrasts are reported (congruent > neutral; incongruent > neutral; and modality interactions), satisfying the requirement for within-group voxelwise contrasts. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and not only between-group contrasts. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

Exclusion applied: E3. The NeuroStore record shows only region-of-interest analyses with small-volume correction (Model fit over: region of interest; Inference restricted to: region of interest; Thresholding: GRFT small-volume correction), and no whole-brain voxelwise group-level task activation map is reported.
Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI assessing inhibition/stop-signal task), I6 (executive function domain: inhibition), I8 (within-group task contrast: StopInhibit > Go regression across subjects), I9 (participant group: healthy adults), I10 (results reported as coordinate peaks).
Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (whole-brain evidence: no voxelwise whole-brain group-level task map reported).
Because E3 is met (only ROI/SVC results reported), the study is excluded.

This is an event-related fMRI study of proactive inhibition (an executive/inhibition task) using task-based designs (oddball/vigilance; cue-target delays). Analyses are whole-brain, voxelwise group-level contrasts (one-sample t-tests) with coordinates reported in tables. Multiple within-group task contrasts are reported (baseline/cued, short/long cue–target delay, conjunction), satisfying the requirement for within-group voxelwise task contrasts. Participants are healthy adults (n=14). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and not only between-group contrasts. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I5–I10 and none of the exclusions.

The study reports task-based fMRI of a Continuous Performance Task (vigilance), which falls within executive function domains (I5,I6). Model fitting and inference were performed voxelwise over the whole brain and reported peak coordinates (satisfies I7 and I10). Within-group task contrasts (vigilance > fixation) are reported for healthy participants (analysis_0) and for patients (analysis_2), meeting the within-group requirement (I8). Any participant groups are acceptable (clinical sample present; I9). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, and within-group contrasts are present (E3–E5 do not apply).

This fMRI study examines deception (lie vs truth) during an Old/New recognition task, which recruits executive processes (inhibition/cognitive control) relevant to executive function domains. The record reports multiple group-level, voxelwise, whole-brain analyses (Analyses 9–12) with voxel-level thresholding and tables of peaks, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps. Several contrasts are within-group task contrasts (e.g., main effect of making deceptive responses: LT+LN > TR+CR; TR>FR; FR>CR), meeting the within-group contrast requirement. Participants are healthy adults (n=20). Whole-brain results are reported in tables/peaks. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and empirical). Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

This is an fMRI task-based study of working memory (executive function) reporting a within-group contrast (distractor-plus correct > control) analyzed with a group-level one-sample t-test/GLM. The NeuroStore record states the model was fit and inference was performed over the whole brain (voxelwise), with peaks reported and corrected voxel-level thresholding. Thus it provides whole-brain, group-level task activation maps for an executive function task. Although the analysis label includes 'prefrontal area 8 ROI', the record explicitly indicates whole-brain model fit and whole-brain inference, so E3 (ROI-only) does not apply. No exclusion criteria are met. All required inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) are satisfied.

The study reports task-based fMRI using the Stroop task (an inhibition/selective-attention executive function task), includes whole-brain voxelwise model fitting and inference, and reports within-group contrasts (incongruent > congruent) for both smokers and nonsmokers. These elements satisfy all inclusion criteria for task domain, whole-brain voxelwise results, and presence of within-group contrasts. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and not limited to between-group contrasts). The NeuroStore record provides sufficient detail (group-level voxelwise results and reported peaks) to include this study in the meta-analysis of executive function activations.

The NeuroStore record shows this is an fMRI study of executive function with multiple within-group task contrasts (I5, I6, I8, I9 satisfied). However, all reported analyses were fitted and tested within a priori regions of interest (Model fit over: region of interest; Inference restricted to: region of interest; thresholding corrected for multiple ROIs; region-level). No voxelwise whole-brain group-level statistical maps are reported, so the study fails I7. This meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only/small-volume-corrected analyses with no voxelwise results). Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I8, I9. Inclusion criteria not met: I7. Therefore the study is excluded.

This is an fMRI study of working memory/cognitive control (meets I5 and I6). The NeuroStore record reports a whole-brain, voxelwise group-level contrast (Analysis 14766185_analysis_3: all response conditions > fixation; model fit over: whole brain; voxel-level thresholding, p<0.001, cluster extent 5), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain evidence and a within-group task contrast (I7 and I8). Participant group is a typical sample (n=16) so I9 is met. Whole-brain results are reported in table/tbl1, consistent with I10. Although several ROI analyses are also reported, they do not preclude inclusion because a qualifying whole-brain voxelwise analysis is present. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and empirical human fMRI data).

This is a task-based fMRI study of the Stroop task (an inhibition executive function paradigm) reporting group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with within-group task contrasts (e.g., incongruent > neutral; oddball contrasts). NeuroStore extraction reports model fit over the whole brain, random-effects group analysis, and tables of reported peak coordinates. Results are presented as within-group contrasts and coordinate tables. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study using the Stroop task (inhibition), which falls squarely within executive function domains. The NeuroStore record reports within-group task contrasts (interference > color naming for both controls and MJ smokers; Analyses 2 and 3) and whole-brain, voxelwise within-group regression analyses (Analyses 4 and 5 reported model fit over whole brain, voxelwise regression of interference with errors of commission). Thus the paper provides at least one within-group voxelwise task-evoked statistical map and meets the meta-analysis requirements. Although several ROI analyses are reported, the presence of whole-brain voxelwise results means it is not limited to ROI-only reporting. Participant groups (chronic cannabis users and controls) are acceptable per criteria. Therefore include.

This is an event-related fMRI study of working memory (an executive function) reporting group-level, voxelwise within-group contrasts (manipulation > monitoring and monitoring > manipulation) with whole-brain model fitting and reported peak coordinates. Although some inference was directed to predicted regions, the model was fit over the whole brain and results are reported as peaks (coordinates), which satisfies whole-brain evidence and the allowance for coordinate reporting. The study therefore meets criteria for fMRI executive-task domain, whole-brain voxelwise results, and within-group contrasts. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using the Sternberg working-memory task (executive function domain). Group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses are reported (model fit over: whole brain; Talairach coordinates and voxelwise thresholding reported), including within-group contrasts (parametric modulation of exponential signal change; first vs. last retrieval section within-group). Results are presented as coordinate tables and peak lists. Thus the report meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 and I10. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) apply. Full text is available via the NeuroStore record provided, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This PET study investigates selective responding and sustained attention (vigilance/oddball task) using task-based contrasts. It meets inclusion criteria: (I5) PET task-based neuroimaging of executive function/cognitive control; (I6) tasks map to established executive domains (vigilance/monitoring/selective responding); (I7) model was fit over the whole brain (voxelwise analyses reported); (I8) multiple within-group task contrasts are reported (e.g., S > NS, time on task interactions); (I9) participant group is acceptable (healthy adults reported); (I10) whole-brain voxelwise results are reported as stereotactic coordinates (Talairach) and tables. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains within-group contrasts, empirical data). Full text is available as a derived NeuroStore record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using a working memory/source memory paradigm (meets I5 and I6). The NeuroStore record includes a group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analysis (analysis_16256377_analysis_2: model fit over whole brain, Talairach coordinates) satisfying I7. Within-group task contrasts are reported (e.g., source memory > old-new and contrasts reported separately for young adults in the abstract), satisfying I8. Participant groups are acceptable (young and older adults), satisfying I9. Results/coordinates are reported (Talairach peaks), satisfying I10. No exclusion criteria apply: the study does not report only ROI/SVC analyses (whole-brain voxelwise results are present), nor is it connectivity-only or non-empirical, and it includes within-group task contrasts (so E3–E6 do not apply). Therefore the paper meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This study reports task-based fMRI of an antisaccade (inhibition) task, a canonical executive-control paradigm. Multiple group-level, voxelwise within-group contrasts are reported (simple effects for pro, anti, nogo and contrasts anti>pro, anti>nogo, nogo>pro), with whole-brain model fitting and whole-brain inference and coordinates listed in tables. Results are presented as voxelwise activation peaks (Talairach coordinates). Participant sample is healthy adults (n=10). Thus all inclusion criteria for executive-function, whole-brain voxelwise within-group contrasts, and reporting of coordinates are met, and no exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply.

The paper reports group-level fMRI task contrasts (M > L; H > L) in a working memory (cross-modal temporal order) task, but NeuroStore extraction states the model was fit over a region of interest (Model fit over: region of interest) and lists only ROI-based results. This means no voxelwise whole-brain task activation map is reported, violating inclusion criterion I7 and meeting exclusion criterion E3. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (working memory domain), I8 (within-group contrasts reported), I9 (participant group reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I7 (whole-brain voxelwise evidence). Therefore the study is excluded.

This study meets all inclusion requirements for the meta-analysis: it is an event-related fMRI task study of executive/attentional control (Simon and spatial Stroop tasks) (I5,I6). It reports group-level, random-effects, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (model fit over whole brain, FILM random-effects) with within-group task contrasts (Simon Incongruent > Simon Congruent; Stroop Incongruent > Stroop Congruent) and tables of reported peak coordinates (I7,I8,I10). Participant group is acceptable (healthy adult sample, n=11) (I9). No exclusion criteria are met: analyses are not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, and not limited to between-group contrasts or non-empirical. The NeuroStore record supplies sufficient detail to verify criteria. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This study is excluded because it does not report any within-group voxelwise task activation contrasts. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (reports only between-group/group×condition interaction contrasts). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (working memory task — n-back), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise model fit with reported coordinates), I9 (participant groups including clinical sample permitted), I10 (whole-brain results reported as coordinates/tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I8 (no within-group task contrast reported for any group). The NeuroStore record lists only between-group interaction contrasts (patients>controls, controls>patients) and no main-effect or within-group task vs baseline contrasts; therefore it fails the required within-group evidence for inclusion in the meta-analysis of task activations.

Meets all inclusion criteria for the review: the study is a task-based fMRI study (BOLD response) using an oddball paradigm (an established vigilance/attention executive domain). It reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses (model fit and inference over whole brain, voxel-level results) and includes a within-group task contrast (target > non-target, Analysis 18838100_analysis_2). Peak coordinates are reported (Table tbl4). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, and within-group contrasts are present).

This PET study reports task-based, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps for established executive/cognitive-control tasks: RVIP (sustained attention/vigilance and working memory) and a paired-associates learning task. The record shows explicit within-group task contrasts (RVIP > rest; PAL > passive listening) with reported peak coordinates and whole-brain inference, and results are reported for healthy participant groups. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 and I10. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical human imaging).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of executive processes (response initiation and suppression) using the Hayling sentence-completion task. The NeuroStore record reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses and lists coordinate peaks for within-group contrasts (response initiation > control; response suppression > control; suppression > initiation). Thus it meets: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (executive domains: initiation/inhibition), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise group analyses), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported), I9 (participant group acceptable), and I10 (results reported as coordinate peaks/tables). No exclusion criteria are met: analyses are not limited to ROIs/SVCs (E3), not connectivity/resting-only (E4), not only between-group contrasts (E5), and the paper is empirical (E6). Note: small sample size (n=6) and minor inconsistency in reported sex counts were observed in the record, but these do not conflict with inclusion criteria. No indication the full text is incomplete.

The paper is an fMRI study of planning (Tower of London) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise results and coordinate tables. However, all reported analyses are between-subject effects (cross-subject regressions relating performance to activation and a between-group sex contrast). No within-group task-versus-baseline (main effect of task) contrast is reported in the NeuroStore record. This meets exclusion criterion E5 (only between-group contrasts/no within-group task activation). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (planning = executive domain), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise results), I9 (participant group acceptable), and I10 (results reported as coordinates). Inclusion criterion not met: I8 (no within-group task contrast reported). Full text appears complete in the record.

This fMRI study reports a within-group, whole-brain, voxelwise activation contrast that probes response selection/conflict (Incompatible > Compatible), an executive-function domain (response selection/inhibition). The analysis is random-effects, whole-brain, voxel-level inference (p<0.001) with reported peaks (Table 1). Participants are healthy adults (n=12). Therefore the study meets I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (task in an executive-function domain), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results), I8 (within-group contrast), I9 (participant group acceptable), and I10 (coordinates/peaks reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Included for meta-analysis of executive function activations.

This fMRI study reports whole-brain, voxelwise within-group task contrasts for a semantic judgment (lexical semantics) task (meets I7, I8, I9, I10). However, the task is a semantic association/lexical decision task and does not target an established executive function domain (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Although the authors mention working memory demands in discussion, the paradigm and reported contrasts assess lexico-semantic processing rather than executive function. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I5 and I6 and must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered.

This is a task-based fMRI study that examines spatial interference during bimanual coordination and explicitly reports activation of regions “shown previously to contribute to executive functions.” The study reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (Analyses 0–2) with coordinates/tables, and the contrasts are within-group task contrasts (AmpInterf, DirInterf, conjunction, etc.). Participant sample (healthy adults) is acceptable. Results are reported as voxelwise peaks (tables), satisfying whole-brain reporting. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and it is empirical). Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for the executive-function activation meta-analysis.

This fMRI study uses a Go/No-Go task (inhibition), an established executive function domain, and reports multiple within-group voxelwise contrasts (e.g., performed errors > correct responses; observed errors > correct responses). Model fits were conducted over the whole brain and the paper includes whole-brain inference/results (Analyses 4 and 5 report whole-brain contrasts and peaks), satisfying the requirement for group-level voxelwise task-evoked maps. Participants are healthy adults and task-based activation contrasts are clearly reported. Although some analyses used ROI-restricted inference, the presence of whole-brain, voxelwise within-group contrasts means the study is not excluded by ROI-only criteria. Therefore all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The NeuroStore record documents an fMRI Sternberg working-memory task (meets I5 and I6). Analyses were whole-brain, voxelwise with voxel-level thresholding and reported peak coordinates in tables (meets I7 and I10). Participant sample includes clinical and control groups (I9). However, all extracted contrasts in the document are between-group comparisons (controls > patients) and the listed analyses (two tables of peaks) do not include any within-group task contrasts for either group. Therefore the study reports ONLY between-group contrasts and fails inclusion criterion I8. This violates exclusion criterion E5 (only between-group contrasts). Per the screening instructions I excluded the study relying on the provided document.

The study used task-based fMRI and explicitly manipulated/assessed working-memory demands during sentence comprehension (authors state executive resources such as working memory support grammatical processes). Analyses are whole-brain voxelwise (model fit over whole brain) and report within-group task contrasts with coordinate peaks in tables. Thus it satisfies the requirement to assess an executive domain (working memory), provides whole-brain voxelwise results, reports within-group contrasts, and presents coordinate results. The study is empirical human fMRI (not ROI-only, connectivity-only, or between-group-only). Note: the task is language-based rather than a canonical WM paradigm, but the authors explicitly tested working-memory-related recruitment, so it meets the inclusion criteria for this meta-analysis.

This fMRI study reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise within-group task contrasts of language switching (a task-switching paradigm reflecting cognitive flexibility/executive control). Analyses include forward/backward switching > non-switching and direct forward>backward contrasts, with thresholded voxelwise results and coordinate tables (reported peaks). Task fits the executive function domain (cognitive flexibility/task switching). Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10) and does not meet any exclusion criteria (no ROI-only, no connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text is available via the NeuroStore record provided, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of selective attention/cognitive control (Stroop and oddball paradigms), satisfying executive-function domain requirements. Group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses are reported (model fit over: whole brain; random-effects GLM) with voxelwise thresholding and tables of peak coordinates. Multiple within-group task contrasts are presented (e.g. Stroop-incongruency > control; Word-oddball > control), meeting the within-group contrast requirement. Participant group is reported (n=9 healthy adults). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and not limited to between-group contrasts. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study using a Stroop task (an inhibition/action-monitoring executive function), reporting whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise task>control (within-group) contrasts for both OCD patients and healthy controls (Analyses 0 and 1). Results are thresholded and reported as peak coordinates/tables. The study therefore meets all inclusion criteria for task modality, task domain, whole-brain voxelwise analysis, presence of within-group contrasts, and reporting of coordinates. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and within-group contrasts are present).

The study is an fMRI oddball task in MDD and reports whole-brain, voxelwise task activations (peaks in tables), so it meets I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (oddball = vigilance/executive domain), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise results), I9 (clinical sample allowed), and I10 (results reported in tables). However, all extracted analyses are between-group contrasts or group x condition interactions (e.g., control > MDD, MDD > control, interaction contrasts like Target-after-Sad vs Target-after-Neutral). No within-group task contrast for any group (e.g., target > baseline or target > neutral within controls or patients) is reported in the provided document, so inclusion criterion I8 is not met. Because the paper reports only between-group/interactions with no within-group activation contrasts, it violates exclusion criterion E5. Therefore the study must be excluded.

This fMRI study reports task-based, within-group voxelwise contrasts of semantic verbal fluency (word generation > control) across whole-brain analyses (Talairach), with coordinate tables and cluster-level inference. Verbal fluency engages executive processes including initiation and response control, fitting the review’s executive-function domains. Multiple within-group contrasts are reported (overall task, paced, unpaced, overt, covert, paced>unpaced, covert>overt), satisfying the requirement for group-level task activation maps. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical).

This is an event-related fMRI study of tactile object discrimination that explicitly invokes working memory and stimulus discrimination processes. It reports whole-brain, voxelwise group analyses (model fit over whole brain; corrected voxel-level thresholding) and multiple within-group task contrasts (e.g., P2>P1, P1>Ss, delay). The task falls within an executive function domain (working memory/decision), and participant data (n=7 healthy adults) are provided. Results are reported as coordinates/peaks. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and it is empirical). Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria.

The study used fMRI Stroop task (executive/inhibition domain) in a randomized, double-blind crossover with within-subject contrasts, so I5, I6, I8 and I9 are met. However, all reported analyses were fit and inference-restricted to regions of interest (Model fit over: region of interest; Inference restricted to: region of interest) with cluster-level ROI thresholding and no voxelwise whole-brain group maps reported. Thus it does not provide whole-brain voxelwise group-level task activation maps (I7 not met) and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results). Exclusion IDs met: E3. Inclusion IDs met: I5, I6, I8, I9. Inclusion IDs not met: I7.

The task is a social/cooperative-competitive game and the paper frames findings in social cognition; it does not clearly report that the paradigm was designed to assess established executive function domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Therefore inclusion criteria I5 and I6 are not met. The study does meet I7 (group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses reported), I8 (within-group task contrasts: cooperation>independent, competition>independent, etc.), I9 (healthy participant group reported) and I10 (whole-brain results reported as tables of coordinates). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Based on lack of clear executive-function task characterization, the study is excluded from this meta-analysis.

The study reports task-based fMRI of a sequencing task (forward and reverse recitation of months) that engages working memory and related executive processes. It includes group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (voxelwise t-statistics) with within-group task contrasts (FORWARD>baseline, REVERSE>baseline, and REVERSE>FORWARD cognitive subtraction). Results are reported as peak coordinates/tables and sample characteristics are provided (n=18 healthy adults). All required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an event-related fMRI study of cognitive control using incongruent>congruent flanker/gaze contrasts, so inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function), I6 (task in executive function domain - inhibition/conflict), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported), I9 (participant groups acceptable), and I10 (coordinates/peaks reported) are satisfied. However, the NeuroStore record explicitly indicates that the model was fit over and inference was restricted to a region of interest (Model fit over: region of interest; Inference restricted to: region of interest), i.e. no group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation maps are reported. Thus it fails I7 (whole-brain evidence) and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only analyses). Therefore the study should be excluded.

This is an fMRI task-based study of response inhibition (Go/No-Go), an executive function domain (inhibition). The NeuroStore record shows whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (one-sample and paired-sample t-tests; voxel-wise fixed-effects contrasts) with reported peak coordinates/tables. Within-group task contrasts are reported (e.g., NegT>NegD within follicular and luteal phases; PosD vs PosT paired contrasts), satisfying the requirement for a within-group task contrast. Results are reported as whole-brain voxelwise maps and peaks in tables, meeting reporting criteria. Participants are healthy (within-group results available). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function activations.

This PET study reports task-based activations for orientation short-term memory and resistance to distractors, which fall under the executive function domain of working memory (and manipulation/distractor resistance). It includes group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (model fit over: whole brain; inference over whole brain) with reported peak coordinates/tables. Multiple within-group task contrasts are reported (e.g., TSD L > TSD S, TSD L/TSD D > ID), satisfying the requirement for within-group contrasts. Results are reported as corrected voxelwise statistical maps/peaks (Tables 1 and 2). Participants are an eligible group (healthy adults). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10 and should be included in the meta-analysis.

The study is an event-related fMRI investigation of a working memory task (meets I5 and I6) and reports a within-group contrast (correct > incorrect) (meets I8) in an adult sample (meets I9). However, all reported group-level activation results are confined to a region-of-interest analysis (model fit over: region of interest; region-level thresholding) with no voxelwise whole-brain task activation maps reported. Therefore it does not satisfy I7 (whole-brain voxelwise results required) and meets exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI/small-volume-corrected analyses reported). Consequently the study is excluded.

This is an event-related fMRI study using the Stroop task (an inhibition/cognitive-control executive function paradigm). The NeuroStore record reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses with cluster-size thresholding and tables of reported peaks. Within-group contrasts for controls and for unaffected relatives (incongruent > baseline/high conflict incongruent trials) are explicitly reported, satisfying the requirement for at least one within-group task activation map. Participant groups are acceptable (healthy controls and unaffected relatives). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, or only between-group contrasts) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10) and should be included.

This is a task-based fMRI study that investigates decision making involving deliberation, conflict detection and arithmetic operations—processes consistent with executive functions (planning/conflict monitoring). The paper reports within-group voxelwise whole-brain contrasts (A>B and A>C) with cluster-corrected inference and peak coordinates, in a sample of healthy participants. Thus it meets: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (task engages executive-function-related processes—planning/conflict monitoring), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise results), I8 (within-group contrasts reported), I9 (participant group acceptable), and I10 (results reported as peaks/coordinates). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and it's empirical). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This fMRI study reports voxelwise, whole-brain, within-group task contrasts from a task (probabilistic classification learning) that is not clearly within the prespecified executive-function domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise analysis), I8 (within-group contrast reported), I9 (healthy participant group qualifies), I10 (results/peaks reported in coordinate space). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (task does not fall within the listed executive function domains; it targets category/associative learning and feedback processing rather than classic EF constructs). No exclusion criteria were triggered (E3–E6 not met). Because all inclusion criteria must be satisfied and I6 is not met, the study is excluded.

The study reports a task-based fMRI experiment (MOPT) clearly assessing visual working memory/coherence (an executive function). It provides a group-level, voxelwise within-group contrast (test > control) with model fit and inference over the whole brain and corrected cluster-level thresholding; peaks are reported. These facts satisfy the review’s requirements for fMRI task activation, established executive domain (working memory), whole-brain voxelwise evidence, and a within-group task contrast. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical).

This PET task study assesses judgment and planning during Go problems (territorial planning and checkmate judgment), which map onto executive-function domains (planning, visuospatial decision-making). It reports whole-brain, voxelwise analyses with voxel-level correction and tables of reported peaks. At least one within-group task contrast is present (Task 2 > baseline; within-group subtraction analyses for successful and failed responses, n=6). Between-group contrasts are also reported but do not preclude inclusion because within-group contrasts exist. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical).

This fMRI study reports task-based Go/No-Go (inhibition) activations and meets all inclusion criteria: whole-brain, group-level voxelwise within-group contrasts (nogo > control) are reported for healthy controls and for alcohol-dependent patients (Analyses 17826793_analysis_1 and _2) with tabulated peak coordinates. The task is an established executive function (inhibition). Results are reported voxelwise across the whole brain (Talairach space) and thresholding/cluster details are provided. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, and within-group contrasts are present).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using the Emotional Stroop (a inhibition/attention executive function task), satisfying I5 and I6. The record reports within-group task contrasts (positive > neutral words) with reported peaks, indicating voxelwise group-level task activation maps (I7, I8) and results reported as coordinates/peaks (I10). Participants are a human sample (n=26), so I9 is met. While some analyses are ROI- or connectivity-focused, at least one voxelwise task activation contrast is reported, and no exclusion criteria (only ROI, only connectivity, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears available in the record. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

Exclusion rationale: The NeuroStore extraction shows this is a Go/No-Go fMRI study (I5, I6 met). However, the reported analysis is an interaction/between-group contrast (Controls NoGo > VS NoGo [interaction]) with model fit and inference restricted to a region-of-interest. No within-group, voxelwise whole-brain task activation contrast is reported. Therefore the study violates inclusion criteria I7 (no qualifying whole-brain voxelwise results) and I8 (no within-group task contrast). Exclusion criteria E3 (ROI-only with no voxelwise results) and E5 (only between-group contrasts/group x condition interactions, no within-group contrast) apply. Conclusion: EXCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI task-based study of analogical reasoning that explicitly involves complex working memory and relational integration (executive function domain: working memory/reasoning). It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain contrasts (ANA > CAT and ANA > SEM) with voxelwise thresholding and Talairach coordinates, and these are within-group contrasts (n=14). Results are reported as peaks/coordinates. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for task-based fMRI executive function, whole-brain voxelwise reporting, and within-group contrasts.

This study reports task-based fMRI of executive function (Wisconsin Card Sorting Task; set-shifting/planning) with BOLD measures (meets I5 and I6). Multiple group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses are reported (model fit over whole brain; reported peak tables for several within-group contrasts), satisfying I7 and I10. Several within-group task contrasts are present for both healthy controls and PD patients (e.g., retrieval without shift, continuous shift, retrieval with shift; analyses 0,1,2,3,6,7,9,10), meeting I8. Participant groups include a clinical sample (PD) and controls, which is acceptable per I9. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only (E3), not connectivity/resting-only (E4), and within-group contrasts are reported (E5). The NeuroStore record provides sufficient derived whole-brain, voxelwise within-group activation contrasts with coordinates/tables to include the study in the meta-analysis of executive function activations.

This study used passive visual viewing of violent, fearful, and neutral film clips rather than an executive function or cognitive-control task (e.g., working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility). Although the paper reports voxelwise, group-level within-group contrasts and whole-brain results, it does not assess executive function domains required by the review. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I5 (fMRI/PET assessing executive function) and I6 (task within established executive function domains). Inclusion criteria met: I7 (whole-brain voxelwise analysis present), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported), I9 (participant group reported; any group acceptable), I10 (whole-brain results clearly reported). Exclusion criteria met: none (E3–E6 not applicable).

Although this PET study reports whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise within-group contrasts (I7, I8) with coordinate tables (I10) and includes a qualifying participant group (I9), it does not clearly assess an established executive function domain. The task is a perceptual match-to-sample face discrimination with stimulus degradation; authors interpret some right prefrontal activation as possibly reflecting working memory or attention, but the paradigm is primarily perceptual/visuoperceptual rather than a canonical working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, or initiation task. Thus it fails I6 (task within executive function domains) and, as a result, I5 (study assessing executive function/cognitive control) is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an empirical PET study using a task-based paradigm probing vigilance/target detection (an executive function domain). It reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise contrasts (e.g., Few targets > Passive; model fit over whole brain; voxel-level thresholding) with coordinates in Talairach and reported peak tables. Within-group task contrasts are present (attend few/many targets vs passive). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for imaging modality, task domain, whole-brain voxelwise results, within-group contrasts, and reporting of coordinates. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical).

The study used task-based fMRI (ANT) assessing cognitive control, with whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported as peak coordinates. NeuroStore reports within-group contrasts (arousing > unarousing) estimated over the whole brain for each group (n=22 controls, n=10 autism), with voxelwise thresholding and reported peak tables. Thus it satisfies: I5 (task-based fMRI on executive/cognitive-control task), I6 (ANT taps executive domain—conflict/inhibition), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise results), I8 (within-group task contrast reported), I9 (participant groups acceptable), and I10 (results reported as coordinates/tables). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Although the reported contrast tests emotional modulation rather than a simple task>baseline or incongruent>congruent main effect, it is a within-task, voxelwise contrast indexing modulation of cognitive-control-related activation and therefore meets the review inclusion rules.

This fMRI study reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task activation maps and a within-group task contrast (Hypothesis > baseline, one-sample t-test, n=18).
