The task (generate biological hypotheses) engages executive processes (authors report working-memory load and higher-order inferential processes and DLPFC involvement), so it reasonably falls within executive function domains (working memory/planning/initiative). Results are whole-brain and reported as peak coordinates (Table), meeting reporting requirements. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply.

Although this is a whole-brain fMRI study with group-level, voxelwise within-group contrasts (MI>LI) and reported coordinates, the experimental task is a visual/semantic object categorization paradigm rather than a standard executive function task. The authors emphasize top-down control involvement, but the scanner task does not explicitly test established executive-function domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Therefore it does not meet inclusion criteria I5 (assessing executive function/cognitive control as defined) and I6 (task within established executive-function domains). It does meet I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text is complete as provided.

This fMRI study reports a within-group, voxelwise task contrast (VT > baseline) using both fixed- and random-effects GLMs with whole-brain model fit and whole-brain inference and provides reported peak coordinates/tables. The task probes verbal working memory/attentional maintenance and active search for transformations (an executive function demand), meeting the executive-function domain requirement. Participants are a human group (n=10). All inclusion criteria are satisfied (fMRI task-based executive function; task in working memory domain; whole-brain voxelwise group analyses; within-group contrast reported; participant group qualifies; coordinates/tables reported). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical).

This PET study reports task-evoked, within-group, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts of maze traversal (planning) versus control conditions in healthy adults. Maze traversal is a planning task within executive function domains. Model fit was over the whole brain and multiple within-group contrasts are reported (e.g., Uncovered Maze > Motor Control, Covered Maze > Visual Control). Results are given as coordinate peaks (tables) and thresholding details are provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria for task-based PET executive function activations are met (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory/pair-associates (executive domain: working memory). Multiple group-level, voxelwise within-group contrasts are reported (one-sample t-tests: RET6>RET3, RET4>RET3, parametric modulations for encoding/retrieval), with whole-brain model fit and whole-brain inference and coordinates/tables of peaks provided. Participants (n=23 healthy adults) and task details are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an fMRI (BOLD) task-based study using a pro/antisaccade paradigm that requires inhibitory control (antisaccade), fitting the executive function domain (inhibition). The report includes whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (model fit over whole brain; voxel-level threshold p<0.001) and within-group task contrasts (antisaccades vs prosaccades; All eye movements vs rest; interaction contrasts). Results are reported as peak coordinates/tables. Participants are healthy adults (n=8). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an fMRI, task-based study of cognitive control (emotion regulation) with whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses and within-group task contrasts reported (I5, I7, I8, I9, I10 satisfied). However, the task is an emotion-regulation/anticipation paradigm and does not fall within the specified executive-function domains required by the review (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation), so I6 is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Therefore the study is excluded because it fails to meet inclusion criterion I6 (task domain). Inclusion criteria met: I5, I7, I8, I9, I10. Inclusion criteria not met: I6. Exclusion criteria met: none ([]).

The record reports task-based fMRI experiments of working memory (executive domain) with group-level, voxelwise whole-brain GLM analyses and reported peak coordinates (Tables). Multiple within-group contrasts are listed (e.g. HIGH>LOW, ORG>HIGH, ORG>LOW) from two experiments (n=15 each), satisfying within-group contrast and task criteria. Whole-brain model fit is explicitly stated and peaks are reported, satisfying whole-brain evidence and acceptable reporting format. Participants are human and the tasks clearly probe working memory (an EF domain). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not limited to ROIs or small-volume corrections only, not connectivity-only, and not only between-group contrasts. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) and should be INCLUDED.

This study reports task-based fMRI of an executive function task (task switching), with whole-brain voxelwise group-level analyses and explicit within-group contrasts (color shift > motion shift; motion shift > color shift). Results are reported as whole-brain peaks/coordinates with cluster correction. Therefore it satisfies the meta-analysis requirements for executive-function task activations and provides voxelwise within-group contrasts eligible for inclusion.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of verbal working memory (executive function). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise within-group task contrasts (e.g., L1>Control, L2>L1, L3>L2) with reported peak coordinates (MNI/Talairach) and tables, and cross-subject regressions relating performance. Participants are healthy adults (n=15). Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function), I6 (working memory), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise results), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (participant group acceptable), and I10 (results reported in coordinate tables). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met.

This study reports an empirical task-based fMRI experiment using a working memory task (an executive function domain). It includes within-group contrasts, group-level random-effects analysis fit and inferred over the whole brain with voxelwise thresholding and reported peak coordinates (Table tbl1). Participants (n=20 healthy adults) are human and the paper presents voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps (SDM/linear SVM maps) rather than ROI-only or connectivity-only results. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This fMRI study reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise within-group contrasts comparing incorrect vs. correct arithmetic equations. The task engages working memory and interference resolution (established executive function domains). The analysis is a random-effects, two-stage GLM with whole-brain inference and reported peak coordinates, and the contrast is a within-group task contrast (incorrect > correct). All inclusion criteria for task-based executive-function fMRI and whole-brain voxelwise within-group results are satisfied, and no exclusion criteria apply.

Exclusion criteria met: E5. The study reports only between-group/genotype interaction contrasts and ROI-based regression and connectivity analyses; no within-group task activation contrast is reported for any group. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function — verbal fluency), I6 (task falls within executive function domain), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise results reported for activation contrasts), I9 (participant groups include clinical and healthy samples — acceptable), I10 (results reported as peaks/tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I8 (no within-group task contrast reported for any group). Because E5 is met (only between-group/interactions and no within-group task activation), the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This PET study reports task-based, within-group voxelwise activation contrasts relevant to executive function. It includes a task placing heavy load on spatial working memory (an established executive domain) and reports whole-brain SPM voxelwise analyses with Talairach coordinates and peak tables. Multiple within-group contrasts are listed (M SEQ> M PRED, M PRED> S, M ROT> M PRED), satisfying the requirement for within-group task contrasts. The model was fit over the whole brain and results are reported as coordinates/peaks. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

The study reports HMPAO-SPECT (molecular tracer uptake) activation contrasts during a verbal fluency task. Inclusion criterion I5 requires fMRI or PET; the reported voxelwise analyses are SPECT-based (HMPAO-SPECT). Although FDG-PET was mentioned in the abstract, the provided NeuroStore-extracted analyses and reported peaks pertain to 99mTc-HMPAO SPECT, so the study does not meet I5. Satisfied inclusion criteria: I6 (verbal fluency is an executive function task), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise model fit), I8 (within-group Activation>baseline contrast in controls), I9 (participant groups acceptable), and I10 (results reported as peaks/coordinates). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore EXCLUDED because it fails to meet I5 (modality restriction: not fMRI or PET).

This is a task-based fMRI study that reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts (Talairach coordinates, cluster-corrected tables) and includes within-group task contrasts (e.g., untrained > trained, trained > untrained, untrained > number matching, fact retrieval > number matching). The task engages cognitive processes related to working memory (authors explicitly attribute left inferior frontal activation to higher working memory demands in the untrained condition), so it falls within the executive-function domain (working memory). Participants (n=13) are reported. Results are reported as coordinate tables. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group, and is empirical). Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied.

This PET study reports task-evoked activations for spatial working memory (Corsi Block-Tapping), an executive function domain. It includes within-group voxelwise task contrasts (structured and non-structured array span > control; control > span) with model fit over the whole brain and whole-brain inference (and frontal small-volume corrections), reporting peak coordinates. Thus it provides group-level, voxelwise, task activation maps (reported peaks) suitable for inclusion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical).

The study uses task-based fMRI with whole-brain, group-level voxelwise within-subject contrasts of pelvic floor contraction vs rest, reported in coordinates; however the task does not assess an established executive function domain. The paradigm probes voluntary voiding/visceral motor control (pelvic floor contraction to inhibit micturition) rather than cognitive executive processes (working memory, cognitive inhibition in a cognitive task, set-shifting, planning, vigilance, initiation). Therefore inclusion criteria I5 and I6 are not met, although I7, I8, I9, and I10 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text was available in the provided NeuroStore record.

This is a task-based fMRI study (Iowa Gambling Task) explicitly framed as engaging cognitive control/executive functions (temporal integration, top-down biasing), satisfying I5 and I6. Model was fit over the whole brain and inference was whole-brain with voxelwise thresholding and reported peak coordinates/tables, satisfying I7 and I10. Multiple reported within-group task contrasts (state>event, event>state, W12>W2, etc.) meet I8. Participants are healthy adults and any participant group is acceptable (I9). No exclusion criteria are met: results are whole-brain voxelwise (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only), and this is empirical human neuroimaging data (not non-empirical). Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study reports PET measures during a rest (mental rest) condition and examines metabolic changes related to celecoxib treatment rather than task-evoked activation from an executive-function paradigm. Therefore it does not meet key task-related inclusion criteria. Exclusion criterion E4 applies because the paper reports resting-state/metabolic changes without any task activation map. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (voxelwise whole-brain analysis is reported), I9 (participant group is acceptable; clinical sample with within-group contrasts reported), and I10 (results reported as peaks/coordinates). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I5 (not a task-based fMRI/PET study of executive function), I6 (no executive-function task), I8 (no within-group task contrast—within-group contrasts are treatment pre/post rather than task vs baseline). Hence EXCLUDED.

The study reports task-based fMRI of attention shifting (an executive function: cognitive flexibility/vigilance) with within-group contrasts (shifting vs sustained; sustained vs fixation) and tables of peak coordinates and activation maps described in the abstract. Although one analysis (Analysis 4) is ROI-restricted, multiple contrasts (including the primary shifting>sustained) are reported at the group level with whole-brain activation maps/tables, satisfying voxelwise task-evoked reporting. Participants are healthy humans and the contrasts are within-group. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are triggered. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study (I5) that reports whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects analyses with coordinates/tables (I7, I10). It includes at least one within-group task contrast (prediction under uncertainty > prediction under certainty) reported at group level (I8). The task elicits working-memory-related activations and the manuscript explicitly discusses involvement of mid-dorsolateral and posterior parietal areas underlying working memory, placing it within established executive function domains (working memory) (I6). Participants are healthy adults, so participant eligibility is acceptable (I9). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and a within-group contrast is present. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

Although this is an fMRI study of an executive-function working memory task (2-back) and reports a main effect of task and group/drug interactions, all reported voxelwise inferences were restricted to small-volume-corrected regions of interest (SVC). The document shows model estimates over the whole brain but inference was ROI-only (SVC, voxel-level) for every analysis. Therefore the study reports only SVC/ROI-corrected results with no reported whole-brain voxelwise task activation map, meeting exclusion criterion E3. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task fMRI), I6 (working memory), I8 (main effect of task vs baseline), I9 (clinical participants acceptable), I10 (results reported as coordinate peaks/tables). Inclusion criterion not met: I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked map reported).

This is an fMRI task-based study (Posner cueing) examining inhibition of return (a form of inhibitory attentional control), meeting the executive-function domain of inhibition. Analyses are whole-brain, voxelwise (MNI coordinates) with cluster-level correction, and report within-group contrasts (e.g., cued>uncued; long>short). Results are reported as peaks/tables. Participants are healthy adults. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study reports task fMRI of an executive function (N-back working memory) with within-group contrasts, but all extracted analyses are reported as region-of-interest (model fit over: region of interest) with no group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-activation maps provided. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task fMRI of executive function), I6 (working memory N-back), I8 (within-group contrasts), I9 (participant groups reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I7 (no whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analysis reported).

This is a task-based fMRI study of cognitive inhibition (executive function) reporting group-level, voxelwise whole-brain contrasts (multiple within-group contrasts for men and women) with cluster-level multiple comparison correction and coordinate peaks in tables. The task is an inhibition task (detect decreasing numbers) clearly within the inhibition domain. At least one within-group voxelwise contrast is reported (e.g., backward>forward, forward>motor control) for each participant group. Results are reported as whole-brain voxelwise analyses (model fit over whole brain) and peak coordinates are provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and it is empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

The paper reports an event-related fMRI study using a Sternberg verbal working memory task (an established executive function domain). Analyses were whole-brain, voxelwise group-level random-effects contrasts (model fit over whole brain; voxel-level threshold p<0.001) and report within-group task contrasts (high load > low load for encoding, maintenance, retrieval). Results are provided as coordinate tables. Participants are a healthy adult sample. Thus the study satisfies inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (working memory), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise results), I8 (within-group contrasts), I9 (participant groups acceptable), and I10 (results reported in tables). No exclusion criteria apply: not ROI-only (E3), not connectivity/resting-state only (E4), not only between-group contrasts (E5), and it is empirical human neuroimaging (not E6).

This fMRI study reports within-group, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts relevant to executive function (working memory). Analyses include Temporal production > control and Working memory > control (within-group contrasts), reported with whole-brain inference and tables of peak coordinates. Tasks include working memory (an established executive domain). The paper provides group-level voxelwise statistical maps (reported peaks/thresholds) and therefore meets whole-brain reporting. Although sample size is small (n=5), no exclusion criteria apply. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI task study), I6 (working memory = executive domain), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise results), I8 (within-group contrasts), I9 (participant groups acceptable), I10 (results reported in coordinate tables).

This is an empirical fMRI study of a task described as executive/reasoning (guessing) that implicates working-memory/executive processes. The NeuroStore record reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain GLM analyses with within-group task contrasts (e.g., guessing > reporting and reporting > guessing) and tables of peak coordinates. At least one analysis uses whole-brain inference and voxelwise thresholding; results are reported in tables. Therefore the study meets I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (task falls within executive/reasoning domain), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise results), I8 (within-group contrasts), I9 (participant group acceptable), and I10 (results reported as tables). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains within-group contrasts, empirical). Note: sample size is small (n=5) but not grounds for exclusion under given criteria.

This is an empirical PET study of dual-task/divided-attention performance, explicitly framed as examining executive functioning. It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (multiple within-group contrasts such as Dual task > single tasks; visual/auditory discrimination > baseline) with coordinates/tables of peaks. Participants are healthy adults. Results are voxelwise and not ROI-only, and task activations (not connectivity) are reported. Thus it meets inclusion criteria for a task-based executive-function PET study with whole-brain, within-group voxelwise contrasts and reported coordinates; no exclusion criteria apply.

The study reports task-based fMRI of an executive-function paradigm (emotional Stroop; cognitive control/inhibition) with within-group task contrasts (e.g., IC>CC, CC>IC). Multiple analyses explicitly state model fit and inference were performed voxelwise over the whole brain (satisfies whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked maps). Although some ROI analyses are present, whole-brain results are reported, so E3 does not apply. Participants are healthy humans and the design is task-based event-related fMRI. Thus inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 and I10 are met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met.

The study reports task-based fMRI of cognitive control during selective retrieval (free recall with competition), addressing executive control processes (inhibition/resolution of mnemonic competition). It includes at least one within-group, voxelwise, group-level task contrast (Analysis 17558403_analysis_2: retrieval success correct > failure; model fit over whole brain; voxel-level inference reported), satisfying whole-brain evidence. Participants are healthy adults (n=20). Results are reported as voxelwise peaks. No exclusion criteria (only ROI/connectivity/between-group) apply. Therefore all inclusion criteria required for this meta-analysis are met.

This fMRI task-switching study addresses executive control (I5) and cognitive flexibility (I6), reports within-group task contrasts (I8), reports results as coordinate tables/peaks (I10), and includes a qualifying participant group (healthy adults) (I9). However, NeuroStore indicates that inference was restricted to regions of interest for all analyses ("Inference restricted to: region of interest"), and thresholding for several contrasts is reported at a region/cluster level rather than as voxelwise whole-brain inference. Therefore the paper does not provide a group-level, voxelwise task activation map for whole-brain inference (I7 not met) and meets exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI/small-volume-corrected analyses reported). Because I7 is unmet and E3 applies, the study must be excluded.

This is an fMRI task-based study of working memory (2-back), an executive function domain. The document reports multiple group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (model fit over: whole brain; voxel-level thresholding and reported peak coordinates/tables). Several within-group task contrasts are reported for both healthy participants and schizophrenia patients (2-back > 0-back and degraded variants), satisfying the requirement for within-group task contrasts. Results are reported as coordinates/tables. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and it is empirical).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using a delay paradigm that interrogates maintenance/planning of forthcoming eye or hand movements (planning domain of executive function). The document shows group-level, voxelwise whole-brain SPM analyses (model fit over whole brain; several analyses report inference over whole brain and report peak coordinates/tables). Multiple within-group task contrasts are reported (simple effects and contralateral > ipsilateral within-group contrasts) with peak tables. Participants and BOLD measures are reported. Therefore the study meets I5 (fMRI task-based), I6 (task involves planning/maintenance), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise group analyses reported), I8 (within-group contrasts present), I9 (participant groups acceptable), and I10 (results reported as coordinate peaks/tables). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, empirical). Full text appears complete in this NeuroStore record.

This fMRI study uses a working-memory (Sternberg) task — an established executive function domain — and reports voxelwise whole-brain analyses (model fit over: whole brain; voxel-level inference, reported coordinate peaks/tables). The NeuroStore record includes within-group parametric modulation/one-sample t-test analyses for both controls and patients (analyses 2 and 3), satisfying the requirement for at least one within-group task contrast. Results are reported as peaks/tables (coordinates) and thus meet acceptable reporting formats. No exclusion criteria apply: analyses are not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, and within-group contrasts are present. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of visuo-spatial working memory/mental rotation (an executive function domain). It reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (model fit and inference over whole brain) and provides within-group task contrasts (mental rotation > passive viewing) for men and women and for menstrual phases. Coordinates/peaks and tables are reported. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for task-based executive-function fMRI studies with whole-brain voxelwise within-group contrasts, and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based whole-brain fMRI study using a three-stimulus oddball task involving target detection and distractor processing (vigilance/attention domain). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise within-group contrasts for Target and Distractor conditions with whole-brain inference and peak coordinates in tables. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Participant sample is healthy adults (n=13). The NeuroStore record provides sufficient detail for inclusion.

This PET study uses a task-based Stroop Color-Word paradigm (inhibition domain of executive function) and reports within-group contrast (threat words > neutral words). Model was fit over the whole brain with voxelwise inference (voxel-level p<0.01) and peak coordinates are reported in a table, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked results. Participants are healthy volunteers (n=6), and the study reports task activation maps rather than ROI-only or connectivity-only results. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Note: sample size is small (n=6), which may affect the study's weight in meta-analysis but does not disqualify it under the review criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of working memory (an executive function) using task-based paradigms (matching and reproduction tasks) which meets the review scope. It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise random-effects GLM analyses with corrected thresholding and cluster reporting, and provides coordinate peaks (Table 1). Multiple within-group task contrasts are reported (MAT > MAT CONT; REP > REP CONT; REP > MAT). Participants are healthy adults. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text is available in the supplied record, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of cognitive control (task switching and dual-task performance). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise, group-level within-group contrasts (e.g., task-switching > baseline; dual-task > task-switching) with corrected voxelwise thresholding and coordinates reported in tables (Table 1). At least one group-level voxelwise task activation map is present (fixed-effects group analyses, n=8). The tasks fall within executive function domains (cognitive flexibility/task switching). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains within-group contrasts, and is empirical). Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI task study of working memory manipulation (executive function). It reports group-level, voxelwise, whole-brain random-effects contrasts (e.g., Manipulation > Maintenance) with peak coordinates and cluster/voxel-level thresholding. Within-group task contrasts are present for numbers, syllables, and locations, satisfying executive-domain tasks and within-group requirements. Results are reported voxelwise and in tables. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains within-group contrasts, and is empirical).

This study reports task-based fMRI of a working-memory task (face/color cues) relevant to executive function (working memory), fulfilling I5 and I6. Analyses were fit over the whole brain with voxelwise inference (voxel-level corrected p), and peaks are reported in a table, satisfying I7 and I10. The dataset includes within-group contrasts (Remembering Color > rest; Anticipating Color > rest), meeting I8. Participant group (healthy adults, n=8) is acceptable per I9. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria, and is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This study reports whole-brain, voxelwise fMRI results from a Posner spatial cueing task in healthy participants and uses a within-subject crossover drug design. However, the only reported contrast in the provided record is a drug x task interaction (placebo < S‑ketamine across task conditions) rather than a within-group task activation contrast (e.g., task vs baseline or main effect of task) for any group or condition. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E5 (only a group/condition interaction reported) and does not satisfy inclusion criterion I8. It does satisfy I5, I7, I9 and I10 (task-based fMRI; whole-brain voxelwise analysis; participant group acceptable; results reported as coordinates/peaks). Full text is available in the record provided, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The paper reports task-based fMRI investigating spatial attention and working memory (executive function) and motor preparation. It includes group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLM contrasts (e.g., SAMP task > control; MPP task > control) with reported peak coordinates and tables, constituting within-group task contrasts. Results are clearly reported and meet reporting requirements. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 and I10, and no exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI Stroop study addresses executive function (inhibition) and reports a whole-brain voxelwise contrast (analysis_2), so it meets I5, I6, I7 (and I9/I10). However, the NeuroStore extraction indicates that reported statistical maps are either between-group contrasts or group×condition interactions (labels: ‘between-group’ or ‘interaction’) with no within-group task contrast reported for any group. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E5 (reports ONLY between-group contrasts/interactions with no within-group task activation). Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I7, I9, I10. Inclusion criterion not met: I8 (no within-group task contrast found). Based on these facts the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This study used event-related fMRI to investigate episodic associative memory encoding (discontinuous vs simultaneous associations). Although dorsolateral prefrontal cortex activity is reported, the task is episodic memory encoding/associative memory rather than an executive function/cognitive control task within established EF domains (e.g., working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Therefore it does not meet I5 (must assess executive function/cognitive control) and I6 (task must fall within established executive function domains). It does meet whole-brain voxelwise reporting (I7), reports within-group task contrasts (I8), includes an eligible participant group (I9), and presents whole-brain results in tables (I10). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, or between-group-only reporting).

This fMRI study uses a task-based paradigm assessing phonological control, a component of verbal working memory (an executive function domain), satisfying I5 and I6. The record reports multiple group-level, voxelwise whole-brain second-level analyses (e.g., Analyses 4–8, 9–10) with reported coordinate peaks, meeting I7 and I10. Several reported contrasts are within-group task contrasts (e.g., Pseudo-English > English; Remembered > Forgotten), satisfying I8. Participants are a within-group adult sample (n=17–20), so I9 is also met. No exclusion criteria apply: the paper reports whole-brain voxelwise results (not ROI-only), is not connectivity-only, and includes within-group contrasts rather than only between-group effects. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for a meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This fMRI task study reports within-group, voxelwise whole-brain task activation maps related to cognitive control. Evidence: bold fMRI measure (n=10), group-level voxelwise GLM with a main effect of Congruency inferred over the whole brain (cluster-level whole-brain correction) and reported peak coordinates; also a ROI SVC for an interaction but whole-brain results are present. Tasks probe cognitive control (preparation for semantic vs phonological judgments; unconscious priming affecting control), which fits executive function domains. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise fMRI analyses of a task that requires concealment of information and stimulus-response control (guilty knowledge test), including an omnibus within-subject ANOVA comparing item types and parametric within-group associations with reaction time and SCR. This maps onto executive functions (inhibition/stimulus-response control and working memory processes are discussed by the authors). Results are reported as whole-brain peaks/tables. Therefore it meets the review’s fMRI task requirement, executive-function domain, whole-brain voxelwise reporting, and includes within-group task contrasts and coordinate tables. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete in the record.

The study is an fMRI task-based study with group-level, voxelwise within-group contrasts reported (meets I5, I7, I8). Participant group is acceptable (I9) and whole-brain results are reported as coordinate tables (I10). However, the task is a discourse coherence/inference judgment (sentence-pair coherence ratings) and does not fall within the meta-analysis’ required executive function domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation) — therefore it fails I6. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Conclusion: EXCLUDE because I6 (task within established executive function domains) is not satisfied.

This is an empirical PET study reporting task-evoked activations for executive-function tasks (2-back, 1-back, random-number generation and related memory tasks). Whole-brain voxelwise models were fit (Model fit over: whole brain) and voxelwise, group-level within-group contrasts are reported (e.g., 2-Back > Random-number generation; 2-Back > Reading), with corrected inference and reported peak coordinates. Results are suitable for inclusion in a meta-analysis of executive function activations: working memory tasks clearly map to the executive domain, whole-brain voxelwise maps and within-group contrasts are present, and coordinates/tables are reported. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Document appears to contain sufficient extracted results for screening (full text available in this record).

This is an fMRI task-based study of task-switching (cognitive flexibility), an executive function. It reports a within-group contrast (transition cue > task cue) tested with a group-level, voxelwise random-effects one-sample t-test across participants, with whole-brain model fit and reported peak coordinates (Talairach). Thus it provides whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked activation maps for an executive task. It is empirical human fMRI data and not ROI-only or connectivity-only. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5–I10 and violates no exclusion criteria.

The study reports task-based fMRI of an executive function domain (working memory) using an event-related WM task with novel faces, meeting I5 and I6. Analyses were group-level, voxelwise random-effects whole-brain models with corrected voxelwise inference and reported peak coordinates, satisfying I7 and I10. Multiple contrasts are explicitly described as within-group simple effects for the WM delay and encoding periods, meeting I8. Participant group is reported (n=8), which meets I9 (any participant group allowed). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only (E3), not connectivity/resting-state only (E4), and not only between-group contrasts (E5); the paper is empirical (not E6). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and violates none. Detailed extractions show whole-brain, within-group WM delay contrasts, and reported peaks for hippocampal/parahippocampal activation supporting inclusion.

The study reports an event-related fMRI experiment of verbal maintenance (phonological rehearsal), which falls within the executive function domain of working memory. It provides a group-level, voxelwise whole-brain contrast (Rote > Fixation) using a one-sample t-test (n=16) and reports peak coordinates (Table 2). This is a within-group task contrast against an implicit baseline (fixation). Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10). No exclusion criteria apply: results are whole-brain voxelwise (not ROI-only), not connectivity-only, and include within-group contrasts (not only between-group). Full text is available in the provided NeuroStore record, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

The NeuroStore record indicates all analyses were ROI-based ("Model fit over: region of interest" and "Inference restricted to: region of interest") with reported regions (lateral PFC, dorsal ACC, lateral cerebellum). No group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map is reported, so the study fails inclusion criterion I7 and meets exclusion E3 (ROI-only results). The study does meet I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (working memory executive task), I8 (within-group task contrast/cross-subject regression), and I9 (participant group reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I7 (whole-brain voxelwise evidence). fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study is a task-based PET FDG investigation of a vigilance (oddball) task, which falls within the executive function domain (I5,I6). The NeuroStore record shows multiple reported voxelwise peaks in Tables 2–4 (coordinate tables), indicating whole-brain voxelwise results (I7,I10). The record explicitly includes a within-group simple effects analysis for the MA group (analysis_1), satisfying the requirement for a within-group task contrast (I8). Participant groups include clinical MA-dependent subjects, which is acceptable (I9). Although some reported analyses are ROI-based regressions, the study does not report only ROI results, so exclusion E3 is not met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and does not violate exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI task-based empirical study that reports within-group, voxelwise whole-brain contrasts relevant to executive control. The task required participants to choose when to lie or tell the truth (spoken responses), which involves suppression of a prepotent truthful response and thus maps onto the inhibition/executive control domain. The NeuroStore record shows whole-brain model estimation and voxel-level thresholding, and reports group-level within-subject contrasts (Lie>Truth; Comply>Defy; combined contrasts) with coordinate tables (reported peaks). Participants are healthy adults (n=17). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I5 (fMRI task-based), I6 (task within executive/inhibition domain), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise results), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (participant group acceptable), and I10 (results reported as coordinates). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears available via the provided NeuroStore record (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an event-related fMRI study using the Stroop color-word task (an inhibition/cognitive-control executive function task), reporting group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects analyses and within-group contrasts (e.g., incongruent > congruent, congruent > neutral). Results are reported as coordinate tables/peaks (Tables I & II). Participants (n=18) are an acceptable sample. All required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group contrasts, and is empirical).

This study reports a whole-brain, voxelwise between-group interaction (hypertensives > normotensives: parametric modulation by spatial memory load) from a spatial N-back task using cerebral blood flow measures. It satisfies inclusion criteria I5 (task-based PET/perfusion imaging), I6 (working memory executive task), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise analysis), I9 (clinical participant groups acceptable), and I10 (results reported as peak coordinates). However, no within-group task contrasts are reported in the NeuroStore record—the only reported analysis is a between-group interaction—so it fails I8. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E5 (reports only between-group contrast/group×condition interaction with no within-group task activation). No other analyses were listed in the document.

The NeuroStore record indicates all reported voxelwise analyses were performed within a region-of-interest (Model fit over: region of interest) with no whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps reported. This violates inclusion criterion I7 (requirement for whole-brain voxelwise evidence) and meets exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI/SVC analyses reported). The study does meet other inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (inhibition Go/No-Go task), I8 (within-group task contrast reported: correct rejections > hits), and I9 (participant group reported). Because the review requires at least one whole-brain voxelwise within-group activation map and none is present here, the study is excluded.

NeuroStore extraction shows this is an fMRI study of inhibition (Anti-Saccade task) with voxel-by-voxel ANOVA and reported peak coordinates, so it meets I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (inhibition executive domain), I7 (voxelwise/whole-brain inference reported), I9 (developmental participants acceptable) and I10 (results reported as coordinate peaks/tables). However all analyses extracted are labeled as omnibus, between-group contrasts (Age group × time, Age group × time × response type, etc.), and no within-group task activation contrasts (e.g., task vs baseline or correct vs error reported as group-level within-group contrasts) are present in the document. Therefore exclusion criterion E5 applies: the record reports only between-group/group×condition contrasts with no within-group task contrast for any group. Full text is available in this derived record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This fMRI study reports voxelwise, whole-brain, group-level within-group task activation contrasts for an executive function task (working memory 1-back) in both Alzheimer’s patients and healthy elderly. The NeuroStore record shows multiple within-group activation>baseline contrasts (AD baseline, AD after treatment, elderly) and paired contrasts; results are reported as peak coordinates (tables). Therefore inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (working memory within executive domains), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise analyses), I8 (within-group task contrasts present), I9 (participant groups acceptable) and I10 (results reported as coordinates/tables) are met. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) are triggered. Full text appears complete in the provided record.

This is a task-based fMRI study of executive control (inhibition vs action), meeting the construct of executive function. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (model fit over whole brain, voxel-level thresholding) and within-group contrasts (e.g., INH > REST; ACT and INH conjunctions) with reported peak coordinates. Results are presented in tables. Participants are human (healthy adults). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Therefore all inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

This fMRI study uses task-based paradigms (N-back working memory, CPT attention, sentence completion) satisfying I5 and I6. It also reports within-group task contrasts (e.g., 1-3 back > 0-back cross-subject regression), meeting I8. However, every reported analysis was fit and inference-restricted to a priori ROIs (NeuroStore notes: Model fit over: region of interest; Inference restricted to: region of interest). No group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task activation maps are reported, so the study fails inclusion criterion I7. Because it reports only ROI analyses with no voxelwise results, exclusion criterion E3 applies. No other exclusion criteria appear met. Therefore the paper must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an event-related fMRI study of working memory (verbal rehearsal/distraction), reporting a within-group task contrast (Mem-Dist > Mem-NoDist) estimated with a group-level GLM (one-sample t-test). NeuroStore reports voxel-level thresholding (corrected, voxel-level), reported MNI peak coordinates, and inference over the whole brain, indicating a group-level voxelwise task activation map. These features satisfy inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (working memory = executive function domain), I8 (within-group task contrast), I7 (voxelwise whole-brain evidence — supported by voxel-level thresholding and reported peaks), I9 (participant group acceptable), and I10 (results reported as coordinates). Although the record notes “Model fit over: region of interest,” the presence of whole-brain inference, voxel-level thresholding and reported MNI peaks supports inclusion rather than an ROI-only report. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met.

This study is excluded because it reports only between-group contrasts and no within-group task activation contrasts. (a) Exclusion criteria met: E5 (reports ONLY between-group contrasts with no within-group task activation contrast). (b) Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI study), I6 (includes an executive-function task: Sternberg working memory), I7 (model fit over whole brain; voxelwise results with reported peaks), I10 (results reported as coordinate peaks/tables). (c) Inclusion criteria NOT met: I8 (no within-group task contrast reported for any group), I9 (conditional participant-group allowance not satisfied because no within-group contrasts are provided). The NeuroStore record shows all reported contrasts are controls > patients (between-group) from joint ICA component loadings; no within-group task-vs-baseline or task-condition contrasts are provided. Therefore the study does not meet the requirement for a within-group task activation map and must be excluded.

This is an fMRI study using a Stroop color-word task (inhibition domain of executive function), with whole-brain voxelwise GLM analyses reported. NeuroStore shows model fit over the whole brain, Talairach coordinates and reported peak tables (Table tbl1) for within-group contrasts (SI>CO and RI>SI). The task is a task-based paradigm targeting executive control, participants are a within-group sample (n=14), and results are reported as voxelwise activations (coordinates). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and not only between-group contrasts). Therefore all required inclusion criteria are satisfied.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using a card-guessing/gambling paradigm that explicitly involves learning, strategy acquisition and working-memory/uncertainty management (executive processes). Whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses are reported (model fit over: whole brain) and peak coordinates/tables are provided. The paper includes within-group task contrasts/repeated-measures ANOVAs (e.g., processing of gains vs losses in exploratory vs proficiency phases), satisfying the requirement for at least one within-group task contrast. Participant groups are healthy humans; any participant group is acceptable. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and within-group contrasts are present (so not only between-group). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This PET study used a simple motor execution/drawing task (intermanual transfer of training) rather than an established executive function paradigm (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Therefore it does not meet inclusion criteria I5 and I6. The study does meet I7 (whole-brain, voxelwise analyses reported), I8 (within-group task contrasts such as rTL>rOL and rOL>rest), I9 (participant groups reported), and I10 (results reported as coordinate tables). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an empirical task-based PET study of executive function (random number generation), meeting inclusion criterion I5. The RNG task falls within established executive domains (initiation/cognitive control), satisfying I6. The NeuroStore record reports whole-brain, voxelwise GLM analyses with voxel-level thresholding and corrected results, meeting I7. Multiple within-group task contrasts are explicitly reported for both patients and healthy controls (e.g., RNG > COUNT), satisfying I8 and I9. Results are reported as foci/tables (tbl1–tbl3), so whole-brain results are available in reported coordinates, meeting I10. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This fMRI event-related delayed face recognition study measures decision period activity during a working memory task (delayed recognition), fitting the executive-function domain of working memory. It reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses (Talairach coordinates, tables of peaks) and provides within-group task contrasts (match > nonmatch and nonmatch > match). Results are reported in tables of coordinates. Participant sample (n=9) is acceptable per inclusion rules. No exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study investigates economic decision-making (brand choice; implicit memory influence), not executive functions. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (whole-brain, voxelwise results reported across multiple analyses including 2-level random-effects maps and peak coordinates), I8 (several within-group task contrasts are reported, e.g. DD > TD and TD > DD in group-specific analyses), I9 (healthy participant groups reported), and I10 (results reported as tables of coordinates/peaks). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I5 (study does not assess executive function or cognitive control using an executive-task paradigm) and I6 (task does not fall within listed executive domains such as working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). No exclusion criteria from E3–E6 apply. Therefore exclude because key scope criteria (I5 and I6) are not satisfied.

This is an fMRI study using a delayed-match-to-sample task (working memory), reporting group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (second-level one-sample t-tests and repeated-measures ANOVAs) with voxelwise thresholding and peak coordinates in tables. Multiple within-group task contrasts are reported (e.g., object delay>location delay; ODMS delay>OCON delay; familiar>trial-unique), satisfying within-group voxelwise activation requirements. Participants are a healthy adult sample (n=17). Results are reported as whole-brain voxelwise maps and coordinates. No exclusion criteria apply: analyses are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and include within-group contrasts. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective.

This is an fMRI task-based study explicitly examining cognitive control/response conflict during intentional false responding, which maps onto executive function (inhibition/response conflict). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (model fit and inference over whole brain) with voxelwise FDR thresholding and tables of peak coordinates. Multiple within-group contrasts are reported (e.g., FALSE > TRUE, AUTO > NONAUTO, FALSE AUTO > TRUE AUTO). Participants are healthy adults. Therefore all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis: it is an fMRI task-based empirical study of executive function (reasoning and a match-to-sample working memory task) (I5,I6). Analyses were voxelwise, with the model fit and inference performed over the whole brain and results reported as peak coordinates (MNI), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements (I7,I10). Multiple within-group task contrasts are reported (R>M, M>R, M>Mc), so a within-group task contrast is available (I8). Participant group is an eligible cohort (n=19 young adults) (I9). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and within-group contrasts are provided. Therefore the study should be included in the meta-analysis.

This fMRI study reports within-group, voxelwise whole-brain task activation contrasts for antisaccade (inhibition) and saccade tasks in healthy participants. The antisaccade task is a canonical inhibition/executive-control paradigm. Group-level, voxelwise results are reported (tables of peaks) for contrasts including antisaccade>rest, saccade>rest, and antisaccade>visually guided saccades. The analyses were whole-brain and voxel-level, satisfying the requirement for voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps. Therefore all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study investigates task-switching (cognitive flexibility), uses a task-based BOLD paradigm, and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts (one-sample t-test across subjects) with voxelwise thresholding (p<0.001). It includes a within-group contrast (switch > repeat) and an interaction contrast, and reports peak coordinates in Talairach. All required inclusion criteria for executive-function task activations are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical).

The study reports an event-related fMRI, task-based investigation of semantic interference in a picture-word paradigm that the authors interpret as involving selective attention/response suppression (inhibition), placing it within established executive-function domains (inhibition). Analysis 11668653_analysis_0 is a within-group contrast (semantically-related vs lexical control) estimated voxelwise over the whole brain, with whole-brain inference for several regions and reported peak coordinates (Table). Thus it provides group-level, voxelwise task-evoked activation maps. All required inclusion criteria are met (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text is sufficiently represented by the NeuroStore record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study reports a task-based fMRI Go/No-Go inhibition paradigm (executive function domain) with BOLD measures. It includes a group-level, voxelwise within-group contrast (Analysis 16202396_analysis_0: Go/NoGo > Go), modeled as a random-effects one-sample t-test with whole-brain model fit and reported peak coordinates (Table tbl1), satisfying requirements for whole-brain voxelwise task activation. Although some genotype comparisons used small-volume correction, at least one qualifying whole-brain within-group task contrast is present. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (an executive function) that reports whole-brain, voxelwise, within-group task contrasts (multiple contrasts of Remembering/Anticipating > resting). Results are reported as coordinate tables (Talairach). Although the sample is small (n=8) and analyses used a fixed-effects model, the inclusion criteria do not exclude these features. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis requirements for task domain, whole-brain voxelwise analyses, and within-group contrasts.

This fMRI study uses a Stroop-like emotional conflict task and reports within-group contrasts and connectivity, meeting I5 (task-based fMRI of cognitive control), I6 (conflict/inhibition domain), I8 (within-group task contrasts), and I9 (healthy adult participants). However, all reported analyses were ROI-based: “Model fit over: region of interest” and “Inference restricted to: region of interest” (amygdala, frontal masks, rostral cingulate). No group-level, voxelwise whole-brain activation maps are reported. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI/small-volume analyses reported) and does not meet I7 (whole-brain voxelwise evidence).

The NeuroStore record describes an empirical fMRI study of a task labeled 'executive and reasoning' that manipulates a brief reflective process ('refresh'). It reports a within-group voxelwise contrast (refresh > read; repeat) with model fit over the whole brain and reported peak coordinates (Table 2), satisfying whole-brain, voxelwise reporting. The task falls within executive-function component processes (selection/refreshing), and results are task-evoked activation maps rather than ROI-only or connectivity-only analyses. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the study meets all listed inclusion criteria for the review.

The NeuroStore record indicates this is an fMRI study of saccade tasks (pro/anti-saccades) assessing preparatory set, which maps onto executive function (inhibition/intention). A within-group task contrast (pro-saccades vs fixation) is reported. However, the extracted analyses show model fit over region-of-interest (FEF and IPS defined by functional localizer) and ROI-restricted results (corrected thresholds reported). No group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task activation maps are reported in the document. Therefore the study reports only ROI analyses and lacks voxelwise whole-brain activation results required by I7, meeting exclusion criterion E3. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI), I6 (task in executive domain), I8 (within-group contrast), I9 (participant group acceptable). Inclusion criterion not met: I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise map reported). Full text appears accessible in the record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The report indicates ROI-based analyses only (Model fit over: region of interest; Thresholding: region-level), so no group-level voxelwise whole-brain task activation map is available. This triggers exclusion E3 (only ROI/SVC analyses). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI study of executive function - N-back working memory), I6 (task falls within working memory domain), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported: 3-back > fixation and fixation > 3-back), I9 (participant group is acceptable), and I10 (results reported as peaks/coordinates in a table). Inclusion criterion not met: I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise analysis reported). Therefore the study is excluded under E3.

This is an event-related fMRI study using a working memory task (emotional and nonemotional distractors) with group-level, voxelwise second-level random-effects analyses reported over the whole brain (model fit over: whole brain) and voxelwise thresholding (p<0.001). Multiple within-group task contrasts are reported (Scram > Emo, Scram > Neu, Neu > Emo) with tables of reported peaks. These facts satisfy the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for fMRI/PET task-based executive function studies (working memory), whole-brain voxelwise results, and within-group contrasts. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group contrasts, and is empirical).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using the Stroop Color-Word task (an established inhibition/executive control paradigm). It reports group-level, voxelwise analyses fit over the whole brain (coordinate space: Talairach) with thresholded peak tables (Table tbl1) for Stroop > resting baseline (GE-BOLD) and resting baseline > Stroop (p-fMRI perfusion), satisfying a within-group task contrast. Results include reported peaks and quantitative CBF change estimates. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The NeuroStore record indicates only between-group/group×condition interaction contrasts comparing estrogen and placebo (e.g., 'placebo; target > estrogen' and 'estrogen; target > placebo' labeled as [interaction, between-group]). No within-group task activation contrasts (e.g., targets>baseline or task>implicit baseline reported for either group) are listed. Therefore Exclusion E5 applies: the paper reports only between-group contrasts/interactions with no within-group task maps. The study does meet several inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (oddball vigilance task = executive domain: vigilance), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise results reported), I9 (participant group acceptable), and I10 (coordinates/tables of peaks reported). Inclusion I8 (at least one within-group task contrast) is not met. Full text appears available (derived NeuroStore record), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study reports task-based fMRI contrasts that probe blink inhibition (a form of motor inhibition) and spontaneous blinking. It includes group-level, voxelwise whole-brain random-effects analyses and reports peak coordinates in tables. Specific qualifying items: (a) a within-group contrast for blink inhibition > baseline and for spontaneous blinking > closed eye are reported; (b) the task involves inhibition (falls within executive function domains); (c) analyses were whole-brain and voxelwise at the group level; (d) results are reported as peak coordinates/tables. No exclusion criteria apply: the study does not report only ROI/SVC, connectivity-only, or only between-group contrasts, and it is empirical human fMRI data. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for an executive-function activation meta-analysis.

The study reports an event-related fMRI investigation of response inhibition (an executive function) using a within-group contrast (lures; simple effect) analyzed with a one-sample t-test in n=14. The model was fit over the whole brain and inference was performed over the whole brain, with voxelwise thresholding and reported peak coordinates (Table 1). This satisfies inclusion criteria: task-based fMRI of executive function (I5), inhibition domain (I6), whole-brain voxelwise group-level results (I7), a within-group task contrast (I8), acceptable participant group (I9), and reporting of whole-brain results in a table of coordinates (I10). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical).

This is an empirical fMRI study that reports within-group, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts including a two-back working memory > rest contrast (executive function). Results are whole-brain GLM with voxel-level thresholding and reported peak coordinates (tables). Participants are healthy adults. The methods and reported peaks satisfy criteria for task-based executive-function activation (I5, I6), whole-brain voxelwise results (I7), within-group contrasts (I8), inclusion of acceptable participant group (I9), and coordinate/table reporting (I10). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and empirical data are reported).

This is an fMRI task-based study using the PVSAT (working memory/mental arithmetic), satisfying executive-function domain (I5,I6). NeuroStore shows model fit over the whole brain with voxelwise thresholding (p<0.001), meeting whole-brain evidence (I7). The abstract explicitly reports within-group activations ("In controls, the PVSAT elicited a fronto-parietal network..."), satisfying the requirement for at least one within-group task contrast (I8). Participant groups include clinical (CIS, CDMS) and healthy controls, which are acceptable (I9). Results are reported in text/tables/peaks (coordinate tables present), consistent with acceptable reporting formats (I10). Although the extracted analyses list between-group contrasts, the abstract and reported peaks/tables indicate within-group task activation maps were evaluated. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, only between-group contrasts without any within-group, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

The study reports an event-related fMRI Go/No-Go task (response inhibition), fitting executive function domains. It includes a group-level, voxelwise within-group contrast (Analysis 16650836_analysis_0: STOPS > ongoing Go trials; model fit and inference over whole brain; one-sample t-test; n=71) satisfying whole-brain evidence and the within-group contrast requirements. Results are reported as cluster peaks/tables. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical).

This fMRI study reports task-evoked, within-group, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts of a task that recruits executive resources (working memory/executive reasoning) during quantifier comprehension. It uses BOLD fMRI, random-effects t-tests, and reports voxelwise peaks in tables. At least one contrast is a within-group task contrast (proposition and response > proposition alone). Results were estimated over the whole brain and reported voxelwise (thresholds/peaks provided). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is a task-based fMRI study reporting within-group, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts for deductive (relational and conditional) reasoning. However, the meta-analysis requires tasks to assess executive function domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Deductive/reasoning tasks reported here are not among the specified executive function domains and the abstract/methods do not indicate the task targeted those executive processes. All other methodological inclusion criteria are met (whole-brain voxelwise analyses, within-group contrasts, participant reporting, coordinate reporting). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study must be excluded for not meeting I5/I6.

The study reports a whole-brain, voxelwise, within-group fMRI contrast (test > control) with reported peak coordinates, so it meets I7, I8, I9 and I10. However, the task is a recall/recognition Word Memory Test (delayed recognition of word pairs), which is an episodic memory task and not an executive function task as defined by the review (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Therefore it does not meet I5 (fMRI study assessing executive function) nor I6 (task within established executive function domains). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Because key inclusion criteria I5 and I6 are not satisfied, the study must be excluded.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of executive/reasoning processes (Raven-like relational reasoning) that manipulates relational complexity and distractor load. It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain contrasts (model fit over: whole brain) and provides coordinate tables/peaks for multiple within-group task contrasts (e.g., complexity level 4 > 0; distractor level 4 > 1; other within-group contrasts). The paradigm involves executive demands (relational integration/working-memory demands), satisfying the review objective of executive function activations. Results are voxelwise (not ROI-only) and include thresholding and reported peaks. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10). No exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study reports whole-brain, voxelwise within-group task contrasts (PASAT > rest and recall > rest) for both patients and controls, using SPM99. The PASAT is an established executive-domain task (working memory/sustained attention/vigilance), satisfying the review’s executive-function scope. At least one analysis is a group-level voxelwise task-evoked map (model fit over: whole brain) and within-group contrasts are explicitly reported for both groups. Results are reported as coordinate tables and cluster/voxelwise thresholding, fulfilling reporting requirements. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and within-group contrasts are present).

This PET study reports a task-based executive function paradigm (Stroop Color-Word Task) and several within-group task contrasts (e.g. incongruent > neutral; medial frontal TMS (mfTMS) > midline parietal control (MPC) TMS) — satisfying I5 and I6. The record includes group-level, voxelwise whole-brain statistical maps for Stroop-related contrasts (analyses 13, 14 and 8), corrected for multiple comparisons, thus meeting I7 and I8. Participants are healthy volunteers (I9) and results are reported in tables/analyses (I10). Although some analyses are ROI/small-volume-corrected, the presence of whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts prevents exclusion under E3. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Therefore the study should be included for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

The record reports a task-based fMRI study with group-level, voxelwise within-group contrasts (e.g., Rotation>Control, Intact>Scrambled) and reported whole-brain peaks. Critically, one analysis is labeled as an N-Back Task (working memory), which falls within the executive function domains specified (I6). Whole-brain, voxelwise inference is reported (FDR; voxel-level) and peaks/tables are provided. Participants are healthy adults and within-group contrasts are used. Therefore the study meets fMRI task-based requirement (I5), contains an EF task (working memory; I6), provides whole-brain voxelwise group-level results (I7), includes within-group contrasts (I8), has an acceptable participant sample (I9), and reports coordinate/table results (I10). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group contrasts, and is empirical). Note: there is minor ambiguity in labeling of the object-decision analysis as “N-Back Task,” but we accept the dataset extraction as the study record for screening purposes.

This fMRI study reports multiple whole-brain, voxelwise, group-level within-subject contrasts (e.g., run 8 > run 1; Day 2 > Day 1; transfer contrasts), with results reported as peak coordinates — satisfying whole-brain reporting (I7), within-group contrasts (I8), participant eligibility (I9), and acceptable reporting formats (I10). However, the experimental goal and tasks center on motor skill learning and visuomotor/spatial representations of typing sequences rather than assessing an established executive function or cognitive-control process per se. Although the authors interpret some activations as related to planning, the paradigm is a motor-sequence learning task rather than a task designed to probe executive-function domains listed in I6. Therefore I5 (study assessing executive function/cognitive control) and I6 (task falls within established executive function domains) are not met. No exclusion criteria apply.

Both reported analyses were region-of-interest (ROI) restricted: 'Model fit over: region of interest' and 'Inference restricted to: region of interest' (left IFG). The review requires at least one group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task activation map (I7). Because no voxelwise whole-brain results are reported and all inference was ROI-limited, the study meets exclusion criterion E3. The study does meet several inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (includes working memory task within executive domains), I8 (within-group contrasts reported), I9 (healthy adult participant group reported), and I10 (coordinates/peaks reported). However I7 is not met, so the study must be excluded.

This study reports a task-based fMRI experiment of visual target selection involving spatial inhibition (an inhibition-related executive process). It provides group-level, voxelwise whole-brain random-effects GLM results (model fit and inference over whole brain) with reported peak coordinates and a within-group contrast comparing targets in previously inhibited vs new locations. Sample and task details are reported. No exclusion criteria are met.

This fMRI study uses a Stroop counting task probing cognitive control/inhibition (meets I5 and I6). Analyses were fit and inferred over the whole brain with voxelwise contrasts reported as peak coordinates and cluster-level correction (meets I7 and I10). A within-group task contrast (incongruent > congruent) is explicitly reported (meets I8). Participant group (healthy adults) is acceptable (meets I9). No exclusion criteria apply: results are whole-brain voxelwise (not ROI-only), not connectivity-only, and a within-group contrast is present. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

This fMRI study uses the Multi-Source Interference Task (an executive/cognitive control task) in healthy adults and reports group-level, voxelwise task activation contrasts. Analysis details show group-averaged voxel-wise t-tests with the model fit over the whole brain and reported coordinate peaks (Tables), and a within-group contrast comparing interference vs control blocks. Although inference was reported as restricted to a region of interest in one analysis, the presence of whole-brain model fitting and voxelwise group results (reported peaks) means this is not ROI-only. All required inclusion criteria are met (I5: task-based fMRI; I6: executive function domain - interference/cognitive control; I7: group-level voxelwise map; I8: within-group task contrast; I9: participant group acceptable; I10: whole-brain results reported as coordinates). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears available via the NeuroStore record provided.

The study is an fMRI study of an executive (working memory) task (I5, I6 met) but reports only multivariate functional connectivity (ICA component loadings) and between-group contrasts (controls > pre-HD). No within-group task activation contrasts (task > baseline or similar) are reported for any group. Therefore it meets exclusion criteria E4 (connectivity-only analyses without a task activation map) and E5 (only between-group contrasts with no within-group task activation contrast). Although model fitting was performed over the whole brain, the reported results are connectivity component loadings and group comparisons rather than voxelwise task-evoked activation maps; thus the study does not satisfy I7 or I8 (and I9’s conditional requirement).

This PET study reports whole-brain, voxelwise, within-group contrasts (multiple NR/TR/RS contrasts) and tables of coordinates, so it meets I7 (whole-brain voxelwise results), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (any participant group allowed), and I10 (results reported as coordinate tables). However the task is a free-recall episodic memory paradigm (recall of abstract designs) rather than a task in established executive-function domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Although the authors discuss attentional/control involvement, the primary manipulation assesses memory retrieval/learning, not a canonical executive function task. Therefore it does not satisfy I5/I6 (assessing executive function/cognition within specified domains), so it must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete in the record.

This fMRI study uses the PASAT, an executive working-memory task, and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level activation contrasts. Analysis 15543553_analysis_0 is a within-group (one-sample) PASAT > REPEAT contrast in healthy controls (whole-brain, voxelwise, random-effects), satisfying the requirement for a within-group task activation map. The study also reports between-group comparisons, but at least one qualifying within-group contrast is present. Results are reported as coordinates and thresholding details. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical, and includes within-group contrasts). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This fMRI study presents whole-brain, within-group task contrasts and reports voxelwise/group-level results, but the task is mental arithmetic (multiplication and subtraction) rather than an established executive-function paradigm. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I8 (multiple within-group task contrasts), I9 (participant group reported; healthy adults), I10 (results reported in tables of coordinates). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (tasks do not clearly fall within the listed executive-function domains such as working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation), and therefore I5 (study does not primarily assess executive function/cognitive control using an established EF task) is not satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered by the provided document. Because I6 (and consequentially I5) are not met, the study is excluded from the executive-function meta-analysis.
