The study reports task-based fMRI (BOLD) including a visual short-term memory (working memory) task, which is an executive function domain. It includes group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (analyses 0 and 1: whole-brain model fit and voxel-level FDR inference) and within-group contrasts/parametric modulations (set-size effects and parametric regressors). Participants are healthy adults. Whole-brain results are reported (tables of peaks). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and it is empirical). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and should be included in the meta-analysis of executive-function task activations.

Although this is an fMRI task study with voxelwise whole-brain results and within-group contrasts, the task is a gambling/reward-processing decision-making paradigm focused on reward feedback. The review requires studies to assess executive function/cognitive control within established domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). The Card-Guessing (Gambling) task here assesses reward processing/decision-making rather than one of the specified executive domains, so inclusion criteria I5 and I6 are not satisfied. The study does meet I7 (whole-brain voxelwise results), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported), I9 (participant groups acceptable), and I10 (results reported in tables). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore the study is excluded for failure to meet the executive-function domain requirement.

This is a task-based fMRI study of the Sternberg item recognition task (working memory), an executive function domain. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise within-group contrasts (visual search > control; memory search > control) with whole-brain model fitting and voxelwise thresholding (p<0.001, cluster extent 10) and tables of peak coordinates. Thus it provides qualifying whole-brain task activation maps. Although an ROI conjunction analysis is reported, it does not preclude inclusion because whole-brain results are available. No exclusion criteria (only ROI results, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This PET study reports task-based executive function (Stroop inhibition) activations and includes whole-brain, voxelwise within-group contrasts for both patient and healthy groups (incongruent > congruent; Analyses 1 and 2: model fit over whole brain, peaks reported). The modality is PET (cerebral blood flow), task falls under inhibition (an executive function), and results include coordinate peaks/tables. Although a between-group ROI analysis is reported, it is not the only analysis: whole-brain within-group contrasts are available, satisfying voxelwise map requirement. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, and includes within-group contrasts). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective and should be INCLUDED.

This study reports task-based fMRI using a modified Stroop task (executive/inhibition domain), meeting I5 and I6. It provides whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (model fit over whole brain) and reports within-group task contrasts (Stroop activation > rest) for controls and patients (Analyses 0 and 1), satisfying I7 and I8. Participant groups include healthy and clinical (schizophrenia) samples (I9). Whole-brain results are reported as peak coordinates in tables (I10). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, and within-group contrasts are present (E3–E5 not applicable); the paper is empirical (E6 not applicable). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and violates none, and is appropriate for inclusion in the meta-analysis of executive-function task activations.

This fMRI study used an antisaccade task (inhibition of a reflexive saccade and generation of a volitional saccade), which is a canonical executive function (inhibition) paradigm. It reports a group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise within-group contrast (standard antisaccade > fixation baseline) analyzed with a random-effects 1-sample t-test and reports Talairach coordinates (Table 2). Participants: n=17 healthy adults. Thresholding and reported peaks are provided. Thus the study meets inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function), I6 (inhibition domain), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise group analysis), I8 (within-group task contrast), I9 (participant group acceptable), and I10 (whole-brain results reported as coordinates). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, and empirical task activation data are reported). Full text appears sufficiently represented by the NeuroStore record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is a task-based fMRI study using a challenging working-memory/mental-arithmetic task (modified PASAT) — an executive function domain — and reports voxelwise, whole-brain group-level results (tables of peak coordinates). NeuroStore extraction indicates whole-brain model fitting and whole-brain inference with voxelwise thresholding (reported peak tables for PASAT; Analysis 17408973_analysis_2 lists 12 peaks; cross-subject regressions and group contrasts are also voxelwise). At least one within-group task contrast is reported (within-group PASAT main effects and reported peaks), satisfying the requirement for a within-group activation map. Results are not ROI-only or connectivity-only. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 and I10 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study using a Go/No-Go task (inhibition domain) with voxelwise, group-level whole-brain contrasts (e.g., FA>Rest, CR>Rest) reported with voxel-level FDR thresholding and peaks in MNI space. Within-group task contrasts are present. Participants are a human sample (n=10). Results are reported as whole-brain maps/coordinates. Thus it satisfies all inclusion criteria for task-based executive-function fMRI with whole-brain, within-group voxelwise results. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete in the provided record.

This fMRI study investigates language control/selection during picture naming in bilinguals, which operationalizes cognitive control processes (language selection, inhibition of non-target language, and switching) consistent with executive function domains (inhibition/cognitive flexibility). The NeuroStore record reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain random-effects analyses with reported peak coordinates and multiple within-group task contrasts (e.g., L1 vs L2, context contrasts), satisfying requirements for voxelwise within-group activation maps. Participants are healthy adults. Results are reported as coordinate tables. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group contrasts, and is empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10) and should be included.

This is an fMRI task-based study (Simon task) probing interference control/inhibition—an executive function domain. The NeuroStore record reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (Model fit over: whole brain; Inference over: whole brain) for within-group contrasts (IG > neutral; CG > neutral) with reported peak coordinates/tables. Thus the study provides task-evoked, within-group, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps and meets reporting requirements. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical).

This study uses task-based fMRI of working memory (meets I5 and I6). The reported analysis is a spatial-normalization group-level GLM fit over the whole brain (Model fit over: whole brain) with reported peak coordinates (Table tbl4), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked results (I7, I10), even though inference was restricted to an ROI. The primary contrast is a within-group simple effect (Delay 3), meeting the within-group contrast requirement (I8). Participants are healthy adults (n=13), which is acceptable (I9). No exclusion criteria are met: the study is not ROI-only (E3), not connectivity-only (E4), not only between-group contrasts (E5), and is empirical (not E6). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates none.

This is an event-related fMRI task-switching study probing visual and response switching (executive function/cognitive flexibility). The record reports group-level voxelwise task activation peaks with Talairach coordinates and voxel-level thresholding (Bonferroni-corrected voxelwise t-threshold), and within-group contrasts comparing switch vs stay events (VS and RS), so a within-group task contrast and whole-brain voxelwise inference are present. Participants are healthy adults (n=18). Although one analysis entry notes 'model fit over: region of interest', the presence of voxel-level whole-brain inference and reported coordinates indicates voxelwise group results are reported. Therefore all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study reports task-based fMRI (DMS delayed match-to-sample) engaging working memory, an executive function domain. It includes group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (model fit over: whole brain) and reports within-group contrasts (CAT > AUD) across multiple analyses with coordinate peaks reported. Results are presented as voxelwise statistical maps/tables. Participant sample is healthy adults. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusions are triggered.

Excluded because the task is an implicit Double Serial Reaction Time (procedural sequence-learning) paradigm, which does not fall within the review's required executive function domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). The study does use fMRI and reports whole-brain, voxelwise, cluster-corrected, within-group task contrasts, but the primary cognitive construct is procedural/implicit sequence learning rather than executive function. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (whole-brain voxelwise task analyses reported), I8 (within-group task contrasts present), I9 (participant group acceptable), I10 (whole-brain results reported in tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (does not specifically assess executive function or cognitive control despite using fMRI), I6 (task does not fall within established executive function domains). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered.

This study reports task-based fMRI (BOLD) including an established executive-function task (working memory: Sternberg Item Recognition) and an episodic retrieval task. Analyses are group-level, voxelwise whole-brain second-level GLM tests with reported peak coordinates (tables), and contrasts are within-group (high-load > baseline, low-load > baseline, episodic retrieval > baseline). Reporting and thresholds are voxelwise and peaks are provided, satisfying whole-brain evidence. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Therefore all inclusion criteria relevant to the review are met.

This fMRI study uses a working memory/attentional control task (Old/New recognition with instructions to remember or ignore scenes/faces), meeting the executive-function task requirement. It reports group-level, voxelwise task activation results (Analysis 17725995_analysis_0: Remember Scenes and Remember Faces > Passive View; whole-brain random-effects GLM with reported peak coordinates in Table 1), satisfying whole-brain and within-group contrast requirements. Multiple within-group contrasts are reported. Results are reported as peak coordinates in tables. No exclusion criteria apply: the paper includes voxelwise activation maps (not only ROI or connectivity), and is an empirical task-based fMRI study. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

This is an fMRI task-based study with whole-brain, voxelwise, within-group contrasts reported (meets I5, I7, I8, I9, I10). However, the tasks are semantic memory/object-recall and associative semantic decisions, not established executive-function tasks (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Although the authors mention involvement of verbal working memory and conflict monitoring, the paradigm primarily probes semantic recall/association rather than a canonical executive-function domain. Therefore it does not satisfy I6 and must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text is complete for screening.

This fMRI study is excluded because it does not assess executive function tasks as defined by the review. Specifically, the reported tasks are semantic decision (lexico-semantic), tone discrimination (auditory psychophysics), and visuomotor coordination — none map onto the specified executive domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Inclusion criteria met: I7 (whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I8 (within-group task contrasts task>control), I9 (within-group contrasts reported for participant groups), I10 (whole-brain results reported as peak coordinates). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I5 (study assessing executive function/cognitive control task), I6 (tasks within established executive function domains). No exclusion criteria are triggered (exclusion_criteria_applied=[]). Full text is complete for screening (fulltext_incomplete=false).

The study used FDG-PET during a resting (eyes-closed) acquisition and reports pharmacological contrasts (ethanol vs placebo) and correlations between resting metabolism and behavioral reaction times. No task-based, within-group voxelwise activation contrast from an executive-function task is reported. Inclusion criteria met: I9 (participant group acceptable) and I10 (results reported in tables/coordinates). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I5 (no task-based PET/fMRI activation paradigm), I6 (imaging does not reflect an executive-function task paradigm despite behavioral attention testing being performed), I7 (no whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked map), I8 (no within-group task contrast). Exclusion criteria met: E4 (resting-state / task-absent analyses without a task activation map). Therefore the study does not meet the meta-analysis requirements and should be excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study (task-based) that examines encoding and decision processes during an interval timing task and reports working-memory-related activations during decision making. The NeuroStore record lists multiple group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (e.g. main effect of encoding; hard>easy contrasts; omnibus contrasts) with reported peak coordinates, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps. Several contrasts are explicitly within-group (omnibus, hard>easy), satisfying the within-group contrast requirement. The task engages working memory/rehearsal systems (left middle-frontal and parietal cortex, auditory rehearsal network), placing it within an executive-function domain (working memory) for the purposes of this meta-analysis. Participants are healthy adults and results are reported in tables of peaks. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 and is INCLUDED.

This is a task-based fMRI study of mental calculation reporting whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts (tables of peaks). The arithmetic tasks explicitly engage mnemonic/working memory and attentional processes (authors note engagement of working memory-related left inferior frontal areas), so they fall within executive domains (working memory). At least one within-group task contrast is reported (multiple contrasts > result matching). Whole-brain model fitting is reported and coordinates are provided in Table 1. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group). Small sample size (n=5) reduces confidence but does not violate inclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI task study directly probing intentional inhibition (an executive function: inhibition). It reports within-group, voxelwise contrasts (action > tone; inhibition > tone; inhibition > action) analyzed with random-effects one-sample t-tests across participants and model fit over the whole brain with voxelwise thresholding and reported peak coordinates. Thus the study provides whole-brain, group-level task activation maps relevant to executive function. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group contrasts, empirical data).

This study uses an Emotional Face Matching Task (affective processing/regulation), not an established executive-function task (working memory, inhibition, flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Although it is an fMRI study (I5), reports whole-brain voxelwise results (I7), includes a within-group task contrast (main effect of task) (I8), includes acceptable participant groups (I9), and reports coordinates/peaks (I10), it does not meet I6 (task within established executive function domains). No exclusion criteria are triggered (no ROI-only or connectivity-only reporting). Therefore the study is excluded because it fails I6.

This fMRI study reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise within-group task contrasts (e.g., New > Rest, Familiar > Rest, New > Familiar) and provides coordinate tables of peaks. The task involves memorizing and executing saccade sequences, engaging spatial working memory and sequence planning (executive functions). Analyses were voxelwise over the whole brain. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore it satisfies the meta-analysis requirements.

This fMRI study reports group-level voxelwise between-group contrasts comparing callosum-damaged participants to controls, but does not report any within-group task activation contrasts. Exclusion criterion E5 applies (only between-group contrasts reported). Inclusion criteria met: I7 (at least one whole-brain, voxelwise group-level map is reported), I9 (participant groups are acceptable), and I10 (results are reported as coordinates/tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (the tasks are perceptual discrimination/auditory judgment tasks and are not clearly within established executive-function domains), I6 (tasks are not categorized as working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, or initiation), and I8 (no within-group task contrast is provided for any group). Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis of executive-function task activations.

This is an event-related fMRI task-based study examining inhibition during memory retrieval (retrieval-induced forgetting), which maps to the executive domain of inhibition. The paper reports multiple group-level, voxelwise within-group contrasts and regressions with whole-brain model fitting and voxelwise inference (analyses 2,3,4,5: whole-brain, p<0.001 cluster extent 10) as well as ROI results. At least one within-group task contrast is present (P+ > P- and P- > P+). Participants are human adults and results are reported as standard coordinate tables. No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive-function task activations.

This study reports task-based fMRI working-memory (n-back) experiments and explicitly includes whole-brain, group-level within-subject contrasts (parametric n-back effect and Verbal>Spatial and Spatial>Verbal contrasts; analyses 4–6). These meet the review focus on executive-function task activations. Tasks are working-memory (an established executive domain). Whole-brain voxelwise group analyses are reported with corrected thresholds and peak coordinates (Table 4). Although the paper also contains lesion between-group analyses, at least one qualifying within-group, whole-brain fMRI contrast in healthy participants is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI task-based study (I5) reporting whole-brain voxelwise group analyses (I7) with at least one within-group task contrast (COPY > spatial cue) (I8). Participant sample (n=12 healthy adults) is acceptable (I9), and results are reported as coordinates/peaks (I10). However, the experimental paradigm is an imitation task (observing and copying finger movements) and does not fall within the review’s defined executive function domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Therefore inclusion criterion I6 is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

The study reports whole-brain, group-level within-group task contrasts (LEFT/RIGHT/CENTRAL/MIXED > REST) and provides voxelwise results, so it satisfies I7, I8, I9, and I10. However, the task is auditory spatial attention reorienting (localizing sounds) with movement suppression requested; it does not clearly assess an executive function domain as defined (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Although the authors note inferior frontal activation related to inhibition of a motor response, no contrast isolating inhibitory control or other executive processes is reported—the reported contrasts are task>rest for spatial positions. Therefore the study does not meet I5 and I6 and must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered.

The study is an empirical task-based fMRI investigation of working memory (an executive function) with a verbal immediate serial recall task, meeting I5 and I6. It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (Model fit over: whole brain; Inference over: whole brain) with corrected cluster-level thresholding and reported peak coordinates, satisfying I7 and I10. Contrasts are within-group (omnibus, within-group) and include ANOVA effects across task epochs and reward conditions, meeting I8. Participant sample is appropriate and within-group contrasts are present (I9). No exclusion criteria apply: analyses are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and not limited to between-group contrasts. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

The NeuroStore record shows an event-related fMRI working-memory study (I5,I6) with whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses reported (I7) and participant groups including clinical (pre-HD) and controls (I9). Coordinates/peaks are reported in tables (I10). However, the extracted analyses are all between-group contrasts (controls vs pre-HD; close vs far pre-HD; omnibus/group x load interactions) or ROI-based cross-subject correlations; no within-group task>baseline or other within-group task activation contrast is reported for any group. Therefore the study reports ONLY between-group contrasts and ROI association(s) with no within-group task activation maps, meeting exclusion criterion E5. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I7, I9, I10. Inclusion criterion not met: I8 (no within-group task contrast). Exclusion criterion met: E5. Conclusion: EXCLUDED.

The study uses fMRI and includes executive function tasks (N-back working memory) and reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses, so I5, I6, I7 and I9 are satisfied. However, all reported statistical contrasts are between-group comparisons or group×condition interaction contrasts (genotype group contrasts: A carrier vs T,T and T,T vs other groups) and ROI/SVC analyses for the episodic tasks; no within-group task activation (e.g., Two-back > Zero-back within a single group or main effect of task versus baseline) is reported for any participant group. This violates exclusion criterion E5 (reports only between-group/interactions with no within-group task contrast). Therefore the study must be excluded.

This fMRI study reports task-evoked activations during stimulus-response delay tasks that manipulate remembering (working memory) and response anticipation, domains relevant to executive function. It includes voxelwise, whole-brain group-level analyses (model fit over whole brain) with reported peak coordinates/tables and multiple within-group contrasts (controls: anticipating > resting; patients: remembering > resting). Thus it meets inclusion requirements for task-based fMRI (I5), established executive domains including working memory (I6), whole-brain voxelwise results (I7), presence of within-group task contrasts (I8), and acceptability of participant groups (I9). Results are reported as peaks/tables satisfying I10. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. The document appears complete for screening purposes (fulltext_incomplete=false).

The NeuroStore record indicates this is an fMRI study using a working memory (executive) task with whole-brain, voxelwise analyses in a schizophrenia sample (meets I5, I6, I7, I9). However, the extracted analyses listed are only between-group contrasts (patients > controls; group difference) and no within-group task activation contrast for any group is reported in the document. Therefore the study reports ONLY between-group contrasts and does not provide a within-group task activation map, violating inclusion criterion I8 and meeting exclusion criterion E5. Excluded for E5. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I7, I9. Inclusion criteria not met: I8.

The study is an fMRI within-subject task study (I5, I8) and reports a within-group contrast and participant details (I9). However, the NeuroStore record indicates the primary reported statistical maps/contrasts (analyses 0 and 1) were estimated and thresholded over a priori regions of interest (region-level, ROI) and no analysis is clearly described as a group-level voxelwise (whole-brain) task-evoked statistical map. Other analyses (2–5) list reported peaks but provide no model-fit or inference metadata to confirm voxelwise whole-brain results. Therefore the study appears to report only ROI/small-volume analyses with no confirmed voxelwise whole-brain activation map, meeting exclusion criterion E3. Additionally, the task (mental rotation) is primarily a visuospatial/recognition manipulation and is not clearly described as within an established executive-function domain in this document (I6 not met). Because E3 is met (and I7/I6 not met), the study must be excluded.

This is a PET study reporting task-evoked activations (I5 met). It includes multiple whole-brain, voxelwise group contrasts with reported peak coordinates (I7 and I10 met), and several within-group task contrasts (I8 met). Participants are healthy human adults (I9 met). However, the tasks are episodic memory paradigms (object-location recognition, spatial reconstruction, and free recall of pseudo-words) rather than established executive-function domains such as working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, or initiation. Therefore I6 is NOT met. No exclusion criteria are triggered (E3–E6 not met). Decision: EXCLUDED because it does not meet inclusion criterion I6 (task domain).

The study reports task-based fMRI using the Stroop Color-Word task (an established inhibition/cognitive-control paradigm) and also reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses. The NeuroStore record includes within-group task contrasts (one-sample t-tests for controls: dominant- and non-dominant-hand task > rest) and a two-sample group comparison; model fit is over the whole brain and results are reported as peak coordinates. Thus the paper meets inclusion requirements: (I5) task-based fMRI of executive/cognitive control (Stroop), (I6) task within an executive domain (inhibition), (I7) whole-brain voxelwise group-level analyses, (I8) presence of within-group task contrasts, (I9) participant groups are acceptable, and (I10) results are reported as coordinates/tables. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text is available via the NeuroStore record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The NeuroStore record shows an fMRI task of working memory (meets I5, I6) with a within-group interaction contrast reported (meets I8). Participants and coordinate reporting are provided (meets I9 and I10). However, the only explicitly described model was fit over a region of interest (ROI) and the other analyses have no model-fit/voxelwise details—results are reported as peaks from ROI-defined regions. There is no evidence of a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation map. Therefore the study reports only ROI/small-volume analyses and does not meet the whole-brain voxelwise requirement (I7). This triggers exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI/SVC analyses). Full text is considered complete for screening.

The study investigates episodic encoding and subsequent memory (free recall vs associative recognition), not an executive function or cognitive control task. Although it reports group-level, voxelwise within-group contrasts and whole-brain voxel-level results (analyses with whole-brain model fit and voxelwise thresholds), the task paradigm (episodic encoding/imagery and plausibility judgments) does not fall within established executive function domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Therefore it does not meet I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria are triggered.

This PET task-based study reports within-subject, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (Attending vs Suppression and vice versa) and correlations with physiological measures. The task involves voluntary emotion suppression, which operationalizes inhibitory control (an executive function domain). Group-level contrasts and peak coordinates are reported (tables), satisfying voxelwise reporting. Participants are a human within-group sample. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply.

The study reports task-based BOLD fMRI using a Go/No-Go response inhibition task (an established executive function domain). It includes a group-level, within-group voxelwise contrast (nogo > go) with whole-brain inference (FWE, voxel-level) and reported peak coordinates (Table tbl2). Therefore it meets I5 (fMRI task assessing executive function), I6 (inhibition), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise group analysis), I8 (within-group task contrast), I9 (participant group acceptable), and I10 (results reported in tables). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, and empirical original data).

The study reports task-based fMRI (BOLD) investigating feature-based attentional control with rapid event-related design involving shifts versus holds of attention (transient and sustained control). These manipulations map onto executive function domain of cognitive flexibility/attentional control (shift operations). All analyses are group-level, voxelwise whole-brain GLM contrasts (model fit and inference over whole brain) and report peak coordinates/tables. Within-group task contrasts are reported (hold motion > hold color; hold color > hold motion; shift > hold conjunctions). Participants are a human group (n=13). Results are reported as voxelwise, whole-brain contrasts with thresholds and peak tables, satisfying reporting requirements. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective and should be INCLUDED.

This fMRI study reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., difficult>easy; difficult>baseline) from an overt word-generation task. Verbal word-generation/fluency maps onto the ‘initiation’ executive function domain. The paper provides whole-brain corrected cluster results in tables (coordinates), uses within-group contrasts, and includes healthy participants. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for an executive-function task activation meta-analysis and violates no exclusion criteria.

This fMRI study uses a Stroop task (inhibition, an executive-function paradigm) and reports voxelwise, whole-brain, group-level within-group task contrasts (interference > facilitation) for both healthy controls and patients, with reported peak coordinates and voxel-level thresholding. It therefore meets criteria for task-based fMRI of executive function, whole-brain voxelwise analyses, and includes within-group task contrasts. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Inclusion criteria satisfied: I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10.

The study reports task-based fMRI of attention shifting/working memory (meets I5 and I6). Multiple analyses include whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise contrasts (Model fit over: whole brain; random-effects models; reported peaks/tables), satisfying I7 and I10. Within-group task contrasts are reported for at least one group (Analyses 3 and 4: Arrow simple effect within Good and Poor performers), satisfying I8. Participant groups are healthy adults, which is allowed (I9). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only (E3), not connectivity-only (E4) since task activations are reported, and within-group contrasts exist so E5 is not met. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

This is an fMRI study (I5) with whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported (I7) and within-group task contrasts (easy>difficult, difficult>baseline, difficult>easy) (I8). Participant reporting and task results are provided (I9, I10). However, the task is temporal discrimination/interval timing, which does not fall within the predefined executive function domains required by the review (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Therefore inclusion criterion I6 is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text is available from the NeuroStore record, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

The study reports a task-based fMRI Stroop (counting Stroop) contrast (Stroop > control) using a group-level, voxelwise whole-brain 1-sample t-test with reported peaks (Table tbl1). The task assesses response inhibition/conflict (an executive function). Although additional seed-based connectivity analyses are reported, the paper also provides a within-group task activation map (whole-brain), satisfying the requirement for voxelwise task-evoked results. All inclusion criteria for task type, domain, within-group contrast, and whole-brain voxelwise reporting are met. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-empirical) apply.

This fMRI study uses a Stroop task (inhibition/selective attention — an executive function domain) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task activation contrasts. The NeuroStore record includes within-group Stroop>rest contrasts for healthy controls and for patients (Analyses 0 and 1) and reports peak coordinates in tables, satisfying voxelwise, whole-brain reporting. Results are reported as group-level maps (second-level random effects for between-group contrasts also present) and coordinate tables. Therefore all inclusion criteria for task, domain, whole-brain voxelwise reporting, and presence of within-group contrasts are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

The study reports task-based fMRI (BOLD) of a Mental Arithmetic task that the authors explicitly link to working memory and related executive resources. It reports a within-group, voxelwise contrast (complex > simple) analyzed at the group (second-level random-effects one-sample t-test) with whole-brain inference and reported peak coordinates (Talairach, tables). Thus it provides whole-brain, group-level task activation maps for an executive-function-relevant task (working memory demands during complex mental calculation). No exclusion criteria apply: analyses are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and include within-group contrasts. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 and I10.

This is a task-based fMRI study using an oddball/vigilance paradigm (executive domain: vigilance), with group-level, voxelwise GLM contrasts reported across the whole brain and within-group task contrasts (e.g., when>what; what>when; where>when). Results are reported as peak coordinates (tables), satisfying reporting requirements. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Therefore all relevant inclusion criteria are met and the study is appropriate for inclusion in the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an event-related fMRI study reporting whole-brain, within-group task contrasts and analyses of cognitive-control-related regions. However the task is a non-verbal associative recognition (episodic retrieval) paradigm rather than a task that clearly falls within the specified executive-function domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Therefore it does not meet inclusion criterion I6 and must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered; inclusion criteria met: I5, I7, I8, I9, I10; inclusion criterion not met: I6.

This fMRI study uses an N-back task (working memory), an established executive function domain. Group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects analyses are reported (Predict > Detect contrasts for 1-back, n=18, corrected p<.05; 3-back, n=10, uncorrected), with coordinates/peaks listed in a table. At least one within-group task contrast is present. Results are reported in Talairach coordinates. These elements satisfy inclusion criteria for task-based executive-function fMRI with whole-brain voxelwise within-group contrasts. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and not only between-group contrasts).

This is an fMRI N-back (working memory) study with within-group contrasts and participant details, but it does not provide a whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical map. The only explicit task contrast (3-back > rest) was reported with model fit and thresholding restricted to regions of interest. The whole-brain voxelwise results reported are cross-subject regressions with personality traits (likely reflecting resting/task-correlations) rather than a group-level voxelwise task activation map. Therefore inclusion criterion I7 (whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked evidence) is not met, so the study must be excluded.

This study is excluded because all reported voxelwise analyses were confined to anatomically defined ROIs with small-volume correction (model fit over: region of interest; inference restricted to ROI; SVC p<0.05), i.e. no whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps are reported. Exclusion criterion met: E3 (only ROI/SVC analyses). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (executive function domain: inhibition; Go/No-Go task), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported for patient and control groups), I9 (participant groups acceptable), I10 (results reported in tables/peaks). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise evidence reported). Therefore the paper does not provide the required whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps and must be excluded.

This fMRI study reports task-based activations for an episodic/working memory (EWM) task (working memory is an established executive function domain) and semantic memory contrasts. Group-level, voxelwise analyses were fit over the whole brain with reported peak coordinates for within-group contrasts in both healthy controls and Alzheimer’s patients (e.g., EWM > SM within-group). Results are not limited to ROIs or connectivity-only analyses, and at least one within-group task contrast is reported, satisfying the review’s requirements. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5 (task fMRI), I6 (working memory within executive domains), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise results), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (participant groups acceptable), and I10 (coordinates/peaks reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met.

The study uses an SRT implicit rule/sequence-learning task, which is not one of the established executive-function domains listed in inclusion criteria (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Although the paper reports task-based fMRI with whole-brain, voxelwise within-group contrasts (Sequence>Random) for healthy controls and patients and provides ROI and coordinate results, the task assesses procedural/implicit sequence learning rather than executive/cognitive-control processes required by I5/I6. Therefore I5 and I6 are not met. The study does meet I7 (whole-brain voxelwise group analyses present), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported), I9 (participant groups acceptable), and I10 (results reported as coordinates/tables). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Conclusion: exclude because the task does not fall within the executive function domains required by the review.

ROI-only voxelwise analyses: all reported analyses have 'Model fit over: region of interest' and 'Inference restricted to: region of interest' (parieto-frontal scans defined a priori), so no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps are reported. Exclusion IDs met: E3. Inclusion IDs met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (working memory task), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported), I9 (any participant group; healthy participants), I10 (coordinates/peaks reported). Inclusion IDs not met: I7 (no whole-brain group-level voxelwise analysis). Therefore excluded per E3.

Exclusion E3 applies: the paper reports analyses confined to a predefined region of interest (retinotopic IPS) with model fit over ROI and no voxelwise whole-brain task activation maps. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (anti-saccade task is an inhibition/executive-control task), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported: leftward>rightward and rightward>leftward), I9 (human participant group reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (no whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task-evoked statistical map reported). Therefore the study must be excluded under E3.

This fMRI study reports task-based, group-level voxelwise contrasts that assess attention/visuomotor preparation and pointing (motor planning). The tasks include an attention/vigilance task (counting digits) and preparation/planning of movements, which map onto executive domains (vigilance and planning). Multiple analyses are whole-brain, voxelwise, group-level within-group contrasts with reported peak coordinates. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Therefore all inclusion criteria are met.

This fMRI Stroop study meets all inclusion criteria: (I5) task-based fMRI assessing executive function (Stroop/inhibition); (I6) Stroop falls within inhibition/cognitive control domain; (I7) analyses were whole-brain, voxelwise (model fit over whole brain, voxel-level threshold reported); (I8) it reports within-group task contrasts — paired (before vs after treatment) contrasts for the interference condition in the patient group (two within-group analyses listed); (I9) participant group is a clinical OCD sample (acceptable); (I10) voxel peaks/results are reported in tables. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only (E3), not connectivity/resting-state only (E4), and not limited to between-group contrasts (E5) because within-group pre/post task contrasts are provided. Therefore include for meta-analysis of executive-function task activations.

This event-related fMRI study reports task-based activations for a numerical Stroop (conflict/interference) task, which is an executive control paradigm involving inhibition/attention. NeuroStore shows whole-brain voxelwise model fits and multiple group-level within-group contrasts (e.g., Incongruent > Congruent; task > null; Distance contrasts) with reported peak coordinates/tables. These meet I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (executive function/cognitive control domain), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise results), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (participant group acceptable), and I10 (coordinates/tables reported). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Full text appears available in the NeuroStore record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This fMRI study used a sentence-comprehension paradigm examining lexical ambiguity. It reports whole-brain, voxelwise, within-group task contrasts (Ambiguous > Unambiguous) and coordinates, and reports correlations with reading span. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (whole-brain voxelwise analyses), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (participant group reported), I10 (results reported in tables of coordinates). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 and I6 — the task is a language/sentence-comprehension paradigm and was not designed as an executive-function/cognitive-control task within established EF domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Because I5 and I6 are not satisfied, the study is excluded.

This study reports task-based fMRI Stroop contrasts (incongruent>neutral) and tables of peak coordinates, satisfying I5 (fMRI task), I6 (executive function - inhibition), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported), I9 (acceptable participant group), and I10 (results reported as coordinates/peaks). However, all reported analyses were fit and thresholded over regions of interest (model fit over: region of interest; thresholding: region-level) rather than as group-level, voxelwise whole-brain statistical maps. Therefore it violates I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise map) and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only/small-volume-corrected analyses with no voxelwise results). Conclusion: EXCLUDE for E3 (ROI-only analyses); inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I8, I9, I10; inclusion criterion not met: I7.

This fMRI study examines executive/reasoning (fluid reasoning) using a task-based paradigm (serial 3×3 matrix reasoning), satisfying I5 and I6. Analyses were estimated over the whole brain with whole-brain inference and reported coordinate peaks/tables, meeting I7 and I10. Multiple group-level, voxelwise within-group contrasts are reported (Hard > Easy; Correct > Incorrect; interaction), satisfying I8. Participants (healthy adults) are an acceptable group per I9. No exclusion criteria are met: results are whole-brain voxelwise (not ROI-only; E3 not met), not limited to connectivity or resting-state (E4 not met), and within-group task contrasts are present (E5 not met); this is empirical human neuroimaging data (E6 not met). Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria, and is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an fMRI task study of cognitive control of emotion (reappraisal), but the task does not fall within the meta-analysis’ specified executive function domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported, e.g., increase>look, decrease>look), I9 (participant group reported), I10 (whole-brain results reported in tables). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (task does not fall within the established executive function domains required by this review; emotion regulation/reappraisal is not listed). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered by the document. Therefore exclude for not meeting I6.

This study reports task-based fMRI data from a continuous performance task that manipulates reward expectation and cognitive processing, which falls within executive function domains (vigilance/attention and cognitive control). It provides group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (model fit and inference over whole brain; voxelwise FDR thresholding) and reports peak coordinates (MNI). At least one analysis is a within-group task contrast (parametric modulation, one-sample t tests of contrast images). Participants are healthy adults. Thus all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Excluded because the paper reports only between-group contrasts and interactions with no within-group task activation maps for any group (exclusion E5). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise group-level results reported for between-group contrasts), I9 (developmental and adult participant groups acceptable), and I10 (results reported as coordinates/tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (tasks are numerical/arithmetic and magnitude comparison, not established executive-function domains such as working memory, inhibition, or cognitive flexibility) and I8 (no within-group task contrasts reported). Full text is complete as provided.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that probes voluntary selection of covert attention (a form of attentional control/volition fitting established executive domains such as initiation/attention control). It reports a within-group contrast (choose > instructed) estimated voxelwise over the whole brain with whole-brain inference and cluster-level correction, and reports peak coordinates (MNI). Participants are a healthy cohort (n=11). Thus the study meets inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI of executive/cognitive control processes), I6 (task within executive domains — volitional/initiation/attentional control), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise results), I8 (within-group task contrast), I9 (participant group acceptable), and I10 (results reported as coordinates). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full text appears accessible in the NeuroStore-derived record.

This is a task-based fMRI study of a mental arithmetic paradigm that engages working memory/executive processes (continuous subtraction from 1000). It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (model fit over whole brain; inference over whole brain for the main contrast) with within-group contrasts (mental arithmetic > eyes-closed rest and the reverse), and coordinates/peaks are reported (tables). Results satisfy requirements for whole-brain voxelwise task activation reporting. Although the sample is small (n=8), the inclusion criteria do not exclude small or specific participant groups. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and not between-group-only). Therefore the study should be included in the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

The study reports task-based fMRI of an executive function (Multi-Source Interference Task measuring cognitive control/interference). It includes group-level, voxelwise within-group contrasts (I > C) for healthy participants (n=24) and opiate users (n=24) with whole-brain model fitting and whole-brain cluster-wise correction (FLAME/FILM), satisfying voxelwise task-evoked statistical map requirement. Between-group contrasts are also reported but at least one within-group contrast is present for each group. Reporting of peaks/tables meets acceptable reporting formats. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the article meets all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 and I10 and should be included.

This fMRI task-based study assesses cross-modal attention shifts using oddball and vigilance paradigms (vigilance is an included executive domain). It reports multiple within-group task contrasts (e.g. Focus-Auditory within older adults; Shift > Focus within groups). Crucially, Analysis 16549368_analysis_0 indicates a group-level, voxelwise model fit with whole-brain inference (Monte Carlo cluster correction) demonstrating task-evoked whole-brain results; reported peak coordinates are provided. Results are reported as coordinate peaks/tables for other within-group contrasts as well. Thus the study meets fMRI task requirement, uses an accepted executive domain (vigilance/attention), provides at least one whole-brain voxelwise group analysis, and includes within-group contrasts. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, and not only between-group contrasts).

This is a task-based fMRI study (bold response) assessing sequence judgment of daily activities—a task that taps planning/goal-directed behavior (an executive function). Group-level, within-group task contrasts are reported (LF/MF/HF > control; and frequency-specific contrasts). Although some contrasts report inference restricted to a region-of-interest, the GLM was fit over the whole brain and several parametric-modulation analyses (emotion, scene-likeness) report voxel-level thresholding (voxelwise results with reported peak coordinates in tables). The study therefore provides whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps and within-group contrasts, and reports coordinates in tables. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study that investigates attentional control/ cognitive control processes (zooming in/out), satisfying I5. The task involves dynamic shifting of attentional focus (analogous to cognitive flexibility/vigilance), meeting I6. Analyses were whole-brain (model fit over: whole brain) and voxelwise second-level group analyses are reported, satisfying I7. Multiple within-group task contrasts are reported (e.g., zooming out > zooming in; zooming in > zooming out; parametric within-group contrasts), satisfying I8. Participant group is healthy adults (n=12), so I9 is met. Results are reported as peak coordinates/tables, satisfying I10. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. The reported thresholds and cluster corrections are appropriate and at least one group-level voxelwise task contrast is available for inclusion.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that examines maintenance of temporal information across delays (0–9s) and reports activation of a prefrontal–parietal–temporal working memory network during continuation, indicating involvement of working memory/executive processes. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (e.g., syncopate>synchronize; Pacing>Continue; Continue>Pacing) with thresholding and peak coordinates. At least one within-group task contrast is present. Results are reported as whole-brain coordinate peaks (Talairach). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Therefore the study meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study (N=20) using a virtual driving paradigm and reports multiple within-group voxelwise contrasts analyzed with second-level random-effects GLMs and whole-brain model fitting. Reported contrasts include action planning, traffic rules, stopping, turning, avoiding collisions, etc., mapping onto established executive domains (planning, initiation, monitoring/vigilance, rule processing, inhibitory/avoidance responses). Results are reported as peak coordinates (MNI) in tables. Therefore inclusion criteria I5 (fMRI task), I6 (tasks map to executive domains), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise analyses), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (participant group acceptable), and I10 (coordinates reported) are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, and within-group contrasts are present). fulltext_incomplete set to false.

The study is excluded because its imaging analyses are reported only as region-of-interest (ROI) level results (Model fit over: region of interest; Thresholding: region of interest-level), so there are no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-activation maps reported (violates I7 and meets exclusion E3). Additionally, the task is prototype-distortion category learning (category-matching), which is not within the specified executive function domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation), so it does not meet I5/I6. The paper does report a within-group contrast (after 250 trials > after 750 trials), satisfying I8, and includes a qualifying participant group (healthy adults), satisfying I9. Therefore the study must be excluded because it fails the whole-brain requirement and does not assess an executive function task.

The study reports an event-related fMRI working-memory task (Delayed Match-to-Sample) with a within-group contrast (six-letter > one-letter arrays) and voxelwise, whole-brain multivariate results reported as Talairach peak coordinates (Tables). This meets I5 (fMRI task-based study), I6 (working memory = executive function), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise results reported), I8 (within-group task contrast present), I9 (participant group acceptable), and I10 (results reported as coordinate tables). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study reporting whole-brain, voxelwise group contrasts examining conflict and goal-selection during bimanual reaching. The task probes selection/planning and cognitive control (goal-selection conflict, reaction time costs, engagement of pre-SMA and cingulate motor areas), which fit established executive-function domains (planning/cognitive control). Neuroimaging analyses were fit and inferred over the whole brain with cluster-level correction and reported peak coordinates (tables), and multiple within-group task contrasts (congruency effects for spatial and symbolic cues) are provided. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study reports task-based fMRI with a working-memory-related contrast (analysis_0 labeled 'Working memory') and a within-group, voxelwise whole-brain contrast (analysis_17987468_analysis_2: game > random) with SPM multiple-comparisons correction (p<0.05 voxel-level). Thus it meets I5 (fMRI task), I6 (includes a working memory/executive-function contrast), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise results reported), I8 (within-group task contrast), I9 (healthy participant group reported), and I10 (results reported as coordinate peaks/tables). Although one analysis describes recognition memory, the record also explicitly lists a working-memory contrast; the fixed-effects model and small sample (n=5) introduce uncertainty about generalizability, but do not violate the inclusion/exclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met.

Although this is an empirical fMRI study with whole-brain, voxelwise within-group contrasts reported (contrast maps and coordinate tables), the tasks are episodic memory retrieval (temporal-order and spatial-location judgments of events/objects) rather than established executive function/cognitive-control tasks. Inclusion criteria I7, I8, I9 and I10 are satisfied (whole-brain voxelwise results, within-group contrasts, acceptable participant sample reporting, and coordinate reporting). However, criteria I5 and I6 are not met: the paradigm assesses temporal/spatial memory retrieval and autobiographical/semantic memory, not core executive functions (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). The abstract’s brief note that some conditions ‘‘yielded greater working memory demands’’ does not reclassify the primary task as an executive-function paradigm. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Therefore the study is excluded for not meeting I5 and I6.

This is a task-based PET study using 11C-raclopride to measure task-evoked dopamine release during a working memory (executive) task. It reports voxelwise statistical analyses (parametric images compared using voxel-based SPM) with group-level, within-group task contrasts (VMT > SWT) for both controls and PD patients, and between-group interaction contrasts. Results are reported as peak coordinates (Table 3). Although inference used small-volume correction in regions of interest, the model was fit over the whole brain and voxelwise maps were generated, so this is not a case of ROI-only reporting. Thus it meets I5 (task-based PET), I6 (working memory executive domain), I7 (group-level voxelwise analysis / whole-brain model fit), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported), I9 (participant groups acceptable), and I10 (coordinates reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met.

The study is excluded because it reports only region-of-interest (ROI) analyses with region-level thresholding (Model fit over: region of interest; Thresholding: region-level), and does not provide any group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task activation maps, meeting exclusion criterion E3. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI study) and I9 (participant group reporting within-group measures is present). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I6 (task is gambling/risk/ambiguity decision-making, which does not fall within the specified executive function domains), I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise results reported), and I8 (no clear within-group task contrast of task vs baseline or standard task contrast suitable for activation meta-analysis is provided). Full text is complete enough for assessment (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This study reports task-based fMRI (event-related) contrasts examining selection of actions versus observation, which maps onto executive processes (action selection/initiation and attentional selection). It reports group-level, voxelwise (whole-brain) random-effects GLM analyses with thresholded cluster-corrected results and reported peak coordinates/tables. Multiple within-group task contrasts are provided (e.g., self-selection > observation, observation > self-selection, conjoint activations). Participants are healthy adults. Thus all required inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met (results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and include within-group contrasts).

This is an fMRI task-based study of conflict/interference (executive function/cognitive control), using a within-subject event-related design contrasting high vs low conflict (II>CI) for emotional and nonemotional tasks. Multiple group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task contrasts are reported (analyses with model fit over whole brain and reported peaks), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked maps. The contrasts are within-group task contrasts. Participants are healthy adults. Results are reported with thresholds and peaks. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 are met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an fMRI task-based study of simulated driving that reports task-evoked spatial maps derived from group independent component analysis with voxelwise model fit across the whole brain and tables of peak coordinates. The task and results explicitly implicate executive domains (inhibition/error monitoring in anterior cingulate; vigilance/frontoparietal regions), satisfying the executive-function domain requirement. Multiple analyses are reported as within-group simple effects, meeting the within-group contrast requirement. Whole-brain voxelwise results are reported (model fit over whole brain; peaks listed), and coordinate tables are provided. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not solely connectivity/resting-state without task activation, and include within-group contrasts. Therefore the study meets I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 and is eligible for inclusion.

This study reports task-based fMRI BOLD activations for saccade and antisaccade tasks (measuring inhibitory control, an executive function). It includes whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects analyses (model fit over: whole brain) and reports peak coordinates. Crucially, it contains within-group task contrasts (refixation > fixation) for healthy and for schizophrenia participants, satisfying the requirement for at least one within-group task activation. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, or only between-group contrasts) are met. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria.

The study reports two event-related fMRI experiments using a Go/No-Go motor task (inhibition) paired with visual identification — a task within the executive function domain (inhibition). Analyses are group-level, voxelwise whole-brain GLM contrasts (Model fit over: whole brain; coordinate space Talairach) with within-group contrasts reported (NOGO > GO and GO > NOGO) and reported peak coordinates/tables. Results are task-evoked activation maps reported as coordinates (Table). Participants are healthy adult groups (n=16 and n=18). Thus the paper meets all inclusion criteria for task-based fMRI executive function, whole-brain voxelwise evidence, and within-group contrasts. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical).

This is an original task-based fMRI study using a delayed-match-to-sample working-memory task (an executive function domain). Multiple within-group, voxelwise contrasts are reported (e.g. 6 > 1 for stimulus, retention, and probe phases) with whole-brain model fitting and coordinates reported (Talairach). Participants are a healthy cohort (n=40). Results are reported as voxelwise multivariate maps (Ordinal Trend Canonical Variates Analysis) with voxel-level thresholding and peak tables. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function), I6 (working memory), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise evidence), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (participant group acceptable), and I10 (coordinates/tables reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met.

This fMRI study reports a voxelwise, whole-brain, group-level within-group contrast (voluntary saccades > fixation) in Parkinson’s patients (second-level GLM, model fit over whole brain, coordinates reported). The task is a task-based paradigm (voluntary saccades) that the authors describe as involving frontal planning/selection and voluntary initiation of saccades, which fits the review’s executive domains (planning/initiation). The paper therefore provides a task activation map at the group level and meets the meta-analysis requirements for inclusion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, or absence of within-group contrasts) are met. Confidence is slightly reduced because the saccade task is borderline between sensorimotor and executive initiation/planning, but the authors frame it in terms of frontal executive control, supporting inclusion.

Excluded because the paper does not report any within-group, voxelwise task activation contrasts and does not assess an executive-function task. Specifically, exclusion criterion E5 applies: the reported analyses are described as between-group contrasts (Forgotten > Remembered and Remembered > Forgotten labeled between-group) with no within-group task contrast for any group. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (whole-brain, voxelwise model fit is reported) and I10 (results reported as peak coordinates / table). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (study does not assess executive function/cognitive control; it examines episodic recognition memory), I6 (task is not within established executive domains like working memory or inhibition), and I8 (no within-group task contrast reported). Full text was available in the provided NeuroStore record. Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This fMRI study reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise within-group task contrasts (classification>baseline and baseline>classification) and coordinate peaks. However the task is visual concept learning/categorization (learning to distinguish exemplars of novel visual categories), which is not clearly within the specified executive function domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Therefore it does not meet the requirement that the study assess executive function or cognitive control (I5) nor the domain restriction (I6). The study does meet I7, I8, I9 and I10 (whole-brain voxelwise results; within-group task contrasts; acceptable participant reporting; coordinate reporting). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Exclude because I5 and I6 are not satisfied.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a spatial Stroop task (executive function/inhibition). Multiple group-level, voxelwise within-group contrasts are reported (incongruent > neutral), with whole-brain inference and reported peak coordinates (Talairach), satisfying the requirement for voxelwise task-evoked maps. Analyses include whole-brain model fits and coordinate tables (Table 4). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and include within-group contrasts. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This study reports fMRI whole-brain group x condition interaction / between-group contrasts (older > younger) for motor coordination tasks; no within-group task>rest or other within-group task contrasts are provided in the NeuroStore record. The tasks are motor execution/coordination rather than canonical executive-function tasks. Therefore it does not meet the requirement for a within-group task activation contrast and does not clearly assess established executive function domains. Exclusion applied: E5 (only between-group contrasts reported). Inclusion criteria met: I7 (whole-brain voxelwise results reported), I9 (participant groups acceptable), I10 (results reported in tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (not clearly an executive-function task), I6 (task not within established executive domains), I8 (no within-group task contrast reported).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study (IGT) assessing decision-making processes that rely on executive functions (planning and cognitive control), satisfying I5 and I6. Multiple group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses are reported (inference over whole brain; coordinates/tables of peaks provided), satisfying I7 and I10. Several within-group task contrasts are reported (e.g., risky > safe; win > loss), meeting I8. Participant group (healthy adults) is acceptable per I9. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only (E3), not connectivity- or resting-state-only (E4), and within-group contrasts are present (not E5). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and violates none, and is eligible for inclusion in the executive-function task activation meta-analysis.

This fMRI task-switching study directly examines cognitive flexibility (an executive function) using a task-based paradigm. It reports multiple group-level, voxelwise within-group contrasts (whole-brain model fit) such as main effects of irregular timing and unpredictable task order and task-switching > baseline, with coordinates/tables of peaks. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function), I6 (task-switching = cognitive flexibility), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I8 (within-group task contrasts present), I9 (participant group acceptable), and I10 (results reported in tables of peaks). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. The NeuroStore record appears complete enough to assess eligibility (fulltext_incomplete=false).

The study reports task-based fMRI of thought suppression, a cognitive-control/inhibition task, using group-level, voxelwise whole-brain random-effects analyses with reported peaks (tables) for multiple within-group contrasts (e.g., SUPPRESS > FREE-THOUGHT). Analyses are voxelwise (model fit over whole brain) and thresholded at voxel-level p<0.001; contrasts are within-group. Thus all inclusion criteria for executive-function task activations are met (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and not only between-group contrasts or non-empirical. Full text is sufficiently represented by the NeuroStore record, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

This is an event-related fMRI study using a Stroop color-word task (an inhibition executive function paradigm) in healthy adults (n=17). It reports at least one group-level, voxelwise whole-brain contrast (NEG-P > NO-P) with whole-brain inference (FDR-corrected p<0.05), and also reports within-group task contrasts (incongruent>congruent and NEG-P>NO-P). Results are reported with peaks/coordinates. Thus all inclusion criteria for a task-based executive-function whole-brain within-group activation study are met, and no exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical).

The study reports task-based fMRI (BOLD) in healthy participants performing Continuous Performance Tasks (attention/vigilance), meeting executive-function domain inclusion (vigilance). Multiple analyses are voxelwise, group-level, whole-brain contrasts (attention > control and CPT-IP vs CPT-DS), with coordinates/peaks reported in tables. At least one within-group task contrast is reported. Results are presented as voxelwise statistical maps summarized by peak coordinates. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the paper satisfies I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 and should be included in the meta-analysis.

The NeuroStore record reports task-based fMRI assessing cognitive control (abstract states ‘cognitive control’ and analyses examine ACC coupling during letter vs visuospatial decisions), satisfying relevance to executive function. The record includes group-level, within-group, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (Analyses 0 and 1: letter>visuospatial and visuospatial>letter; n=16, whole-brain, corrected cluster-level), meeting the requirement for voxelwise activation maps. Within-group contrasts are present, and participant group details are provided. Results are reported in MNI coordinates/peaks. No exclusion criteria are met: the study reports whole-brain task activation contrasts in addition to connectivity analyses (so it is not ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study using an N-back working memory task (an established executive function). Multiple group-level, voxelwise within-group contrasts are reported (e.g. 2-back > 1-back and visibility/main-effect contrasts) with model fit and inference performed over the whole brain (random-effects group analyses, reported peaks and corrected voxelwise thresholds). Although a small-volume correction was used for one ventral-temporal ROI, several analyses explicitly state whole-brain inference. Results are reported as coordinate peaks (tables) and voxelwise thresholding, satisfying reporting requirements. Participants are an eligible sample (healthy adults, n=14). Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are met and no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This fMRI study reports task-based activations (word reversal and rhyme judgment) that involve mental manipulation akin to working memory/visuospatial manipulation (an executive process). It includes whole-brain, voxelwise, group-level within-group contrasts (WR>baseline, RJ>baseline, WR>RJ) with corrected voxelwise inference and tables of peak coordinates. Participants are healthy adults (n=12). Thus it meets I5 (task-based fMRI of executive/cognitive control processes), I6 (task maps onto executive domain—working memory/mental manipulation), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise results reported), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (participant group acceptable), and I10 (results reported as coordinate tables). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and empirical). Full text appears available in the provided NeuroStore record. Consequently, the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

The study uses an fMRI Stroop task (an executive-function inhibition paradigm) and reports a within-group contrast (incongruent > congruent), but all task-evoked functional activation analyses are reported only within a priori ROIs (amygdala), not as group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps. Although there is a whole-brain structural (VBM) analysis, it is not a task-evoked activation map. This violates inclusion criterion I7 (whole-brain task-evoked evidence) and meets exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI/SVC functional results). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (executive/inhibition task), I8 (within-group task contrast), I9 (participant group acceptable). Inclusion criterion not met: I7 (whole-brain voxelwise task activation). Full text is complete in the provided document.

The study reports task-based fMRI (Stroop numerical) assessing cognitive control (inhibition/conflict) in healthy adults (n=15). Second-level random-effects voxelwise GLM was fit over the whole brain, and within-group contrasts are reported (e.g., incongruent > congruent; error > correct). Although small-volume correction was used for ACC/PFC, the record also indicates whole-brain correction for regions outside PFC/ACC and tables of peak coordinates are reported. These features satisfy the review’s requirements for whole-brain, voxelwise, within-group task activation results relevant to executive function. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group contrasts, empirical data present).

The NeuroStore record reports an fMRI task-based study (n=22) probing preparatory attentional states, which maps to executive-domain vigilance/attentional control; results are whole-brain and reported as coordinate peaks. However, all extracted contrasts are labeled as 'omnibus, between-group' and no within-group task activation contrast is provided in the document. Therefore the study appears to report only between-group/omnibus contrasts and lacks a qualifying within-group task contrast required by I8, triggering exclusion under E5.

The NeuroStore record reports only a region-of-interest (caudate nucleus and putamen) voxelwise model and inference restricted to that ROI (Bonferroni-thresholded peaks). No whole-brain voxelwise task activation map is reported, and the only extracted contrast is a between-group interaction (controls antisaccades > siblings prosaccades). Therefore the study fails the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results (I7) and does not report any within-group task contrast for any group (I8). It thus meets exclusion criteria E3 (ROI-only analyses with no voxelwise whole-brain results) and E5 (only between-group contrast / interaction reported). Included criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (task in executive domain — inhibition/antisaccade), I9 (participant groups acceptable). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 and I8.

The study is excluded because it does not assess an executive function task per the review’s scope.
