Inclusion criteria met: I7 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported with coordinates/tables), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported—e.g. consonants>vowels during lexical decision), I9 (participant group reported), I10 (whole-brain results reported in tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (the study investigates language processing of vowels vs consonants rather than explicitly assessing executive function/cognitive control), I6 (the tasks—lexical decision and reading aloud—are language tasks and do not fall within established executive function domains such as working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, or initiation, despite the authors’ interpretation of some activation as related to inhibition). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text is complete in the provided record.

The study reports task-based fMRI of executive function (feedback-based rule shifting / task switching), meeting I5 and I6. The NeuroStore record shows group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (Model fit over: whole brain; voxel-level threshold p<0.001, cluster extent 10) for within-group contrasts (e.g., extradimensional negative FB > positive FB; intradimensional negative FB > positive FB), satisfying I7 and I8. Participants are healthy adults (n=18), which is acceptable under I9. Whole-brain results are presented as reported peaks and tables (Table tbl1), satisfying I10. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only (E3), not connectivity-only (E4), not only between-group contrasts (E5), and the paper is empirical (E6). Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study reports task-based fMRI (I5) of free vs externally specified selection of actions and colours, which falls within executive function domains (initiation/selection/cognitive control; I6). The NeuroStore record shows voxelwise, whole-brain model fitting and group-level contrasts (I7) with multiple within-group task contrasts (e.g., FA>EA, FC>EC, main effects and interactions), satisfying I8. Participants are a human healthy sample (I9). Results are reported as whole-brain peaks/tables (coordinate peaks), meeting I10. No exclusion criteria apply: the paper includes voxelwise activation maps (not only ROI/SVC or connectivity), and reports within-group contrasts. Full text appears available via the extracted NeuroStore record, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

This is a task-based BOLD fMRI study of semantic categorization that explicitly reports activation during rule-based and similarity-based category acquisition and test phases. The task involves maintaining rules in working memory and selective attention, which fall within executive function domains (working memory/cognitive control). Analyses were whole-brain, voxelwise (model fit over whole brain; Talairach coordinates reported in tables), and the paper reports within-group contrasts (e.g. RULE: EARLY minus LATE; SIMILARITY: LATE minus EARLY), satisfying the requirement for a within-group task contrast. Peak coordinates are listed in tables. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and it is empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10 and none of the exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete in the provided record.

The study reports whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise task activation analyses (Talairach coordinates, peak tables) and includes within-group contrasts (ER>VA, VA>ER, conjunction). The tasks include a Sternberg Item Recognition Task (working memory) and a sustained visual attention/target-detection task (vigilance), both of which fall within the meta-analysis’ executive function domains. Analyses are random-effects GLMs reported at the voxel level (cluster and voxel thresholds). The report is empirical fMRI data (n=20 healthy adults) and not ROI-only or connectivity-only. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study reports task-based fMRI (group-level, voxelwise) of spatial attention shifts, which reflect executive control processes (shift and maintenance of attention). Evidence: (1) fMRI event-related design targeting attention control (meets I5); (2) task falls within executive domains (attention shifting/maintenance maps to cognitive flexibility/vigilance; meets I6); (3) model was fit over whole brain with inference over whole brain (meets I7); (4) analyses are within-group contrasts (covert shift and overt shift simple effects; meets I8); (5) participant group reported (healthy adults) and any group is acceptable (meets I9); (6) whole-brain results reported as peak coordinates/table (meets I10). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only (E3), not connectivity-only (E4), and include within-group contrasts (not E5); the paper is empirical original data (not E6). Full text is available in the provided NeuroStore record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This fMRI study uses a picture-naming negative priming task that indexes inhibitory processes (an executive function: inhibition). It reports a within-group contrast (repetition ignored > control) analyzed at the group level with a mixed-effects t-test. Crucially, one analysis (analysis_1) is a whole-brain, voxelwise group-level contrast (p<0.001, voxel with extent threshold) with reported peaks, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results. The study therefore meets inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (inhibition domain), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise evidence), I8 (within-group contrast), I9 (participant group acceptable), and I10 (results clearly reported). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical).

This fMRI study used an Eriksen Flanker Task (an inhibition/cognitive-control executive function paradigm) and reports multiple group-level, voxelwise within-group contrasts and parametric modulations with whole-brain model fitting and whole-brain inference (coordinate tables reported). Thus it meets task domain and imaging modality criteria, provides whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results (reported peaks/tables), and includes within-group contrasts. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical).

This study should be excluded because all reported analyses are region-of-interest / sphere-level (model fit over: region of interest; thresholding: sphere-level or region-level), indicating no group-level, voxelwise whole-brain activation maps were reported. This meets exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI/small-volume-corrected analyses). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI task-based study of executive control - Stroop), I6 (task falls within executive function - inhibition/cognitive control), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported), I9 (participant group acceptable), I10 (results reported as coordinates/tables). Inclusion criterion not met: I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise group-level maps). Fulltext appears complete.

The paper reports EEG/ERP and descriptive source-modeling results (dipole fits) and does not provide any group-level, voxelwise fMRI or PET statistical maps required by the review. Inclusion criteria met: I8 — a within-group task contrast is reported (attend > interpret cues); I9 — a participant group (healthy adults) is present. Inclusion criteria NOT met: I5 — study is not an fMRI or PET task activation study (NeuroStore extractions list only electrophysiology analyses); I7 — no whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical map is reported (source-model fitting is descriptive, not a voxelwise statistical map); I6 — the task targets visual-spatial orienting/attention, which is not clearly within the specified executive-function domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). No exclusion criteria E3–E6 are directly met. Because key inclusion criteria (I5 and I7) are not satisfied, the study must be excluded.

The study reports a task-based fMRI investigation using a Stroop paradigm (an established inhibition/cognitive-control executive function task) with group-level, voxelwise analyses. The NeuroStore extraction lists a within-group contrast (incongruent > neutral), model fit over the whole brain, voxel-level thresholding, and reported peak coordinates, satisfying whole-brain voxelwise reporting. Participants (n=10) and BOLD measures are reported. Thus all inclusion criteria for the review are met (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; not connectivity-only; not only between-group contrasts; not non-empirical).

This fMRI study investigates phonological processing and auditory imagery (metrical stress discrimination of spoken and imagined words), not executive function or cognitive control. While it reports group-level within-subject voxelwise contrasts and whole-brain model fits (satisfying I7, I8) and includes participant groups (I9) with coordinate reporting acceptable for meta-analysis (I10), the task does not fall within established executive function domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Therefore it fails I5 and I6 and must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) appear to be met.

This PET study reports task-based, within-group voxelwise contrasts probing language switching (task switching) and translation, which are measures of cognitive control/cognitive flexibility. Analyses are whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise maps with reported peak coordinates (tables). Multiple within-group task contrasts are explicitly labeled. Participant group (healthy adult bilinguals, n=6) is acceptable. Reporting in tables of coordinates meets reporting requirements. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied.

This is a task-based fMRI study of an executive function (Stroop-like conflict/inhibition) reporting whole-brain, voxelwise group-level contrasts. Multiple within-group task contrasts are reported (e.g., informative > uninformative cues, target contrasts), with results given as coordinate tables. Participants are healthy adults (n=12). Thresholding and random-effects GLM are reported. These elements satisfy required inclusion criteria for task-based executive function activations and do not meet any exclusion criteria.

This fMRI study reports whole-brain, within-group voxelwise contrasts of a visual/semantic categorization task (CA vs FR). It meets I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise results reported), I8 (within-group task contrasts: CA, FR, CA>FR, FR>CA), I9 (healthy adult participants; any group acceptable), and I10 (results reported as coordinate peaks). It does NOT meet I6: the task is a categorization/rule-learning paradigm and is not clearly within the prespecified executive function domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore exclude for failing to satisfy I6.

This is an fMRI task study of cognitive control (conflict/interference) in healthy adults, reporting within-group contrasts and correlations with anxiety, so it meets I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (executive/cognitive control domain), I8 (within-group task contrasts), and I9 (participant group acceptable). However, all reported analyses are region-of-interest (model fit and inference restricted to ROIs, with small-volume correction) and no whole-brain, voxelwise group-level statistical maps are reported. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI/SVC results with no voxelwise results) and fails to meet inclusion criterion I7 (whole-brain evidence). On that basis the study must be excluded.

This study reports only between-group interaction contrasts (aged > young during automatic sequence performance) and does not report any within-group, voxelwise task activation contrasts for any group. Exclusion E5 applies. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (whole-brain, voxelwise analysis reported), I9 (human participant groups reported), I10 (results reported as peak coordinates). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (the primary paradigm probes motor automaticity/dual-task performance rather than a clear executive-function/cognitive-control task as defined by the review), I6 (task does not clearly fall within the predefined executive domains such as working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, or initiation), and critically I8 (no within-group task contrast reported). Because I8 is not satisfied and exclusion E5 is met, the study must be excluded.

Exclusion E3 applies: the reported analysis was fit and inferred only within anatomically defined ROIs (Model fit over: region of interest; Inference restricted to: region of interest), with no group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation map reported. Inclusion criteria met: I8 (a within-group, task contrast Task1 > Task2 is reported) and I9 (a participant group with a within-group contrast is present; healthy adults). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (while fMRI was used, the task is a conditional motor execution task and is not clearly characterized as assessing executive function/cognitive control in the required domains), I6 (task does not clearly fall within the specified executive domains such as working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, or initiation), I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise results), and I10 (no qualifying whole-brain results reported in tables/figures). Full text is complete in the provided NeuroStore record.

Primary exclusion: the task is Raven's Progressive Matrices (figural reasoning / fluid intelligence), which does not fall within the review's specified executive function domains (I6 not met). The study otherwise meets multiple inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5), reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses (I7), includes a within-group task contrast (complex g-task > simple g-task; one-sample t-test) (I8), includes an acceptable participant sample (adolescents) (I9), and reports coordinates/results in standard form (I10). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Because it fails I6 (task domain mismatch), the study must be excluded.

This is an fMRI study using a Go/No-Go task (inhibition), an established executive function domain, meeting I5 and I6. Analyses are reported as group-level, voxelwise whole-brain GLM with inference over the whole brain and coordinate peaks reported (Table tbl1), satisfying I7 and I10. Multiple contrasts are explicitly within-group task contrasts (Go vs Nogo and emotion-based within-group contrasts), satisfying I8. Participant group is healthy adults, so I9 is met. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and the paper is empirical. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

This fMRI study uses a semantic judgment (conceptual priming) task, not an executive function or cognitive control task. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (group-level, voxelwise whole-brain results reported), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported), I9 (participant group reported), I10 (whole-brain results reported as coordinate peaks/tables). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I5 (does not assess executive function/cognitive control), I6 (task is not within specified executive function domains such as working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, or initiation). No exclusion criteria from E3–E6 apply. Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis focused on executive function activations. Key details: semantic judgment task, n=12, whole-brain and ROI analyses, contrasts of repeated vs novel words with FDR thresholding.

The study is excluded because it does not assess an executive function or cognitive control task within the specified domains. The fMRI task involves affective valuation and binary choices about whether to repeat pleasant/unpleasant thermal stimuli (affective decision-making), which is not clearly within the listed executive domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Inclusion criteria met: I7 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses are reported), I8 (within-group task contrasts such as decide>rate and yes>no are present), I9 (within-group contrasts in a healthy adult sample), I10 (whole-brain results and contrasts are clearly described). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is not an executive function or cognitive control task as defined), I6 (task does not fall within the specified executive domains). Exclusion criteria met: none (not solely ROI/SVC analyses; voxelwise results and whole-brain contrasts are present). Full text is complete for screening.

The study uses fMRI with whole-brain, voxelwise, group-level contrasts (meets I7) and reports within-group task contrasts (insight > noninsight; meets I8). Participant sample is reported and a within-group contrast is present (meets I9). Results are reported as whole-brain peaks/coordinates (meets I10). However, the task is a Remote Associates Task assessing verbal insight/creative problem solving, which is not one of the established executive function domains listed in the inclusion criteria (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation); therefore it does not meet I5 or I6. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Conclusion: EXCLUDE because key inclusion criteria I5 and I6 are not satisfied.

The study reports task-based fMRI of an executive function task (Stroop Color-Word Task) with within-group voxelwise contrasts (NeuI>C and NegI>NeuI) estimated with whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses and reported peak coordinates. This meets inclusion requirements for fMRI task activation studies of executive function domains (inhibition), whole-brain voxelwise results, and within-group contrasts. Although the sample is small (n=8) and thresholding details are limited, inclusion criteria do not exclude studies for small samples or reporting thresholds. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the paper should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

The study meets all inclusion criteria: it is an event-related fMRI task study of reversal learning (an executive function: cognitive flexibility) (I5, I6); reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level statistical maps/model fits and inference (Model fit over: whole brain; inference over whole brain reported for multiple contrasts) (I7); contains within-group task contrasts (multiple one-sample t tests and ANOVA contrasts such as CR > BL, FRE > BL) (I8); participant group (healthy adults) is acceptable (I9); and whole-brain results are reported as peak coordinates/tables (I10). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and within-group contrasts are present. Full text appears available as a NeuroStore-derived record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study (N-back working memory and motor tasks) that probes cognitive sequence learning. It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain within-group contrasts (multiple analyses list model fit and inference over the whole brain with thresholded peaks) satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task activation maps. At least one contrast is a within-group task contrast. Participants are healthy adults (eligible). Results are reported as peaks/tables. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function activations.

This fMRI study reports event-related task-switching data (cognitive flexibility) with group-level, voxelwise analyses. NeuroStore shows whole-brain model fits and voxel-level thresholding and reports within-group contrasts (e.g., task switch > task repeat; all conditions > null; left hand > right hand) analyzed with a random-effects one-sample t-test across 18 participants. The task falls squarely within executive function (cognitive flexibility). Results are reported as peak coordinates (tables), satisfying reporting requirements. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and it is empirical human neuroimaging data). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

The study reports task-based fMRI of an executive function task (color-word Stroop) with within-group, voxelwise whole-brain contrasts. NeuroStore extractions include a whole-brain model fit and a within-group contrast (Analysis 16135781_analysis_8: I1; N1 > I4; N4) with voxelwise thresholding and reported peak coordinates (tables). Results are reported as peaks/tables and meet the meta-analysis requirement for voxelwise task activation. Therefore all inclusion criteria for task modality, task domain, whole-brain voxelwise evidence, within-group contrasts, participant eligibility, and reporting (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) apply.

The study used task-based fMRI with whole-brain, within-group contrasts (meeting I7, I8, I9, I10). However, the task is episodic memory cued-retrieval and reconstruction of perceptual details, not an executive function or cognitive-control task (does not fall within working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, or initiation). Therefore it fails I5 and I6 and must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the executive-function meta-analysis. It reports task-based fMRI (I5) using a Rapid Serial Visual Presentation task that requires covert shifts and maintenance of attention, which maps onto established executive domains (attention shifting/cognitive flexibility and vigilance) (I6). Analyses were whole-brain voxelwise with model fit and inference over the whole brain (I7) and report group-level, within-group task contrasts (multiple contrasts listed as within-group) (I8). Participant group is acceptable (healthy adults) (I9). Results are reported as coordinates/tables (Talairach peaks) satisfying reporting requirements (I10). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not limited to ROIs or SVC only, are not connectivity-only, and include within-group activation contrasts rather than only between-group effects. Thus the study should be INCLUDED.

This study investigates phonological processing (consonant discrimination and rhyming) across auditory and visual modalities rather than testing executive function or cognitive control per se. Although some analyses are labeled as 'N-Back Task' in the extraction, the primary aims and tasks described are phonological judgments, not established executive-function tasks (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). The study does provide whole-brain, voxelwise, within-group task contrasts and reports peak coordinates, so it meets criteria for whole-brain evidence and within-group contrasts. Therefore it does not meet inclusion criteria I5 and I6 (not an fMRI/PET study assessing executive function tasks within established EF domains), and is excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an event-related fMRI study testing cognitive control/monitoring (anterior cingulate role in error avoidance) using a task that requires response inhibition/decision to reject trials to avoid errors, fitting executive-function domains. The NeuroStore record shows whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (model fit and inference over whole brain) with reported peak coordinates. Multiple within-group task contrasts are reported (e.g., reject > error, error > reject, reject-only, set-size contrast), satisfying the requirement for at least one within-group task contrast. Participants are healthy adults and results are reported as coordinates/peaks. No exclusion criteria are met: analyses are not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, and not only between-group contrasts. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10 are satisfied and no exclusions apply.

This is an event-related fMRI study (BOLD) using a task that requires inhibition of a prepotent belief response (belief-bias manipulation), which falls within the executive function domain of inhibition. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (model fit and inference over whole brain) with coordinates/peaks and corrected random-field-theory thresholds for several within-group contrasts (e.g., correct inhibitory belief trials > incorrect inhibitory trials; belief-laden > belief-neutral; belief-neutral > belief-laden), and an interaction including baseline. These meet the requirement for at least one within-group task contrast and whole-brain voxelwise reporting. Participants are a human sample (n=14). Reporting of peaks/coordinate space satisfies the acceptable reporting formats. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an event-related fMRI study using a go/no-go task (inhibition), an established executive function domain. NeuroStore shows group-level, voxelwise whole-brain second-level analyses with corrected cluster inference and MNI coordinates (peaks in Table 1). Reported contrasts are within-subject, within-group task contrasts (co-action vs single actor; go vs nogo and their interaction), satisfying a within-group task activation requirement. Results are reported as whole-brain voxelwise maps summarized in tables of coordinates. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical, and within-group task contrasts are present). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 and I10 and should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study reporting whole-brain voxelwise group analyses. The picture-sequencing task targets semantic event sequencing (planning/ordering), which maps to an executive function domain (planning). A within-group task contrast is reported (PS > CON) with whole-brain inference and peaks in a table. Participants are healthy adults. Results are reported as voxelwise activations (reported peaks), satisfying reporting requirements. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group, and not non-empirical).

This fMRI study reports whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise within-group task contrasts (TI > HT and HT > VIS) examining transitive inference, which involves manipulation of information and reasoning consistent with executive-function processes (cognitive flexibility/complex reasoning). Analyses report Talairach coordinates and thresholding; results are not ROI-only or connectivity-only. Participant group (n=15) is reported. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis criteria for task-based fMRI executive function activations.

This is an fMRI study using an established executive function task (antisaccade; inhibition). The NeuroStore record reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain GLM analyses (model fitted over whole brain; inference over whole brain) with cluster-level thresholding and reported coordinate peaks (Table 1). Within-group task contrasts are reported (preparation and response contrasts comparing antisaccade vs prosaccade trials). Participants are healthy adults, and results are reported as coordinates, satisfying reporting requirements. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and empirical task activation data are presented). Therefore all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 are satisfied.

This fMRI study uses a task-based paradigm (compound remote-associate problems) labeled as ‘executive and reasoning’ and reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (model fit over: whole brain) with within-group contrasts (insight preparation > noninsight preparation; noninsight > insight). Results are reported as peak coordinates (Table 1). Thus it meets fMRI task requirement (I5), falls under executive/cognitive control tasks as categorized in the record (I6), provides whole-brain voxelwise group maps (I7), includes within-group task contrasts (I8), involves a participant group (n=25) so qualifies (I9), and reports peaks/tables of coordinates (I10). No exclusion criteria apply. fulltext_incomplete=false

All reported analyses are between-group contrasts or interactions (model stated as between-group task ST-PLS; analyses labelled [contrast, between-group] and [interaction, between-group]) and no within-group task activation contrast for any group is presented. This meets exclusion criterion E5. The study does meet other inclusion criteria: it is an fMRI study with an executive-style task (reverse alphabetizing) (I5), the task falls within executive domains (working memory/manipulation) (I6), results are voxelwise whole-brain analyses with coordinate tables (I7, I10), and participant groups are acceptable (I9). However it fails I8 (no within-group task contrast). Therefore exclude under E5.

The study reports a task-based fMRI Stroop experiment (an established inhibition/cognitive-control task) with a within-group contrast (incongruent > neutral). Analysis was a group-level, voxelwise model fit over the whole brain and reports peak coordinates, satisfying whole-brain evidence. Participants (n=6) are acceptable under inclusion rules. The paper is empirical and not ROI-only or connectivity-only. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10) and violates no exclusion criteria.

The study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations. It uses fMRI with a Stroop Color-Word Task (an established inhibition/executive function paradigm) satisfying I5 and I6. It reports at least one group-level, voxelwise whole-brain contrast (Analysis 15494184_analysis_0: emotional > neutral, model fit over whole brain) satisfying I7. Multiple within-group task contrasts are reported (e.g., number > fixation, fixation > number, emotional > neutral), satisfying I8. Participant groups are reported (healthy adults), satisfying I9. Results include coordinate/contrast reporting consistent with I10. No exclusion criteria are met: the study is not ROI-only (E3), not connectivity/rest-only (E4), and includes within-group contrasts rather than only between-group contrasts (E5). Fulltext is available as the NeuroStore-derived record, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

Excluded because all reported analyses were region-of-interest (ROI) confined (Model fit over: region of interest; Inference restricted to: region of interest; region-level thresholding), meaning no group-level voxelwise whole-brain activation maps were reported. This meets exclusion criterion E3. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (task involves planning/initiation within executive-function domains), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported), I9 (healthy participant group reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise results presented). fulltext_incomplete set to false.

The study reports task-based fMRI of working memory (WM) during language processing, which falls within executive function domains (working memory). It includes group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (e.g., Analyses 5 and 6: Space > Nonspace and Nonspace > Space; Model fit over: whole brain; Inference over: whole brain; FWE-corrected), and multiple within-group task contrasts and parametric/modulation within-group regressions (e.g., Analyses 5, 6, 7, 8–13). Participants are healthy adults (n=20). Results are reported as voxelwise peaks/tables. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and empirical). Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study is a PET task-based investigation that assesses initiation and related executive processes (meets I5, I6). It reports within-group task contrasts (SI>EC, EC>SI, TP>EC) and parametric associations (meets I8) in a healthy participant sample (I9) and reports results as peak coordinates/tables (I10). However, all analyses were fit and inferred within an a priori region-of-interest mask using small-volume correction (Model fit over: region of interest; Inference restricted to: region of interest; SVC and voxelwise thresholds), indicating no whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps are reported. This violates inclusion criterion I7 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI/SVC analyses reported). Therefore the study is excluded.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation of dual arithmetic that explicitly examines capacity limits on executive processing (the abstract references the executive network). It reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level contrasts (e.g., Single-addition > Baseline, Single-subtraction > Baseline, Dual-* > Baseline) with voxelwise thresholding and cluster extent correction, and provides coordinate tables of peaks. All inclusion criteria are satisfied: (I5) task-based fMRI assessing executive/cognitive-control processes; (I6) task involves executive domains (working memory/dual-task coordination); (I7) whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported; (I8) within-group task contrasts are provided; (I9) participant group is reported (healthy adults) and within-group contrasts are available; (I10) results include coordinate tables and clear descriptions. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore the study should be included in the meta-analysis.

This paper reports fMRI task data (I5) and includes within-group contrasts (contrast labeled 'interaction, within-group') (I8) on a healthy participant sample (I9). However, all extracted analyses are psychophysiological interaction (PPI) connectivity results (seed-based functional connectivity), with no voxelwise task-evoked activation maps reported. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E4 (connectivity-only results). In addition, the report does not provide a clear whole-brain task-activation statistical map (I7 not met) and it is unclear that the task cleanly maps onto established executive-function domains (I6 not met). Because E4 is violated, the study must be excluded.

This fMRI study reports whole-brain, voxelwise, within-group task contrasts (meets I7, I8) and qualifies across participant groups (meets I9). Results are reported as coordinates/tables (meets I10). However, the experimental paradigm is a reactive aggression/provocation task whose primary aim is to elicit aggressive behavior and examine affect, reward and motivational processes; it is not an established executive-function paradigm (e.g., working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Therefore it does not meet the review’s task-domain requirement (I6) and, on that basis, does not satisfy the requirement that the imaging data assess executive function/cognitive control as defined in I5/I6. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I7, I8, I9, I10. Inclusion IDs not met: I5, I6.

This is an event-related fMRI study of response inhibition/motor intention (executive function domain). The record reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (model fit and inference over whole brain) with thresholding and tables of reported peaks, and multiple within-group task contrasts (e.g., DPGo > DPNogo). Participant group is a human sample (n=6) which is acceptable per inclusion criteria. Results are presented as coordinates/tables. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study is excluded because it reports only region-of-interest (ROI) voxelwise modeling (model fit over: region of interest) with no whole-brain voxelwise analysis provided, meeting exclusion criterion E3. The paper does report a within-group task contrast (first correct > subsequent correct), satisfying inclusion criterion I8, and the participant sample is acceptable (I9). However, it does not meet the review’s domain requirement (I6) because the task is associative visual-motor learning rather than a canonical executive function domain (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). It also fails I7 because no whole-brain voxelwise results are reported (model fit restricted to ROI). Full text appears complete for screening (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an event-related fMRI study of selective attention/conflict (executive control) with a cued global/local task in healthy adults (n=16). NeuroStore shows at least one group-level, voxelwise, whole-brain analysis (Analysis 15238434_analysis_0: voxelwise RFX ANOVA; model fit over whole brain) reporting a within-group contrast (global cue-only > local cue-only). Results include reported peak coordinates. Thus the paper meets criteria for task-based fMRI assessing executive function (I5), task falls within executive/cognitive control domain (I6), provides whole-brain voxelwise group results (I7), reports a within-group task contrast (I8), includes an eligible participant group (I9), and reports coordinates/results (I10). No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, or between-group-only reporting).

The study reports task-based fMRI of a conflict (size-congruity/Stroop-like) task (meets I5,I6). Multiple within-group contrasts are reported (incongruent>neutral, incongruent>congruent, congruent>neutral), satisfying I8. Analysis 18632120_analysis_2 explicitly indicates a group-level, whole-brain model fit for the incongruent>congruent contrast (voxelwise, corrected threshold, peaks in Table tbl1), satisfying I7 and I10 (coordinates/peaks reported). Participants (n=14) are an acceptable sample per I9. The report also includes ROI and connectivity analyses, but these do not exclude the study because at least one whole-brain voxelwise within-group activation map is provided. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

The study reports whole-brain, voxelwise fMRI maps and within-subject contrasts (negativity/positivity vs baseline; coordinates and tables provided) and includes clinical participants, so it meets I7, I8, I9 and I10. However, the task is SCP self-regulation/neurofeedback (producing negative/positive slow cortical potentials) and is not an established executive function domain (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Therefore it does not satisfy I5 and I6 (task does not assess a standard executive/cognitive-control domain). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met.

This fMRI study uses a gambling/probability learning paradigm focused on reward-related reinforcement learning rather than an executive function domain. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I8 (within-group task contrasts/omnibus within-group analyses), I9 (participant group reported, within-group contrasts present), and I10 (whole-brain results reported as tables of peaks). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (task is not within established executive function domains such as working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, or initiation). No exclusion criteria were triggered (E3–E6). Therefore the study is excluded for failing I6.

Excluded because the task (lexical decision / visual word recognition) is a language processing task and does not clearly fall within established executive function domains required by I6 (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Although authors report prefrontal activations and interpret them as involving executive control, the paradigm itself is not an established executive function task. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI, task-based), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I8 (within-group task contrasts present), I9 (participant group acceptable), I10 (results reported as peaks/tables). Exclusion criteria met: none (E3–E6 not applicable). Therefore the study is excluded for not meeting I6.

The study uses task-based fMRI of inhibition and conflict (meets I5, I6) and reports within-group contrasts (HIGH>LOW and LOW>HIGH; meets I8) across eligible participant groups (I9). However, all reported analyses in the NeuroStore record are region-of-interest (ROI) / region-level model fits and thresholding (Model fit over: region of interest; region-level thresholding). No whole-brain, voxelwise group-level activation maps are reported in the document. Therefore the study reports only ROI/small-volume analyses and no voxelwise whole-brain results, violating exclusion criterion E3 and failing inclusion criterion I7 (whole-brain evidence). Full text was available in the provided record. Decision: EXCLUDED.

This fMRI study reports task-based, within-group contrasts of visuo-attentional processing (colour vs age judgements) using an established task paradigm and explicitly examines attention-dependent responses. Multiple analyses include whole-brain, voxelwise group-level contrasts (Analyses 1–3), and coordinates are reported. Although one analysis used an ROI, whole-brain voxelwise results are present. Participant groups (mild AD patients and controls) are acceptable per criteria. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group contrasts, empirical data). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 and I10.

Exclusion criterion met: E3. The paper reports task-based fMRI of executive processes (meets I5), tasks within executive domains (initiation/sequencing/planning; meets I6), reports within-group contrasts (meets I8), and uses healthy participants (meets I9). However, all reported analyses were conducted and inference restricted to predefined regions of interest (model fit over: region of interest; inference restricted to: region of interest) with no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps reported, so it fails I7 (whole-brain evidence). Because results are ROI-only, E3 applies and the study must be excluded. Also, no qualifying whole-brain results are reported (I10 not met).

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation using the Multi-Source Interference Task, an established cognitive control/executive function paradigm. It reports within-group voxelwise contrasts (INC>CON and CON>INC) with model fitting over the whole brain and peak coordinates (Talairach), and provides ROI-restricted inference but does not appear to be ROI-only. Participants are healthy adults (female twins). Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 and I10. No exclusion criteria are met. The provided NeuroStore record constitutes the full available document for screening.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of executive function (set-shifting using modified WCST), reporting group-level, voxelwise whole-brain results. Multiple analyses are within-group contrasts (A > D and D simple effect), thresholded voxelwise (FDR-corrected) with coordinate tables, satisfying requirements for whole-brain, voxelwise task activation maps. The task falls under cognitive flexibility (an established executive domain). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included in the meta-analysis.

The study reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task contrasts (footstep > rest and rest > footstep) with coordinate peaks (Table) and participant details; however the experimental task is a perceptual judgment of auditory motion (indicating walking direction). This does not clearly fall within established executive function domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation), and the paper’s focus is on functional/effective connectivity during an auditory goal-directed/perceptual task rather than an explicit executive control paradigm. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met.

This is an event-related and block-design fMRI study of saccade tasks that probe working memory and inhibitory control (memory-guided and anti-/visually guided saccades), which fall within established executive-function domains. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (Memory>Visual, Visual>Memory, and epoch-specific contrasts) with coordinates and tables of peaks. At least one within-group task contrast is reported. Results are presented as whole-brain voxelwise inference. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an fMRI study of mood induction (happy/sad) with a gender-discrimination control task. Although the paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise, within-group task contrasts (sadness>cognition; happiness>cognition) and provides coordinate tables, the tasks do not assess established executive function domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). The ‘cognition’ condition is a gender-discrimination perceptual task used as a control, and the primary manipulations are emotional mood induction rather than an executive function/cognitive-control paradigm. Therefore it fails the core inclusion requirements that the study assess executive function/cognitive control (I5,I6).

This is an fMRI task-based study that reports within-group, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts relevant to cognitive control. The study used a conflict paradigm (semantic content vs prosodic intonation) designed to probe attentional/cognitive control processes and reports a within-group contrast (CONF > NOCONF) with whole-brain random-effects analyses and corrected inference, with peak coordinates listed. Participants are healthy humans (n=10). Thus it satisfies I5 (task-based fMRI addressing cognitive control), I6 (task maps onto established executive domains—conflict/attention/inhibition), I7 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain results), I8 (within-group task contrast), I9 (participant group acceptable), and I10 (whole-brain results reported in tables). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group contrasts, empirical). Full text is available in the provided NeuroStore record.

The study is a task-based fMRI experiment reporting within-group, voxelwise contrasts and coordinate tables, but the task is language/semantic processing (passive listening and semantic categorization). It does not assess executive function or cognitive control within the specified domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Therefore inclusion criteria I5 and I6 are not met. It does meet I7 (whole-brain voxelwise results reported), I8 (within-group contrasts), I9 (participant group acceptable), and I10 (results reported as tables/coordinates). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

Although this is an fMRI study using the Hayling sentence-completion task (an executive initiation/inhibition task) and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses, the NeuroStore extract shows only between-group contrasts (controls vs high-risk groups, group x condition interactions, linear trends, and parametric between-group effects). I find no within-group task activation contrasts (task > baseline or active control) reported for any participant group in the provided document. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI task), I6 (task falls within executive domains—initiation), I7 (whole-brain, voxelwise group analyses reported), I9 (participant groups acceptable), I10 (results reported as coordinates/tables). Inclusion criterion not met: I8 (no within-group task contrast reported). Exclusion criterion met: E5 (only between-group contrasts reported with no within-group activation map). Therefore the study does not qualify for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This fMRI study used a Stroop task (inhibition), an established executive function paradigm, and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task activation (interference > neutral) with coordinates (Table 1). The model terms for the main task contrast are 'task condition' (random-effects group analysis), indicating a within-group task contrast / main effect of task was tested and reported. Analyses were whole-brain and reported peak coordinates, which qualifies under coordinate reporting rules. Therefore all required inclusion criteria for task type, executive domain, whole-brain voxelwise results, a within-group task contrast, participant groups, and acceptable reporting are met. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) apply.

This study is excluded because it does not assess executive function or cognitive control using an established executive task. The task is a smooth pursuit/saccade eye-movement paradigm (sensorimotor/oculomotor) rather than an executive function domain (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). The paper does report group-level, voxelwise modeling (model fit over whole brain) and within-group task contrasts (e.g., 20°/s > 5°/s; parametric modulations), and provides coordinate tables, so it meets I7, I8 and I9 (and reporting format I10). However it fails I5 and I6 (not an fMRI study of executive function/cognitive control task). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met from the provided record.

The study reports task-based fMRI of an Emotional Stroop (inhibition/selective attention) — an executive function domain (inhibition). It includes within-group voxelwise contrasts (negative > neutral) for groups and overall, with model fit and inference performed over the whole brain and coordinates/peaks reported (Monte Carlo/AlphaSim cluster correction). Thus it provides whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise task activation maps reported in tables. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and within-group contrasts are present). Participant groups are acceptable per criteria. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

The paper reports task-based fMRI whole-brain, voxelwise within-group contrasts for executive-function tasks (Stroop counting: neutral counting > rest and interference counting > rest). These contrasts reflect inhibition/interference (an executive function domain). Analyses were performed over the whole brain with FWER correction and report coordinates/peak tables, satisfying requirements for a group-level voxelwise task activation map. Participant groups (including adolescents) are acceptable per criteria. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, and within-group contrasts are provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 are satisfied.

This is an event-related fMRI study that tests perception of learned action effects using a go/no-go paradigm (inhibition). The task clearly assesses executive function/cognitive control (inhibition) and falls within established EF domains. Analyses are whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise contrasts with reported peak coordinates and cluster thresholds. Multiple within-group task contrasts are reported (e.g., no-go_left > neutral, incompatible > compatible), satisfying the requirement for within-group task contrasts. Participants are healthy adults (n=18). Results are reported in tables of coordinates. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

The study reports task-based fMRI using a Task Switching (covert attention orienting) paradigm, which falls under executive function (cognitive flexibility). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise GLM results are reported (model fit and inference over whole brain; voxelwise FDR thresholding; coordinates/peaks in table) for within-group contrasts in both congenitally blind (CB) and sighted control (SC) groups (simple effects: left/right/centre). Participant samples and measures are provided. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for task domain, modality, whole-brain voxelwise analysis, and within-group contrasts. No exclusion criteria apply (results are not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, and within-group contrasts are present).

The study uses a probabilistic category-learning task (classification of dot patterns), which is a learning/decision-making paradigm and not one of the specified executive function domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). While the paper meets several inclusion criteria (I5: task-based fMRI; I7: group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported; I8: within-group task contrasts are reported; I9: participant group reported; I10: voxel coordinates/peaks reported), it does NOT meet I6 (task falls within established executive function domains). No exclusion criteria are triggered (no ROI-only results, no connectivity-only analyses, and within-group contrasts are present). Therefore exclude for not meeting I6.

The study reports task-based fMRI analyses including a Stroop Color-Word Task (inhibition), a canonical executive function paradigm. Group-level, voxelwise task contrasts are reported (simple within-group Stroop deactivation and moral-dilemma activation) using whole-brain ICA with FDR thresholding and peaks listed in a table, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise results. At least one contrast is a within-group task effect versus baseline/other condition. Participants are healthy adults but any participant group is acceptable. Results are presented as coordinates/peaks (Table 1). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not only connectivity/resting-state, and not only between-group contrasts). Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for executive function task activations (notably inhibition) and is included.

This is an empirical fMRI study that includes Stroop task contrasts (inhibition/conflict) and a time-estimation task. At least one analysis is a group-level, voxelwise, within-group task contrast (e.g., incongruent > congruent; errors > correct; correct feedback > error feedback) with whole-brain model fit and reported peak coordinates/tables (Talairach space). Thus it assesses executive-function/cognitive-control, provides whole-brain voxelwise results, reports within-group contrasts, and reports results in tables/peaks. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met. Participants are described. Full text appears available in the provided record.

Exclusion because analyses reported are ROI and between-group only. Exclusion criteria met: E3 (only ROI/small-volume analyses reported with no voxelwise whole-brain results) and E5 (only between-group contrast reported with no within-group task activation contrast). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI assessing executive/cognitive control — POP task) and I6 (task falls within executive domains: attentional control/conflict/motor planning). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (no group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task activation map; model fit is region-of-interest only) and I8 (no within-group task contrast reported for any group). Full text appears complete in this record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study reports event-related fMRI (I5) using a Delayed Match-to-Sample task, which maps to the working memory executive domain (I6). Model fitting was performed over the whole brain with voxelwise group-level contrasts and voxel-level thresholding reported (Tables) satisfying whole-brain evidence (I7,I10). The extracted record specifies the contrasts are omnibus within-group task contrasts (I8) in a healthy participant group (n=8) (I9). Results are reported as coordinate tables and voxelwise significant peaks, not restricted to ROIs, and no exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

This fMRI study reports within-group, whole-brain, voxelwise task activation contrasts (Single taps > rest and Sequences of four taps > rest) in healthy participants (n=8). The task probes programming and initiation of repetitive/sequential movements, which maps onto the executive domain of initiation (and sequence programming/cognitive control). Results are reported as peak coordinates (table) and use voxelwise inference; thus they meet the requirements for whole-brain group-level task contrasts. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and it is empirical). Therefore the study satisfies all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This study is excluded because it reports only region-of-interest analyses and does not provide group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task activation maps (Exclusion E3). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (task maps to 'vigilance' / attentional orienting), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported), I9 (participant group reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise results reported; model fit over: region of interest; Regions: anatomical a priori ROI). Therefore it fails the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise evidence and must be excluded.

This study reports a task-based fMRI Emotional Stroop paradigm probing cognitive-emotional interference (an inhibition/cognitive-control task). Group-level, voxelwise one-sample t-tests were fit over the whole brain, and within-group contrasts (incongruence > congruence and congruence > incongruence) are reported with peak coordinates (Table tbl1). Participants include a clinical sample (schizophrenia), which is allowed. Results are whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps rather than ROI-only or connectivity-only analyses. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Excluded because all reported analyses were confined to region-of-interest (Model fit over: region of interest; AAL masks) and the contrasts listed are between-group or group×condition interaction contrasts with no within-group task activation map reported. This violates exclusion criteria E3 (reports only ROI/small-volume analyses with no voxelwise whole-brain results) and E5 (reports only between-group contrasts/group×condition interactions with no within-group task contrast). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI study) and I6 (task is Continuous Performance Test — vigilance, an executive domain), and I9 (clinical participant groups are acceptable). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map) and I8 (no within-group task contrast reported for any group).

This is an empirical fMRI study of task-evoked activations that includes Go/No-Go and selection manipulations relevant to executive functions (inhibition/initiation and selection). Multiple analyses report group-level, voxelwise whole-brain random-effects results (analyses 0,1,2,5,6) with reported peak coordinates/tables and cluster-corrected inference. Several contrasts are within-group task contrasts (e.g., reading>fixation, repetition>fixation, Selection>No-Selection, Go>No-Go). Participants are healthy and within-group contrasts are reported. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for task-based fMRI of executive function domains, whole-brain voxelwise group analyses, and within-group contrasts. No exclusion criteria are met (some contrasts used ROI restriction, but whole-brain voxelwise results are also present).

While the study is an fMRI, whole-brain, within-group task-based study (meets I7, I8, I9, I10), it does not assess executive function or cognitive control. The tasks are semantic judgment and repetition-priming (language/semantic processing), which do not fall within the specified executive function domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Therefore inclusion criteria I5 and I6 are not met. No exclusion criteria are triggered.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of a spatial Stroop (conflict) task assessing preparatory neural activity related to conflict resolution, which falls squarely within executive function/cognitive control. The NeuroStore record reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (model fit over: whole brain) with within-group task contrasts (e.g., position cue > neutral cue; position cue > word cue; word cue > neutral cue) and cross-subject regressions. Results are reported as peaks/tables. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10) and violates none of the exclusion criteria. Full text appears available from the record, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task-based cueing/oddball visual detection paradigm that examines proactive response inhibition and motor activation (executive control processes). It reports a group-level, voxelwise whole-brain contrast (mixed-block no-cue > pure-block no-cue) tested with a random-effects one-sample t-test (n=14) and voxelwise thresholding, with reported peak coordinates (Table tbl1). The contrast is a within-group task contrast. Participants are healthy adults. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I5 (task fMRI), I6 (task taps executive domains—vigilance/inhibition), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise evidence), I8 (within-group contrast), I9 (participant groups acceptable), and I10 (results reported as coordinates/table). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text is available in the provided NeuroStore record representation.

The study reports event-related fMRI of a Stroop task (inhibition/cognitive control) in healthy adults (n=10). Group-level, voxelwise GLM maps were estimated over the whole brain (group analysis by averaging individual z-maps) and within-group task contrasts are reported (e.g. incongruent > neutral; neutral/incongruent > null; red>green), with peak coordinates listed in a table. These features satisfy executive-function task domain (inhibition), whole-brain voxelwise reporting, within-group contrasts, and coordinate-table reporting. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting, not only between-group contrasts, not non-empirical).

This study reports an fMRI training study (BOLD measure) with within-group contrasts (after>before training and an interaction), and NeuroStore lists voxelwise peaks, so I5 (fMRI), I7 (whole-brain evidence; reported peaks indicate voxelwise maps), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (participant groups acceptable), and I10 (results reported as peaks/coordinates) are satisfied. However, the documented tasks are music-reading/motor and perceptual judgments (melody keypresses, rhythm production, and vertical-stem perceptual judgment). These do not clearly fall within established executive-function domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation) required by I6. Although the abstract mentions a musical Stroop paradigm (an inhibition-type task), no Stroop or other inhibition/EF contrasts are present among the extracted fMRI analyses—only learning-related musical-reading contrasts. Because I6 is not met, the study is excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered based on the provided document.

The study reports an event-related fMRI investigation of the antisaccade task, a well-established inhibition (executive function) paradigm. It provides group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (model fit over: whole brain; voxel-level thresholding; reported peak coordinates in Table 1) and multiple within-group contrasts (e.g., Anti > Pro, Correct Anti > Error Anti) qualifying as task-evoked activation maps. Participants are healthy adults (n=10). Results are reported as peaks (tables) and the analyses are clearly task-based. All inclusion criteria for the review are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

Excluded because analyses were performed and reported only within anatomically defined regions of interest with inference restricted to ROIs (NeuroStore notes: 'Model fit over: region of interest' and 'Inference restricted to: region of interest'), meeting exclusion criterion E3. The study is an fMRI task-based investigation (I5) that includes memory-delay and gap paradigms that map onto executive domains (planning/working memory) (I6), reports within-group task contrasts for saccade and pointing (I8), and reports coordinate results (I10). Participant sample is an eligible within-group cohort (I9). However, it does not provide a group-level, voxelwise whole-brain activation map (I7 not met), and therefore fails inclusion.

This is a task-based fMRI study of anticipatory spatial attention (Posner cueing), which maps to the vigilance/attention domain listed under I6. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise, group-level analyses with one-sample t-tests and FWE-corrected inference (Model fit and Inference over: whole brain), satisfying I7. Multiple within-group task contrasts are reported (e.g., V+>ND, V+>V−, V−>V+), satisfying I8. It is empirical fMRI data (I5) on healthy participants (I9) and reports coordinates/tables for whole-brain results (I10). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only (E3), not solely connectivity/resting-state (E4), not only between-group contrasts (E5), and the paper is empirical (not E6). Based on these points, the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

The study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I6: the task (emotion regulation of conditioned fear/extinction) is not within the specified executive function domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). The study does meet several other inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses: analyses 5,6,7,8), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported), I9 (participant group reporting within-group contrasts), and I10 (coordinates/tables reported). No exclusion criteria are triggered (none of E3–E6 apply). Therefore excluded based on failure to satisfy I6 (task domain mismatch).

The study used task-based fMRI and reports voxelwise, group-level within-group contrasts (e.g. cued > neutral) across the whole brain, and reports coordinates — satisfying I7, I8, I9 and I10. However, the task is a Posner spatial cueing task probing endogenous and exogenous spatial orienting (attention/orienting), not an executive function or cognitive control task within the specified domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Therefore it does not meet I5 (assessment of executive function/cognitive control) nor I6 (task within established executive function domains). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text is available in the provided record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

While this fMRI study provides whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation maps and reports within-group contrasts (satisfying I5, I7, I8, and I9), the task paradigm assesses episodic memory retrieval and suppression under posthypnotic amnesia rather than a canonical executive-function task. The inclusion criterion I6 requires tasks to fall within established executive function domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Although the authors propose that some regions may subserve inhibitory processes, the paradigm primarily targets episodic memory and posthypnotic amnesia, not a standard executive-control task. Therefore I6 is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered by the reported analyses. Based on these facts the study should be excluded from the meta-analysis of executive-function task activations.

This is an event-related fMRI study of response inhibition (an executive function: inhibition) reporting within-group, voxelwise task activation maps. Analysis 'Regions of event-related activation during Aware errors' was fit over the whole brain and inference was conducted over the whole brain using one-sample t tests (group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical map). A within-group contrast is reported (Aware errors simple effect and Aware > Unaware errors), satisfying the requirement for within-group task contrasts. Although a separate analysis used an ROI, the presence of a whole-brain group-level voxelwise analysis means the study is not excluded by the ROI-only criterion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

Exclusion applied: E5 (study reports only between-group contrasts/group×condition interactions with no within-group task activation contrast). The NeuroStore record lists only between-group contrasts (Young>Elderly; High-performing elderly>Low-performing elderly) and reports peaks from those group comparisons. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I9 (participant groups acceptable), I10 (whole-brain results reported as coordinate peaks/tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (task is an Old/New recognition memory task, which is not one of the specified executive-function domains such as working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, or initiation), and I8 (no within-group task contrast reported for any group). Because E5 is met (no within-group contrasts), the study must be excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study of cognitive control/interference (executive function), reporting whole-brain, voxelwise group-level contrasts (model fit and inference over whole brain; voxel-level threshold p<0.001) with coordinates in MNI. Multiple within-group task contrasts are reported (e.g., incongruent correct > congruent correct; incorrect incongruent > correct incongruent). Participants: healthy adults (n=14). Thus it meets all inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function), I6 (task within executive domains—conflict/inhibition), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise results), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (participant group acceptable), and I10 (results reported as coordinates/tables). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete as represented in the record.

This study used whole-brain, voxelwise fMRI contrasts (within-group contrasts reported) and reports coordinate tables, but its task (Posner spatial cueing; endogenous/exogenous orienting and IOR) investigates visual-spatial attention/orienting rather than an established executive function domain as specified (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Therefore it does not meet I6 (task within established executive function domains). It also does not clearly assess executive function/cognitive control per I5. Inclusion criteria met: I7, I8, I9, I10. Inclusion criteria not met: I5, I6. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

Excluded because the task does not clearly fall within the meta-analysis' required executive function domains (I6). This study uses an operant/fear extinction paradigm (associative extinction learning), which is not explicitly one of the specified executive domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). The study does meet other inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported, e.g., Successful extinction > control), I9 (participant group reported; healthy adults), and I10 (whole-brain results reported in tables of coordinates). No exclusion criteria apply (E3–E6 not met). Therefore it is excluded from the executive-function meta-analysis because it fails I6.

While this is an fMRI, whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise study with multiple within-group task contrasts (meets I7, I8, I9, I10), the task is a number-bisection mental-arithmetic paradigm focused on numerical representation and magnitude processing. The paper’s primary aim and task do not constitute an established executive function domain (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation) as required by I5/I6. Although the authors report involvement of monitoring and inhibition-related regions, the study primarily assesses numerical/arithmetic processing rather than an executive-function or cognitive-control task per the inclusion definitions. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study of top-down attentional control (cognitive control/executive function). It reports whole-brain, voxelwise, group-level within-group task contrasts: Analyses 15193622_analysis_0 and _1 are fixed-effect, whole-brain, voxelwise within-group contrasts (corrected p<0.05) reported as coordinate peaks, satisfying the requirement for voxelwise within-group task activation maps. Coordinates are provided in tables (qualifies under I10). Participant groups are reported. Although one between-group ROI small-volume analysis is also reported, the presence of whole-brain within-group contrasts means no exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria and is INCLUDED.

This is an fMRI event-related study of emotional prosody and selective attention (dichotic listening with gender decision). While it reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise within-group task contrasts (meeting I7, I8), includes an acceptable participant group (I9), and reports coordinates/tables (I10), the study does not assess executive function or cognitive control per the meta-analysis focus (I5) and the task does not fall within established executive function domains such as working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, or initiation (I6). No exclusion criteria are triggered (E3–E6 not met). Therefore exclude because I5 and I6 are not satisfied.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study examining cognitive control/executive demands during language production (context encoding, maintenance, and selection), with whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses reported in Talairach coordinates. Multiple contrasts are within-group (simple effects and within-group contrasts), and results are reported as peak coordinates. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

The study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I6: the task is a moral-judgment paradigm and is not clearly within the review's specified executive-function domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). The paper does address cognitive control processes, but the task itself is not one of the established EF task categories listed in I6. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI assessing cognitive control/moral judgment), I7 (group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses reported), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported), I9 (participant groups acceptable), I10 (results reported via coordinates/tables). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text is complete for screening purposes.

This fMRI study used an N-back working-memory task (executive function domain) with task-based BOLD contrasts in a group of grapheme-color synesthetes (n=9). It reports multiple within-group, voxelwise task contrasts (explicitly labeled within-group contrasts) including whole-brain model fits and whole-brain inference (random-effects analyses with voxelwise thresholds and reported peak coordinates), and tables of peaks in Talairach space. Thus it meets the meta-analysis objective and all inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (working memory/N-back), I7 (group-level voxelwise/whole-brain results reported), I8 (within-group contrasts), I9 (any participant group allowed), and I10 (whole-brain results reported as coordinates/tables). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and empirical task activation data are provided).

This fMRI study reports a task-based paradigm addressing attention/cognitive control (authors describe challenge-driven attention and right frontal activity linked to cognitive control), satisfying I5 and I6. It includes a group-level, voxelwise second-level random-effects analysis fit over the whole brain with reported peaks (Analysis 18958217_analysis_0), satisfying I7. That analysis is a within-group task contrast (difficult SOA conditions > simultaneous), satisfying I8. Participant sample (n=12 adults) is reported, so I9 is met. Whole-brain results are reported as voxelwise peaks, satisfying I10. No exclusion criteria apply: study is not ROI-only (it has whole-brain voxelwise results), not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

The NeuroStore record shows only region-of-interest analyses with small-volume correction and inference restricted to a priori ROIs (OFC/VLPFC, ACC). No group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps are reported. Thus the study violates inclusion criterion I7 and meets exclusion criterion E3. The study is task-based fMRI of decision-making (Wheel of Fortune) and reports within-group contrasts and coordinate tables, so it meets I5, I8, I9, and I10; however I7 (whole-brain voxelwise results) is not satisfied and I6 (task within explicitly listed executive function domains) is ambiguous/not clearly met. Therefore exclude under E3.

This is an fMRI event-related study with whole-brain, voxelwise, group-level within-subject contrasts (satisfies I7, I8), reports coordinates (I10), and includes a relevant participant group (I9). However, the experimental task is an episodic memory/recognition paradigm (old/new recognition; instructions: 'look' vs 'remember'), which is not an executive function task and does not fall within the specified executive function domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I5 and I6 (not assessing executive function/cognitive control). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text is sufficiently represented by the NeuroStore record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This study reports task-based fMRI (BOLD) of a Task Switching/temporal context retrieval paradigm (meets I5). The tasks include task switching/cognitive flexibility and ordering, which are established executive domains (I6). Analyses were whole-brain, voxelwise, group-level random-effects GLM t-tests (model fit over: whole brain) with reported peak coordinates (satisfies I7 and I10). At least one within-group task contrast is explicitly reported (contrasts labeled within-group) (I8). Participant sample is a within-group healthy adult cohort (I9). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and not only between-group contrasts. Therefore the article qualifies for inclusion in the meta-analysis of executive-function task activations. Full text is available via the NeuroStore record (fulltext_incomplete=false).
